प्रदत्त दस्तावेजों में मुझे इसका उत्तर नहीं मिल सका।

प्रदत्त दस्तावेज तीन सरकारी कल्याणकारी योजनाओं का वर्णन करते हैं:
*   **पीएम किसान सम्मान निधि:** किसानों के लिए एक आय सहायता योजना।
*   **आयुष्मान भारत पीएम-जेएवाई:** एक स्वास्थ्य बीमा योजना।
*   **प्रधानमंत्री आवास योजना (पीएमएवाई):** एक आवास योजना।

इनमें से कोई भी दस्तावेज उन संगठनों के बारे में जानकारी प्रदान नहीं करता है जो वित्तीय अपराधों की रिपोर्ट करने के लिए उत्तरदायी हैं।

सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर, भारत में वित्तीय अपराधों की रिपोर्ट करने के लिए सबसे प्रासंगिक संगठन **राज्य पुलिस की आर्थिक अपराध शाखा (ईओडब्ल्यू)** होगी। साइबर-संबंधी वित्तीय अपराधों के लिए, **साइबर अपराध प्रकोष्ठ** या **राष्ट्रीय साइबर अपराध रिपोर्टिंग पोर्टल** उपयुक्त माध्यम होंगे। **केंद्रीय अन्वेषण ब्यूरो (सीबीआई)** भी बड़े और अंतर-राज्यीय वित्तीय धोखाधड़ी के मामलों की जांच करता है।
b3_contexts: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) provides income support of Rs 6000 per year to farmer families in three equal instalments. Eligibility: small and marginal farmer families with combined landholding up to 2 hectares. Exclusions: institutional landholders, farmer families holding constitutional posts, serving or retired government employees with monthly pension above Rs 10000, income tax payers.

Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) provides health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation. Eligible families are based on SECC 2011 database. Documents required: Aadhaar card, ration card, income certificate. Over 1700 treatment packages covered. No premium to be paid by beneficiary.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) aims to provide affordable housing for all. Urban component provides interest subsidy on home loans. EWS category (income up to Rs 3 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. LIG category (income Rs 3-6 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. MIG-I (income Rs 6-12 lakh): 4% subsidy. MIG-II (income Rs 12-18 lakh): 3% subsidy.

question: Tuberculosis kya hai aur body ka kaunsa part usually attack karta hai?
ground_truth: Tuberculosis (TB) ek bacterial disease hai jo usually lungs pe attack karta hai, lekin yeh body ke doosre parts ko bhi attack kar sakta hai, jaise ki kidneys, spine, aur brain.
triseva_answer: Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease that usually attacks the lungs. It can also affect other parts of the body, such as the kidneys, spine, and brain.

प्रदत्त संदर्भ के अनुसार, एक असत्य या भ्रामक कथन को निम्नलिखित तत्वों द्वारा परिभाषित किया गया है:

*   **कथन की प्रकृति:** यह एक ऐसा कथन है जो असत्य है।
*   **वक्ता की मानसिक स्थिति:** व्यक्ति का यह ज्ञान या विश्वास होना चाहिए कि कथन असत्य है, अथवा उसका यह विश्वास न होना चाहिए कि वह कथन सत्य है।
*   **विशिष्ट परिदृश्य:**
    *   कोई व्यक्ति असत्य साक्ष्य दे सकता है यदि वह शपथ लेता है कि उसने कुछ ऐसा सुना है जो उसने वास्तव में नहीं सुना।
    *   कोई व्यक्ति असत्य साक्ष्य दे सकता है यदि वह यह बताता है कि वह किसी बात पर विश्वास करता है, जबकि वास्तव में वह उस पर विश्वास नहीं करता।
    *   कोई व्यक्ति असत्य साक्ष्य दे सकता है यदि वह यह बताता है कि वह किसी बात को जानता है, जबकि वास्तव में वह उसे नहीं जानता।
    *   कोई व्यक्ति किसी लोक सेवक को ऐसी जानकारी दे सकता है जिसे वह जानता है या मानता है कि वह असत्य है।

ये परिभाषाएँ तब लागू होती हैं जब कोई व्यक्ति कानूनी रूप से किसी लोक सेवक या शपथ द्वारा बाध्य हो, या किसी कानूनी कार्यवाही में हो।

question: What lifestyle factors can increase your risk of developing cancer?
ground_truth: Lifestyle factors that may increase cancer risk include smoking and tobacco use, too much sun exposure, drinking too much alcohol, not getting enough physical activity, and having obesity.
triseva_answer:
- Smoking and tobacco use
- Excessive sun exposure (UV rays)
- Drinking too much alcohol
- Not getting enough physical activity
- Obesity
- Unhealthy diet
triseva_contexts: cancers are named for where they start. For example, lung cancer starts in the lung, and breast cancer starts in the breast. Cancer may also be described by the type of cell that formed it, such as sarcoma if cancer begins in your bone and soft tissue. Carcinoma is the most common type of cancer. It is formed by epithelial cells, the cells that cover the inside and outside surfaces of your body. How does cancer develop? Cancer is a genetic disease. That means changes in your genes cause it. Changes in your genes are also called gene variants or mutations. Genes are parts of DNA in your cells that you inherit from your parents. However, only some cancers are caused by genes passed down from your parents. Genetic changes can occur to your genes over your lifetime that affect how your cells function. Usually, your body gets rid of damaged cells before they turn cancerous, but this ability goes down as you age. Other factors that may affect your risk of developing cancer can include: Exposure to ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun Smoking Your diet Physical inactivity What are the symptoms of cancer? Cancer symptoms depend on the type of cancer. question: गठिया क्या है?
ground_truth: गठिया कोई भी विकार है जो जोड़ों को प्रभावित करता है, जो वह स्थान हैं जहां दो हड्डियां मिलती हैं। यह आमतौर पर जोड़ों में दर्द और सूजन (सूजन) का कारण बनता है, और समय के साथ, एक सूजा हुआ जोड़ गंभीर रूप से क्षतिग्रस्त हो सकता है।
triseva_answer: गठिया (आर्थराइटिस) कोई भी ऐसा विकार है जो जोड़ों को प्रभावित करता है। जोड़ वे स्थान होते हैं जहाँ दो हड्डियाँ मिलती हैं, जैसे कि कोहनी या घुटना। गठिया के अधिकांश प्रकार जोड़ों में दर्द और सूजन (स्वेलिंग) का कारण बनते हैं। समय के साथ, सूजा हुआ जोड़ गंभीर रूप से क्षतिग्रस्त हो सकता है। गठिया के कुछ प्रकार शरीर के अन्य अंगों, जैसे कि आँखों या त्वचा में भी समस्याएँ उत्पन्न कर सकते हैं।

question: Are employees of Central PSEs (Public Sector Enterprises) eligible for PM-KISAN?
ground_truth: No, employees of Central or State PSEs are excluded from PM-KISAN benefits as per the exclusion criteria in section 4.1(b)(iii).
triseva_answer:
Employees of Central Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs) are **excluded** from eligibility under the PM‑KISAN scheme. Therefore, such employees cannot receive PM‑KISAN benefits.

Source: PM‑KISAN Guidelines (exclusion criteria).

Right to Information (RTI) Act 2005 allows Indian citizens to request information from public authorities. प्रदत्त दस्तावेज (PM-KISAN, Ayushman Bharat, और PMAY) इन योजनाओं के लिए पात्रता, लाभ और आवश्यक दस्तावेजों का वर्णन करते हैं, परंतु इनमें आवेदन जमा करने की प्रक्रिया या प्रतियाँ प्राप्त करने की समय-सीमा के बारे में कोई जानकारी नहीं दी गई है।

हालाँकि, भारत में सरकारी आवेदन प्रक्रियाओं के सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर, समय-सीमा योजना के विशिष्ट नियमों और प्रशासनिक प्रक्रियाओं के आधार पर भिन्न हो सकती है। यह सामान्यतः इस बात पर निर्भर नहीं करता कि आवेदन सप्ताह के किस दिन जमा किया गया है। कई मामलों में, एक पावती रसीद तुरंत प्रदान की जाती है, जबकि आवेदन की पूर्ण प्रति में अधिक समय लग सकता है। सटीक समय-सीमा संबंधित योजना के आधिकारिक दिशानिर्देशों में निर्दिष्ट की जाएगी।

प्रदत्त दस्तावेजों में मुझे इसका उत्तर नहीं मिल सका।

**सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर:**

उच्च रक्तचाप (हाइपरटेंशन) से पीड़ित किसी भी व्यक्ति के लिए यह चिंता का विषय है, चाहे वह किसी भी देश का हो या उसमें कोई लक्षण दिखाई दे रहे हों या नहीं। उच्च रक्तचाप को अक्सर "साइलेंट किलर" (मूक हत्यारा) कहा जाता है क्योंकि इसके आमतौर पर कोई स्पष्ट लक्षण नहीं होते हैं। इसका अर्थ यह है कि व्यक्ति वर्षों तक इससे पीड़ित रह सकता है और उसे इस बात का पता भी नहीं चलता, जबकि यह स्थिति उसके शरीर को निरंतर क्षति पहुँचा रही होती है।

लक्षणों के बिना भी यह चिंताजनक क्यों है, इसके कारण निम्नलिखित हैं:

*   **मूक क्षति (साइलेंट डैमेज):** उच्च रक्तचाप धमनियों की दीवारों पर निरंतर अत्यधिक दबाव डालता है। यह दबाव समय के साथ रक्त वाहिकाओं और अंगों को क्षति पहुँचाता है, जिससे अक्सर तब तक कोई लक्षण दिखाई नहीं देते जब तक कि गंभीर क्षति न हो जाए।
*   **प्रमुख स्वास्थ्य घटनाओं का बढ़ा हुआ जोखिम:** यह मूक क्षति जीवन के लिए घातक या अक्षम करने वाली स्वास्थ्य समस्याओं के जोखिम को काफी बढ़ा देती है, जिनमें शामिल हैं:
    *   **हृदय घात (हार्ट अटैक):** हृदय की मांसपेशियों तक रक्त पहुँचाने वाली धमनियों के संकुचित होने (एथेरोस्क्लेरोसिस) के कारण।
    *   **मस्तिष्क घात (स्ट्रोक):** मस्तिष्क में रक्त वाहिकाओं के कमजोर होने या फटने के कारण।
    *   **वृक्क विफलता (किडनी फेल्योर):** वृक्क (किडनी) में रक्त वाहिकाओं के क्षतिग्रस्त होने के कारण।
    *   **दृष्टि हानि:** आँखों की रक्त वाहिकाओं के क्षतिग्रस्त होने के कारण।
    *   **संज्ञानात्मक गिरावट (कॉग्निटिव डिक्लाइन):** मस्तिष्क में रक्त के प्रवाह में कमी आने के कारण।

मुख्य चिंता यह है कि जब तक कोई व्यक्ति लक्षणों को महसूस करता है (जैसे कि हृदय घात या मस्तिष्क घात के दौरान), तब तक क्षति पहले ही गंभीर और संभावित रूप से अपरिवर्तनीय हो चुकी होती है। इसलिए, उच्च रक्तचाप का प्रबंधन करना और नियमित रूप से इसकी जाँच करवाना अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है ताकि इन गंभीर जटिलताओं को रोका जा सके।

यह सामान्य चिकित्सा ज्ञान है।

उच्च रक्तचाप, जिसे हाइपरटेंशन (hypertension) भी कहा जाता है, को अक्सर "साइलेंट किलर" (silent killer) कहा जाता है क्योंकि यह आमतौर पर कोई प्रत्यक्ष लक्षण उत्पन्न नहीं करता है। यही कारण है कि यह विशेष रूप से चिंताजनक है। भले ही कोई व्यक्ति स्वस्थ महसूस करे, लेकिन निरंतर बढ़ा हुआ रक्तचाप समय के साथ शरीर की रक्त वाहिकाओं और अंगों को क्षति पहुँचाता रहता है।

लक्षणों के बिना भी एक भारतीय नागरिक को उच्च रक्तचाप के बारे में चिंतित होना चाहिए क्योंकि यह निम्नलिखित गंभीर और जीवन के लिए घातक स्थितियों के जोखिम को काफी बढ़ा देता है:

*   **हृदय रोग:** यह दिल का दौरा (heart attack) और हार्ट फेलियर (heart failure) का कारण बन सकता है।
*   **स्ट्रोक (Stroke):** यह मस्तिष्क में रक्त वाहिकाओं को कमजोर कर सकता है, जिससे स्ट्रोक का जोखिम बढ़ जाता है।
*   **किडनी (वृक्क) रोग:** यह गुर्दों की रक्त वाहिकाओं को क्षति पहुँचा सकता है, जिससे वे ठीक से कार्य करने में असमर्थ हो जाते हैं।
*   **दृष्टि की हानि:** यह आँखों की रक्त वाहिकाओं को नुकसान पहुँचा सकता है।
*   **डिमेंशिया (Dementia):** समय के साथ, यह संज्ञानात्मक गिरावट और डिमेंशिया के जोखिम को बढ़ा सकता है।

भारत में, उच्च रक्तचाप एक प्रमुख सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य चिंता है क्योंकि यहाँ इसकी व्यापकता बहुत अधिक है। लक्षणों का अभाव भ्रामक हो सकता है, जिससे लोग यह मान लेते हैं कि उन्हें कोई समस्या नहीं है। इसलिए, यह अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है कि उच्च रक्तचाप से ग्रस्त कोई भी व्यक्ति, चाहे वह कैसा भी महसूस करे, डॉक्टर के परामर्श से दवा, आहार और जीवनशैली में बदलाव के माध्यम से इसका सक्रिय रूप से प्रबंधन करे।
b3_contexts: Normal haemoglobin levels: Men 13.5-17.5 g/dL, Women 12.0-15.5 g/dL, Children 11.0-16.0 g/dL. Low haemoglobin is called anaemia. Common causes include iron deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, and chronic disease. Symptoms include fatigue, weakness, pale skin, and shortness of breath.

Metformin is a medication used to treat type 2 diabetes. It works by reducing glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity. Common side effects include nausea, diarrhoea, and stomach upset. It should be taken with meals. Normal fasting blood sugar: 70-100 mg/dL. Diabetic range: above 126 mg/dL fasting.

A fever is a body temperature above 38°C (100.4°F). Common causes include viral infections, bacterial infections, and inflammation. Treatment includes rest, hydration, and paracetamol or ibuprofen for fever above 38.5°C. Seek immediate medical care if fever exceeds 40°C, or is accompanied by severe headache, stiff neck, or difficulty breathing.

question: Soil Health Card Scheme kisne launch kiya?
ground_truth: Pradhan Mantri Narendra Modi ne Soil Health Card Scheme launch kiya.
triseva_answer: Soil Health Card Scheme ko Prime Minister Narendra Modi ne 19 February 2015 ko Suratgarh, Rajasthan mein launch kiya tha.
triseva_contexts: वेबसाइटें तथ्यों की जांच के बारे में तथ्यों की जांच के लिए जमा करें संख्याओं में तथ्य की जाँच Soil Health Card (Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare) January 17, 2022 “Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa.” – Healthy Earth. Green Farm. -Prime Minister Narendra Modi 1. Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. On the occasion, the Prime Minister gave the slogan: "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." - Healthy Earth, Green Farm. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. The International Year of Soils [5] was celebrated in 2015; the same year, the unique programme of soil health card was launched in India to assess the nutrient status of every farm holding in the country. 2. Objective s [6] : To issue soil health cards [7] every two years to all farmers, so as to provide a basis to address nutrient deficiencies in fertilization practices. To strengthen functioning of Soil Testing

but in the Soil Health Card Scheme, the government is paying attention to see to it that the same person carries out soil analysis for a farmer. Such efforts are helping to enhance the effectiveness of the scheme. The soil card gives the farmers a proper idea of which nutrients their soil is lacking, and hence, which crops they should invest in. It also tells the farmers which fertilizers they need. 5. Financial Progress of Soil Health Card Scheme [13] : Soil Health Cards issued [14] : In Cycle- I (2015-17), 107348416 Soil Health Cards were issued to farmers. In Cycle-II (2017-19), 119773040 Soil Health Cards have been issued to farmers across the country. Setting up / strengthening of soil testing laboratories [15] - So far, 11531 new labs (491 static, 107 mobile, 8811 minilabs and 2122 village level labs) and strengthening of 829 labs have been sanctioned to the states. Organization of demonstrations, trainings and farmer melas [16] : Since 2015, around 6.04 lakh demonstrations, 36928 farmers’ trainings and 7425 farmers’ melas are organized/conducted under the programme. Along with state/ district agriculture machinery and panchayats , village level rural development workers like Krishi Sakhis, Pasu Sakhis are involved in educating farmers on right use of fertilizers. So far 6,954 villages have been identified [17] by the States in which against the target of 26.83 lakh samples / Soil Health Cards, 21.00 lakh samples have been collected, 14.75 lakh samples analysed and 13.59 lakh cards distributed to farmers. question: What is the relationship between Chapter III (Authentication) and the core objective of the Act as stated in its title?
ground_truth: Chapter III provides the authentication mechanisms (Sections 7-10) necessary to verify Aadhaar identity, which enables the targeted delivery of financial subsidies and benefits mentioned in the Act's title.
triseva_answer:
The Act’s title states its purpose: "to provide for, as a good governance, efficient, transparent, and targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits and services, the expenditure for which is incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India... through assigning of unique identity numbers to such individuals" (Source 1). Chapter III (Authentication) contains:

- **Section 7** – "Proof of Aadhaar number necessary for receipt of certain subsidies, benefits and services, etc.": the Central or State Government may require an individual to undergo authentication (or furnish proof of Aadhaar) as a condition for receipt of a subsidy, benefit or service funded from the Consolidated Fund (Source 4).
- **Section 8** – "Authentication of Aadhaar number": the Authority shall perform authentication of an Aadhaar number submitted by a requesting entity, subject to conditions and fees specified by regulations (Source 4).

Thus, Chapter III provides the authentication mechanism that enables the Act’s core objective of delivering subsidies, benefits and services in a targeted manner by verifying the identity of individuals before such benefits are disbursed.

The Act’s title identifies its core purpose as the **targeted delivery of financial and other subsidies, benefits and services**. Chapter III (Authentication) operationalises this purpose by:

- **Section 7** – Requires that an individual undergo authentication or furnish proof of Aadhaar (or apply for enrolment) as a condition for receiving any subsidy, benefit or service funded from the Consolidated Fund of India or a State, thereby linking identity verification directly to the delivery of those benefits.
- **Section 8** – Sets out the procedure for authentication of an Aadhaar number, specifying that the Authority shall perform authentication of biometric or demographic information and that requesting entities must obtain consent before collecting identity information for authentication.

Together, these provisions ensure that only verified Aadhaar‑holders can access the subsidies, benefits and services, which is precisely the mechanism the Act’s title promises – a **targeted, identity‑based delivery** of such entitlements.

प्रदत्त दस्तावेजों के आधार पर, "मृदा संशोधन" (soil amendments) शब्द का स्पष्ट रूप से उपयोग नहीं किया गया है। हालाँकि, मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड (SHC) की सिफारिशों के उद्देश्य और कार्य का वर्णन किया गया है।

दस्तावेजों के अनुसार, मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड किसानों को उनके मृदा के पोषक तत्वों की स्थिति के बारे में जानकारी प्रदान करता है और **"मृदा स्वास्थ्य और उर्वरता में सुधार के लिए लागू किए जाने वाले पोषक तत्वों की उचित मात्रा पर सिफारिशें"** देता है।

इन सिफारिशों की भूमिका किसानों को निम्नलिखित में सहायता करना है:
*   **पोषक तत्वों की कमी को दूर करना:** कार्ड किसानों को यह बताता है कि उनकी मृदा में किन पोषक तत्वों की कमी है।
*   **उर्वरकों का सही उपयोग करना:** यह सलाह देता है कि किन उर्वरकों की आवश्यकता है और कितनी मात्रा में, जिससे किसानों को केवल यूरिया जैसे एकल उर्वरक पर निर्भर रहने के बजाय संतुलित उर्वरकों का उपयोग करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया जा सके।
*   **मृदा स्वास्थ्य और उपज में सुधार करना:** इन सिफारिशों का अंतिम लक्ष्य मृदा के स्वास्थ्य और उर्वरता को बढ़ाना है, जिससे कृषि उत्पादकता में सुधार होता है।

triseva_contexts: Anemia Also called: Iron poor blood On this page Basics Summary Start Here Symptoms Diagnosis and Tests Prevention and Risk Factors Treatments and Therapies Learn More Related Issues Specifics Genetics See, Play and Learn No links available Research Statistics and Research Clinical Trials Journal Articles Resources Find an Expert For You Children Women Older Adults Patient Handouts Summary If you have anemia, your blood does not carry enough oxygen to the rest of your body. The most common cause of anemia is not having enough iron . Your body needs iron to make hemoglobin. Hemoglobin is an iron-rich protein that gives the red color to blood. It carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body. Anemia has three main causes: blood loss, lack of red blood cell production, and high rates of red blood cell destruction. Conditions that may lead to anemia include: Heavy periods Pregnancy Ulcers Colon polyps or colon cancer Inherited disorders A diet that does not have enough iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 Blood disorders such as sickle cell anemia and thalassemia , or cancer Aplastic anemia , a condition that can be inherited or acquired G6PD deficiency , a metabolic disorder Anemia can make you feel tired, cold, dizzy, and irritable. You may be short of breath or have a headache. Your doctor will diagnose anemia with a physical exam and blood tests. Treatment depends on the kind of anemia you have. The most common cause of anemia is not having enough iron . Your body needs iron to make hemoglobin. Hemoglobin is an iron-rich protein that gives the red color to blood. It carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body. Anemia has three main causes: blood loss, lack of red blood cell production, and high rates of red blood cell destruction. Conditions that may lead to anemia include: Heavy periods Pregnancy Ulcers Colon polyps or colon cancer Inherited disorders A diet that does not have enough iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 Blood disorders such as sickle cell anemia and thalassemia , or cancer Aplastic anemia , a condition that can be inherited or acquired G6PD deficiency , a metabolic disorder Anemia can make you feel tired, cold, dizzy, and irritable. You may be short of breath or have a headache. Your doctor will diagnose anemia with a physical exam and blood tests. Treatment depends on the kind of anemia you have. Why is this medication prescribed? Darbepoetin alfa injection is used to treat anemia (a lower than normal number of red blood cells) in people with chronic kidney failure (condition in which the kidneys slowly and permanently stop working over a period of time). Darbepoetin alfa injection is also used to treat anemia caused by chemotherapy in people with certain types of cancer. Darbepoetin alfa cannot be used in place of a red blood cell transfusion to treat severe anemia and has not been shown to improve tiredness or poor well-being that may be caused by anemia. Darbepoetin alfa is in a class of medications called erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs). It works by causing the bone marrow (soft tissue inside the bones where blood is made) to make more red blood cells. How should this medicine be used? Pulmonary (lung) TB wale logon ko treatment ke pehle kuch hafton ke liye ghar par rehne ki salah di jaati hai taaki doosron mein infection phailne se roka ja sake. TB germs hawa ke zariye phailte hain jab koi infected insaan khaansata hai, chheenkta hai, baat karta hai ya gaata hai. Ghar par rehne se, khaaskar jab aapko lung ya throat TB ho, aap un logon ki sankhya kam kar dete hain jo un germs ko saans ke zariye andar le sakte hain. Ghar par rehne ke dauraan, aap infection phailne se bachaav ke liye ye upaay bhi kar sakte hain:
- Khaansate ya chheenkate samay apni naak aur munh ko cover karen.
- Jab bhi mumkin ho, taazi hawa ke liye khidkiyan khuli rakhen.
- Ghar ke doosre logon se doori banaaye rakhen.
Ye steps aapke treatment ke dauraan aapke aas-paas ke logon ko protect karne mein help karte hain.

b3_contexts: transplant , steroids , and specialized treatments for certain autoimmune diseases What are the symptoms of tuberculosis (TB)? Most people who have TB germs in their bodies don't get sick with TB disease. Instead, they have inactive TB infection. With an inactive TB infection, you: Don't have symptoms Can't spread TB to others Could get sick with active TB disease in the future if your immune system becomes weak for another reason Need to take medicine to prevent getting sick with active TB disease in the future If you have TB disease , the TB germs are active, meaning that they are growing (multiplying) inside your body and making you sick. If the TB is growing in your lungs or throat, you can spread the TB germs to other people. You can get sick with TB disease weeks to years after you're infected with TB germs. With TB disease, your symptoms will depend on where the TB is growing in your body: General symptoms may include: Chills and fever Night sweats (heavy sweating during sleep) Losing weight without trying Loss of appetite Weakness or fatigue Symptoms from TB disease in your lungs may include: A cough that lasts longer than 3 weeks Coughing up blood or sputum (a thick mucus from the lungs) Chest pain How is tuberculosis (TB) diagnosed? Your health care provider or your local health department can test you to find out if you have TB germs in your body. They will give you either a TB

Your health care provider or your local health department can test you to find out if you have TB germs in your body. They will give you either a TB skin or blood test . If your test shows that you have TB germs, you'll need to have other tests to see if the germs are actively growing: Tests for TB disease in the lungs usually include testing samples of your sputum and having chest x-rays . Tests for TB disease in other parts of your body may include tests of urine and tissue samples . You may need a TB test if you have symptoms of TB disease or if you are at high risk because you are more likely to be near someone with TB disease. People who have HIV also need to get tested for TB. HIV weakens your immune system. So if you have both HIV and inactive TB, the TB can quickly become active TB disease. You will need treatment for the inactive TB as soon as possible to prevent active TB disease. What is the treatment for tuberculosis (TB)? The treatment for both inactive TB infection and TB disease is antibiotics. To make sure you get rid of all the TB germs in your body, it's very important to follow the directions for taking your medicine. If you don't follow the directions, the TB germs in your body could change and become antibiotic resistant . That means the medicine may stop working and your

your medicine. If you don't follow the directions, the TB germs in your body could change and become antibiotic resistant . That means the medicine may stop working and your TB may become hard to cure. For inactive TB infections , you need to take medicines for three, four, six, or nine months, depending on the treatment plan. Treatment helps make sure you don't get TB disease in the future. For active TB disease , you usually need to take medicines for four, six, or nine months, depending on the treatment plan. Treatment will almost always cure you if you take your pills the right way. For TB disease in your lungs or throat , you'll need to stay home for a few weeks, so you don't spread disease to other people. You can protect the people you live with by: Covering your nose and mouth. Opening windows when possible. Not getting too close to them. For drug-resistant TB disease, which means that the TB germs are resistant to certain TB medicines, you will need to take special medicines. Treatment may take a long time, sometimes months or years. The medicines can cause side effects . Your provider will closely monitor your treatment to make sure the medicines are working. By following medical advice for TB testing and treatment, you can keep yourself healthy and help stop the spread of TB. question: Passage ke according, Indian farmers ke liye soil health assessment kyuki zaroori hai?
ground_truth: Soil health assessment is important kyuki mitti mein nutrients ka status samajhne aur appropriate nutrient dosage apply karne se mitti ki fertility improve hoti hai, jo ki ek sacch mein fertile aur prosperous agricultural land ke liye zaroori hai.
triseva_answer: Soil health assessment isatna important hai kyunki yeh farmers ko unki soil ke nutrient status ke baare mein bataata hai aur appropriate fertilizer dosages ke liye recommendations provide karta hai. Yeh farmers ko nutrient deficiencies address karne, balanced fertilizers apply karne, chemical fertilizer use ko 8-10% tak kam karne, aur crop yields ko 5-6% tak badhaane mein help karta hai. Iss scheme ka aim har do saal mein soil health cards issue karna hai taaki farmers apni soil health aur fertility improve kar saken.

question: Why is the prohibition on labour-displacing machines significant in the context of this scheme?
ground_truth: The prohibition ensures that works are performed using manual labour, preserving employment opportunities for workers rather than replacing them with machines.
triseva_answer:
The prohibition on labour‑displacing machines is a core safeguard in the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGA). Its significance is:

- **Ensures manual employment**: By requiring works to be performed manually wherever practicable, the scheme guarantees that a large number of person‑days of unskilled manual work are generated, directly fulfilling the objective of providing at least 100 days of employment per rural household.
- **Protects rural livelihoods**: Manual work is the primary source of income for the poorest rural families; using machines would reduce the demand for labour and undermine the scheme’s goal of strengthening the livelihood resource base of the poor.
- **Promotes asset creation through labour**: The assets created under MGNREGA are intended to be durable and of prescribed quality, achieved through human effort rather than mechanisation, aligning with the scheme’s focus on productive, community‑owned assets.
- **Upholds social inclusion**: Manual labour is accessible to all adult members of a household, including women and marginalized groups, thereby supporting the scheme’s mandate for proactive social inclusion.

*Source: MGNREGA Act, clause 22 – “As far as practicable, works executed by the programme implementation agencies shall be performed by using manual labour and no labour displacing machines shall be used.”*

The documents repeatedly emphasize the focus on manual labour and employment:
*   The scheme is the "Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act" (MGNREGA), which highlights its core purpose of guaranteeing employment.
*   Clause 22 explicitly states that works "shall be performed by using manual labour and no labour displacing machines shall be used."
*   The rules regarding material costs, administrative expenses for personnel, and the prohibition on contractors all point to a scheme designed to create jobs for people rather than simply complete projects efficiently.

Therefore, the prohibition on machines is crucial to ensure that the scheme fulfills its mandate of generating employment and providing livelihoods to the rural workforce. Allowing machines would reduce the number of workers needed, directly undermining the scheme's fundamental goal of an employment guarantee.

The prohibition on labour‑displacing machines is a key safeguard in the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGA) because:

- It guarantees that the work created under the scheme is performed manually, directly fulfilling the scheme’s core objective of providing **unskilled manual employment** to rural households (Source: MGNREGA Act, clause 22).
- By barring machines that replace human labour, the scheme **prevents displacement of workers**, ensuring that the demand for labour translates into actual jobs rather than mechanised output.
- It promotes **skill development and capacity building** among the rural workforce, as workers gain experience in manual construction and asset‑creation activities.
- The restriction supports **social inclusion** by giving priority to the poorest and most vulnerable groups who rely on manual work for their livelihood.
- It helps maintain the **integrity of the employment guarantee**—the scheme’s promise of at least 100 days of work per household is meaningful only when the work is genuinely labour‑intensive.

question: What is the significance of a work being classified as 'preferred work' under this Act?
ground_truth: Preferred work means any work taken up for implementation on a priority basis under a Scheme, indicating it receives preferential treatment in project selection and execution.
triseva_answer:
Under the Act, a work classified as **‘preferred work’** is one that is taken up for implementation on a **priority basis** under a Scheme. This designation means that such works must be executed before other non‑priority works and are subject to specific priority rules:

- The order of priority is set by each Gram Panchayat, considering local needs, resources and potential, and must ensure that **at least 60 % of the works in a district (by cost) are for creating productive assets directly linked to agriculture and allied activities**.
- Works that create individual assets are further prioritized for households belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, nomadic/denotified tribes, families below the poverty line, women‑headed households, physically handicapped‑headed households, beneficiaries of land reforms, and other specified categories.

Thus, the significance of ‘preferred work’ is that it guarantees **priority implementation** and **targeted focus** on agricultural‑linked and socially‑beneficial projects.

question: What information does the soil health card contain regarding nutrients?
ground_truth: The card contains recommendations on the dosage of different nutrients needed and advises farmers on the fertilizers and their quantities they should apply.
triseva_answer:
The Soil Health Card provides the following nutrient‑related information:

- **Nutrient status** for 12 key parameters:
  - Macro‑nutrients: Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K)
  - Secondary nutrient: Sulphur (S)
  - Micro‑nutrients: Zinc (Zn), Iron (Fe), Copper (Cu), Manganese (Mn), Boron (Bo)
  - Physical parameters: pH, Electrical Conductivity (EC), Organic Carbon (OC)

- **Fertilizer recommendations** based on the measured nutrient levels, including the specific dosage of each nutrient needed.

- **Advisory guidance** on the types and quantities of fertilizers to apply, as well as any soil amendments required to correct deficiencies and achieve optimal yields.

question: Which section addresses the penalty for disclosing identity information?
ground_truth: Section 37 addresses the penalty for disclosing identity information.

Source: Aadhaar Act, Chapter VII – Offences and Penalties, Section 37.

question: What principle should guide wage payment to ensure fairness across genders?
ground_truth: The State Government shall link the wages without any gender bias with the quantity of work done.
triseva_answer:
The guiding principle for wage payment is that wages must be linked to the quantity of work performed **without any gender bias**. This ensures equal remuneration for equal work and prevents discrimination based on gender.  
- *Source*: MGNREGA Act – Section 17 states that "The State Government shall link the wages, without any gender bias, with the quantity of work done..."  
- *Source*: MGNREGA Act – Section 18 further provides for a separate schedule of rates for women to improve participation, reinforcing the principle of non‑discriminatory wage fixation.

question: What comprehensive benefit does a farmer gain by following all recommendations in the Soil Health Card?

question: Why might a pregnant woman be at risk of developing anemia?
ground_truth: Pregnancy is listed as a condition that may lead to anemia, likely because the body's iron demands increase during pregnancy to support blood volume expansion and fetal development.
triseva_answer: Pregnancy is listed among the conditions that may lead to anemia. Additionally, a diet that does not provide enough iron, folic acid, or vitamin B12 can increase the risk of developing anemia during pregnancy.

Anemia Also called: Iron poor blood On this page Basics Summary Start Here Symptoms Diagnosis and Tests Prevention and Risk Factors Treatments and Therapies Learn More Related Issues Specifics Genetics See, Play and Learn No links available Research Statistics and Research Clinical Trials Journal Articles Resources Find an Expert For You Children Women Older Adults Patient Handouts Summary If you have anemia, your blood does not carry enough oxygen to the rest of your body. The most common cause of anemia is not having enough iron . Your body needs iron to make hemoglobin. Hemoglobin is an iron-rich protein that gives the red color to blood. It carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body. Anemia has three main causes: blood loss, lack of red blood cell production, and high rates of red blood cell destruction. Conditions that may lead to anemia include: Heavy periods Pregnancy Ulcers Colon polyps or colon cancer Inherited disorders A diet that does not have enough iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 Blood disorders such as sickle cell anemia and thalassemia , or cancer Aplastic anemia , a condition that can be inherited or acquired G6PD deficiency , a metabolic disorder Anemia can make you feel tired, cold, dizzy, and irritable. You may be short of breath or have a headache. Your doctor will diagnose anemia with a physical exam and blood tests. Treatment depends on the kind of anemia you have. However, based on general medical knowledge, a pregnant woman might be at risk of developing anemia for a few key reasons:

*   **Increased Blood Volume:** During pregnancy, a woman's blood volume increases significantly to support the growing fetus. This increase in plasma (the liquid part of the blood) is greater than the increase in red blood cells, which can dilute the concentration of red blood cells and lead to a condition called physiological anemia of pregnancy.
*   **Increased Iron Demand:** The developing fetus and placenta require a substantial amount of iron for their own growth and for producing hemoglobin. If the mother's iron stores are not sufficient to meet this increased demand, she can develop iron-deficiency anemia.
*   **Other Nutrient Deficiencies:** Besides iron, pregnancy also increases the need for other nutrients essential for red blood cell production, such as folate and vitamin B12. A deficiency in any of these can contribute to anemia.

question: What should State Governments do when a land owner dies and the family inherits the land?
ground_truth: State Governments should reassess the eligibility of the family under PM-KISAN. If eligible, details of new beneficiaries with fresh self-declarations should be provided to authorities for inclusion/modifications so benefits can continue to survivors.
triseva_answer:
When a land‑owner dies and the land passes to heirs, State Governments must:

- Establish an administrative mechanism within the existing land‑revenue system to handle the mutation of land records, assigning clear responsibility to the officials who carry out the mutation.
- For inheritances recorded **before 01 December 2018**, determine the family’s eligibility under the scheme according to the prescribed conditions and exclusion clauses.
- For inheritances occurring **between 01 December 2018 and 31 January 2019**, apply the proportionate‑benefit rule for the relevant installment.
- For inheritances **after 01 February 2019**, successors become eligible from the date their names are entered in the land records, provided they satisfy all other scheme requirements.
- After inheritance, reassess the family’s eligibility:
  * If the family remains eligible, submit the new beneficiaries’ details together with fresh self‑declarations to the PM‑KISAN portal for inclusion or modification so that benefits continue.
  * If the family is no longer eligible, update the portal to discontinue the benefits.
- If, after inheritance, a family becomes newly eligible, incorporate their details in the database so that benefits commence from the date the inheritance became operational.

Source: PM‑KISAN Operational Guidelines (Revised) – Sections on succession, mutation of land records, and eligibility reassessment.

When a land owner dies and the land is inherited, State Governments must:

- **Update land records (mutation)**: Put in place an administrative mechanism based on the existing land‑revenue system and assign clear responsibility to officials for carrying out mutation of land records to reflect the new owners.
- **Determine eligibility of successors**: Assess whether the inheriting family members meet the scheme’s eligibility criteria (e.g., ownership of cultivable land, income limits) and apply the exclusion clauses as prescribed.
- **Update the PM‑KISAN portal**: If the family is no longer eligible, update the portal so that benefits are discontinued; if they remain eligible, provide the new beneficiary details along with fresh self‑declarations for inclusion or modification.
- **Handle time‑bound updates**: For inheritance occurring before 01.12.2018, States may update land records in a time‑bound manner; for inheritance between 01.12.2018 and 31.01.2019, provide proportionate benefits from the date of transfer until 31.03.2019.
- **Incorporate freshly eligible families**: If, after inheritance, the family becomes newly eligible under PM‑KISAN, incorporate all details into the database so benefits start from the date inheritance became operational.

Source: PM‑KISAN Operational Guidelines (Revised) – Sections 5.3.1, 5.3.3, 5.3.4; PM‑KISAN Guidelines – Sections 5.3.1, 5.3.3, 5.3.4.

IMPORTANT WARNING: RimabotulinumtoxinB injection may spread from the area of injection and cause symptoms of botulism, including severe or life-threatening difficulty breathing or swallowing. People who develop difficulty swallowing during their treatment with this medication may continue to have this difficulty for several months. They may need to be fed through a feeding tube to avoid getting food or drink into their lungs. Symptoms can occur within hours of an injection with rimabotulinumtoxinB or as late as several weeks after treatment. Symptoms may occur in people of any age being treated for any condition, but the risk is probably highest in children being treated for spasticity (muscle stiffness and tightness). Tell your doctor if you have or have ever had any swallowing problems or breathing problems, such as asthma or emphysema, or any condition that affects your muscles or nerves such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, Lou Gehrig's disease; condition in which the nerves that control muscle movement slowly die, causing the muscles to shrink and weaken), motor neuropathy (condition in which the muscles weaken over time), myasthenia gravis (condition that causes certain muscles to weaken, especially after activity), or Lambert-Eaton syndrome (condition that causes muscle weakness that may improve with activity). If you experience any of the following symptoms, call your doctor immediately: loss of strength or muscle weakness all over the body; double or blurred vision; drooping eyelids; difficulty swallowing, breathing, or speaking; or inability to control urination. Your doctor will give you the manufacturer's patient information sheet

*   गठिया से संबंधित आनुवंशिकी और अन्य संबंधित स्थितियाँ

यह दर्शाता है कि रूमेटोलॉजिस्ट वे विशेषज्ञ हैं जो गठिया के विभिन्न रूपों और उनके उपचारों का प्रबंधन करते हैं।

IMPORTANT WARNING: RimabotulinumtoxinB injection may spread from the area of injection and cause symptoms of botulism, including severe or life-threatening difficulty breathing or swallowing. People who develop difficulty swallowing during their treatment with this medication may continue to have this difficulty for several months. They may need to be fed through a feeding tube to avoid getting food or drink into their lungs. Symptoms can occur within hours of an injection with rimabotulinumtoxinB or as late as several weeks after treatment. Symptoms may occur in people of any age being treated for any condition, but the risk is probably highest in children being treated for spasticity (muscle stiffness and tightness). Tell your doctor if you have or have ever had any swallowing problems or breathing problems, such as asthma or emphysema, or any condition that affects your muscles or nerves such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, Lou Gehrig's disease; condition in which the nerves that control muscle movement slowly die, causing the muscles to shrink and weaken), motor neuropathy (condition in which the muscles weaken over time), myasthenia gravis (condition that causes certain muscles to weaken, especially after activity), or Lambert-Eaton syndrome (condition that causes muscle weakness that may improve with activity). If you experience any of the following symptoms, call your doctor immediately: loss of strength or muscle weakness all over the body; double or blurred vision; drooping eyelids; difficulty swallowing, breathing, or speaking; or inability to control urination. Your doctor will give you the manufacturer's patient information sheet

question: Soil Health Card use karne se chemical fertilizer ka use kam kyun ho jaata hai?
ground_truth: Soil Health Card se mitti mein nutrients ki jaankari milti hai. Isse farmers ko pata chal jaata hai ki unhe sirf utna hi fertilizer daalna hai jitna unki mitti ko zaroorat hai. Isse chemical fertilizer ka zyada use kam ho jaata hai.
triseva_answer: Soil Health Card (SHC) scheme provides farmers with a detailed report of their soil's nutrient status (pH, organic carbon, N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B) and specific fertilizer recommendations. By following these recommendations, farmers apply only the nutrients that are actually needed, using balanced fertilizers and micro‑nutrients instead of blanket application of chemical fertilizers such as urea. This targeted, soil‑test‑based nutrient management leads to an 8‑10 % reduction in overall chemical fertilizer use while maintaining or improving yields.
triseva_contexts: Soil Health Card scheme provides farmers with soil nutrient status and fertilizer recommendations. Key parameters include pH, organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and micronutrients. Farmers should apply balanced fertilizers based on SHC advice rather than using only urea, to improve yield and soil health.

Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. On the occasion, the Prime Minister gave the slogan: "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." - Healthy Earth, Green Farm. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. The International Year of Soils [5] was celebrated in 2015; the same year, the unique programme of soil health card was launched in India to assess the nutrient status of every farm holding in the country. 2. Objective s [6] : To issue soil health cards [7] every two years to all farmers, so as to provide a basis to address nutrient deficiencies in fertilization practices. Some of the findings of the study are as follows: More than 90 per cent of farmers surveyed informed that they have not got their soil tested before the implementation of this scheme. 92 per cent farmers reported not having used balanced fertilizer and micro nutrients in absence of information related to availability of nutrients in their soil. 4.  **Study Findings:** Document 3 mein mention kiye gaye National Productivity Council ke ek study ne iss impact ko confirm kiya hai. Ismein paaya gaya ki "Soil Health Cards ki recommendations ke according fertilizer aur micro-nutrients apply karne se chemical fertilizer application mein 8-10 per cent ki decrease hui."

In essence, Soil Health Card farmers ko unki mitti ki actual needs ke hisaab se fertilizers apply karne mein guide karta hai, jisse chemical fertilizers ka indiscriminate aur excessive use kam ho jaata hai.

question: How can a farmer use the soil health card to improve agricultural productivity?
ground_truth: A farmer can use the nutrient status information and dosage recommendations provided in the soil health card to apply appropriate nutrients, thereby improving soil health and fertility, which enhances agricultural productivity.
triseva_answer:
The Soil Health Card (SHC) provides a detailed report of the farm’s soil status and specific recommendations to boost productivity. Farmers can use it as follows:

- **Review the SHC parameters**: Check the levels of pH, organic carbon, nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), sulphur (S), and micronutrients (Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B) to understand the current soil condition.
- **Apply balanced fertilizers**: Follow the SHC’s dosage recommendations for each nutrient instead of relying solely on urea. Use the suggested types and quantities of fertilizers to meet the crop’s nutrient needs.
- **Implement soil amendments**: Use the SHC’s advice on soil amendments (e.g., lime, gypsum) to correct pH or address specific deficiencies.
- **Select appropriate crops**: Based on the soil nutrient status, choose crops that are best suited to the soil, and avoid those that may not thrive.
- **Seek expert assistance**: Utilize the support of agriculture officers or experts who can help implement the corrective measures outlined on the card.
- **Update regularly**: The SHC is issued once every three years, so obtain a new card to keep the recommendations current as soil conditions change.

question: Why might the cut-off date of 01.02.2019 not apply in certain circumstances?
ground_truth: The cut-off date does not apply when transfer of ownership of cultivable land takes place on account of succession due to death of the landowner.
triseva_answer:
The cut‑off date of 01.02.2019 for determining eligibility under the PM‑KISAN scheme does not apply in the following circumstances:

- **Succession due to death of the landowner** – when ownership of cultivable land passes to heirs because the owner dies, the successors are eligible for benefits even if the land records are updated after 01.02.2019. (Source: PM‑KISAN Operational Guidelines, Clause 5.2 & 5.3)
- **Transfers of ownership between 01.12.2018 and 31.01.2019** – if the land is transferred by purchase, succession, will, gift, etc., during this period, the beneficiary is entitled to a proportionate benefit from the date of transfer up to 31.03.2019. (Source: PM‑KISAN Operational Guidelines, Clause 5.3)
- **Special provisions for North‑East States and Jharkhand** – an exception has been made for these states, meaning the 01.02.2019 cut‑off may not be applied there. (Source: PM‑KISAN Operational Guidelines, Clause 5.2)
- **Late updating of land records for succession before 01.12.2018** – if land records are updated after 01.12.2018 but before 01.02.2019 due to inheritance, the successors become eligible from the date of entry of their rights. (Source: PM‑KISAN Operational Guidelines, Clause 5.3.1)

These exceptions ensure that legitimate changes in land ownership, especially those arising from inheritance, are not excluded by the fixed cut‑off date.

question: Name three lifestyle habits that can increase the risk of heart disease.
ground_truth: Three lifestyle habits that increase heart disease risk include eating a diet high in saturated fats and salt, not getting enough physical activity, and smoking or exposure to secondhand smoke.
triseva_answer:

IMPORTANT WARNING: Cyclosporine is available in its original form and as another product that has been modified (changed) so that the medication can be better absorbed in the body. Original cyclosporine and cyclosporine (modified) are absorbed by the body in different amounts, so they cannot be substituted for one another. Take only the type of cyclosporine that was prescribed by your doctor. When your doctor gives you a written prescription, check to be sure that he or she has specified the type of cyclosporine you should receive. Each time you have your prescription filled, look at the brand name printed on your prescription label to be sure that you have received the same type of cyclosporine. Talk to your pharmacist if the brand name is unfamiliar or you are not sure you have received the right type of cyclosporine. Taking cyclosporine or cyclosporine (modified) may increase the risk that you will develop an infection or cancer, especially lymphoma (cancer of a part of the immune system) or skin cancer. This risk may be higher if you take cyclosporine or cyclosporine (modified) with other medications that decrease the functioning of the immune system. Tell your doctor if you are taking any medications that decrease the functioning of the immune system and if you have or have ever had any type of cancer. Most people who have TB germs in their bodies don't get sick with TB disease. Instead, they have inactive TB infection. With an inactive TB infection, you: Don't have symptoms Can't spread TB to others Could get sick with active TB disease in the future if your immune system becomes weak for another reason Need to take medicine to prevent getting sick with active TB disease in the future If you have TB disease , the TB germs are active, meaning that they are growing (multiplying) inside your body and making you sick. If the TB is growing in your lungs or throat, you can spread the TB germs to other people. You can get sick with TB disease weeks to years after you're infected with TB germs. With TB disease, your symptoms will depend on where the TB is growing in your body: General symptoms may include: Chills and fever Night sweats (heavy sweating during sleep) Losing weight without trying Loss of appetite Weakness or fatigue Symptoms from TB disease in your lungs may include: A cough that lasts longer than 3 weeks Coughing up blood or sputum (a thick mucus from the lungs) Chest pain How is tuberculosis (TB) diagnosed? your medicine. If you don't follow the directions, the TB germs in your body could change and become antibiotic resistant . That means the medicine may stop working and your TB may become hard to cure. For inactive TB infections , you need to take medicines for three, four, six, or nine months, depending on the treatment plan. Treatment helps make sure you don't get TB disease in the future. For active TB disease , you usually need to take medicines for four, six, or nine months, depending on the treatment plan. Treatment will almost always cure you if you take your pills the right way. For TB disease in your lungs or throat , you'll need to stay home for a few weeks, so you don't spread disease to other people. You can protect the people you live with by: Covering your nose and mouth. Opening windows when possible. Not getting too close to them. For drug-resistant TB disease, which means that the TB germs are resistant to certain TB medicines, you will need to take special medicines. Treatment may take a long time, sometimes months or years. The medicines can cause side effects . Your provider will closely monitor your treatment to make sure the medicines are working. By following medical advice for TB testing and treatment, you can keep yourself healthy and help stop the spread of TB. question: What is a transient ischemic attack (TIA) and how does it differ from a stroke?
ground_truth: A TIA, or 'mini-stroke,' occurs when blood supply to the brain is blocked for a short time. Unlike a stroke, the damage to brain cells is not permanent, but having a TIA significantly increases your risk of having a full stroke.
triseva_answer:
A transient ischemic attack (TIA) is a temporary blockage of blood flow to part of the brain, often called a "mini‑stroke." The blockage lasts only a short time, so brain cells are not permanently damaged, but a TIA puts you at a much higher risk of having a stroke. A stroke occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is interrupted for a longer period, causing brain cells to die within minutes, which can result in lasting brain damage, long‑term disability, or death.

- **TIA**: brief interruption, no permanent brain cell damage, symptoms resolve quickly.
- **Stroke**: prolonged interruption, brain cells die, symptoms may be permanent and can cause lasting disability.

*   **Secondary Nutrients:** These are nutrients that plants require in moderate amounts, less than the primary nutrients (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium) but more than micro-nutrients. The three main secondary nutrients are **Calcium (Ca), Magnesium (Mg), and Sulfur (S)**.

A deficiency in even one micro-nutrient can significantly impact plant health and yield. Key micro-nutrients include **Iron (Fe), Manganese (Mn), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Boron (B), Molybdenum (Mo), and Chlorine (Cl)**.

ground_truth: Arthritis ek bimari hai jo joints ko affect karti hai, jo vo jagah hain jahan do haddi aapas mein milti hain, jaise ki elbow ya knee. Isse joint pain aur inflammation (swelling) hoti hai.
triseva_answer: Arthritis is any disorder that affects the joints. Joints are places where two bones meet, such as the elbow or knee. Most types of arthritis cause joint pain and inflammation (swelling), and over time a swollen joint can become severely damaged. Some kinds of arthritis can also cause problems in other parts of the body, such as the eyes or skin.

Based on the provided documents, a false or misleading statement is defined differently depending on the legal context:

**1. In the context of consumer protection (from Doc 1):**

A "misleading advertisement" is one that:
*   (i) Falsely describes a product or service.
*   (ii) Gives a false guarantee or is likely to mislead consumers about the nature, substance, quantity, or quality of a product or service.
*   (iii) Conveys a representation that would be an unfair trade practice if made by the manufacturer or seller.
*   (iv) Deliberately conceals important information.

**2. In the context of criminal law (from Docs 2 and 3):**

A "false statement" (specifically, giving false evidence) is considered to be:
*   Stating something you know to be false while under oath.
*   Stating that you know something to be true when you have no knowledge of the subject.
*   An interpreter or translator providing a false interpretation or translation that they know is not true.
*   Making a false entry in a book, record, or electronic record with the intention of causing a consequence.

question: Why is it important that gestational diabetes is often screened between 24-28 weeks of pregnancy?
ground_truth: Early screening between 24-28 weeks allows for timely detection and management of gestational diabetes, which can help prevent serious health complications for both mother and baby during the remainder of pregnancy.
triseva_answer: Screening for gestational diabetes between 24 and 28 weeks is important because the purpose of the screening is to regulate fetal growth and development, and much of the interaction between blood sugar and the fetus takes place later in pregnancy. Additionally, gestational diabetes is more common in the second or third trimester, making this window an optimal time for detection.

With type 2 diabetes, the symptoms often develop slowly, over several years. The symptoms can be so mild that you might not even notice them. Gestational diabetes often has no symptoms. If you do have symptoms, they may be mild. If you are pregnant, you will usually be screened for this condition between 24 and 28 weeks of pregnancy. How is diabetes diagnosed? To find out if you have diabetes, your health care provider will use one or more glucose blood tests . There are several types, including the A1C test . What are the treatments for diabetes? Treatment for diabetes involves managing your blood glucose levels: If you have type 1 diabetes, you will need to take daily doses of insulin, either by injection or through a special pump. Some people also need to take another type of diabetes medicine that works with insulin. If you have type 2 diabetes, you may be able to manage or even reverse it by making lifestyle changes . These include eating a healthy diet , staying at healthy weight , and getting regular physical activity . Some people also need to take diabetes medicines to manage their diabetes. If you have gestational diabetes, you may be able to lower your glucose levels by eating a healthy diet and getting regular exercise. But be sure to talk to your

If you have gestational diabetes, you may be able to lower your glucose levels by eating a healthy diet and getting regular exercise. But be sure to talk to your provider about your treatment options. Gestational diabetes usually goes away after you give birth. But you will have a higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes later. Checking your blood glucose levels is also an important part of managing your diabetes. Ask your provider about the best way to check your blood glucose level and how often you should check it. Can diabetes be prevented? Type 1 diabetes can't be prevented. You may be able to delay or prevent type 2 diabetes through the same lifestyle changes that are used to manage diabetes (eating a healthy diet, staying at a healthy weight, and getting regular physical activity). These lifestyle changes may also help prevent gestational diabetes . ground_truth: Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects registered with Professional bodies and carrying out profession by undertaking practices are excluded from PM-KISAN benefits.
triseva_answer:
The professionals excluded from PM‑KISAN benefits are:
- Doctors
- Engineers
- Lawyers
- Chartered Accountants
- Architects

These professionals must be registered with the relevant professional bodies and be carrying out their profession by undertaking practices. Source: PM‑KISAN Guidelines (exclusion clause).

question: एक अधिकारी सार्वजनिक सूचना अधिकारी को उनके कर्तव्यों का पालन करने में कैसे सहायता कर सकता है?
ground_truth: एक लोक सूचना अधिकारी किसी भी अन्य अधिकारी से आवश्यक सहायता ले सकता है और उस अधिकारी को अधिनियम के किसी भी उल्लंघन के लिए सार्वजनिक सूचना अधिकारी माना जाएगा।
triseva_answer: सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत, एक लोक सूचना अधिकारी (पी आई ओ) अपने कर्तव्यों के उचित निर्वहन के लिए आवश्यक समझे जाने वाले किसी भी अन्य अधिकारी की सहायता ले सकता है। जिस अधिकारी की सहायता मांगी गई है, उसे पी आई ओ को पूर्ण सहायता प्रदान करनी होगी, और इस अधिनियम के किसी भी उल्लंघन के उद्देश्य से, उस अधिकारी को पी आई ओ के रूप में माना जाएगा। स्रोत: आर टी आई अधिनियम, धारा 5(4)-(5)।

मैं दिए गए दस्तावेजों में इस प्रश्न का उत्तर नहीं खोज पा रहा हूँ।

यह जानकारी सामान्य ज्ञान पर आधारित है:

एक अधिकारी, जन सूचना अधिकारी (PIO) को उनके कर्तव्यों के निर्वहन में कई तरीकों से सहायता प्रदान कर सकता है, विशेष रूप से सूचना का अधिकार (RTI) अधिनियम, 2005 के तहत।

1. **सूचना प्रदान करना:** जन सूचना अधिकारी (PIO) के लिए सबसे महत्वपूर्ण सहायता अन्य अधिकारियों द्वारा प्रदान की जाती है, जिनके पास मांगी गई जानकारी होती है। वे निम्नलिखित माध्यमों से सहायता कर सकते हैं:
    * जन सूचना अधिकारी (PIO) के प्रश्नों का तुरंत उत्तर देना।
    * अनुरोधित दस्तावेजों, फाइलों या डेटा की आपूर्ति करना।
    * यह सुनिश्चित करना कि प्रदान की गई जानकारी सटीक और पूर्ण हो।

2. **प्रक्रियात्मक सहायता:** अधिकारी जन सूचना अधिकारी (PIO) को प्रक्रियात्मक पहलुओं में सहायता कर सकते हैं, जैसे कि रिकॉर्ड का पता लगाना, फाइलों को संकलित करना और यह सुनिश्चित करना कि जानकारी समय पर जारी की जाए।

3. **अनुपालन सुनिश्चित करना:** वरिष्ठ अधिकारी अपने विभागों को RTI अधिनियम के अनुपालन में रहने में मदद कर सकते हैं, जिससे जन सूचना अधिकारी (PIO) का कार्य सुगम हो जाता है। इसमें कर्मचारियों को उनके कर्तव्यों के बारे में प्रशिक्षित करना और RTI आवेदनों को संभालने के लिए स्पष्ट आंतरिक प्रक्रियाएँ स्थापित करना शामिल है।
b3_contexts: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) provides income support of Rs 6000 per year to farmer families in three equal instalments. Eligibility: small and marginal farmer families with combined landholding up to 2 hectares. Exclusions: institutional landholders, farmer families holding constitutional posts, serving or retired government employees with monthly pension above Rs 10000, income tax payers.

Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) provides health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation. Eligible families are based on SECC 2011 database. Documents required: Aadhaar card, ration card, income certificate. Over 1700 treatment packages covered. No premium to be paid by beneficiary.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) aims to provide affordable housing for all. Urban component provides interest subsidy on home loans. EWS category (income up to Rs 3 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. LIG category (income Rs 3-6 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. MIG-I (income Rs 6-12 lakh): 4% subsidy. MIG-II (income Rs 12-18 lakh): 3% subsidy.

question: अनुच्छेद के अनुसार 'अन्यायपूर्ण अनुबंध' की परिभाषा क्या है?
ground_truth: अन्यायपूर्ण अनुबंध एक निर्माता, व्यापारी, या सेवा प्रदाता और उपभोक्ता के बीच एक अनुबंध है जिसमें ऐसी शर्तें होती हैं जो उपभोक्ता के अधिकारों में महत्वपूर्ण परिवर्तन का कारण बनती हैं, जैसे कि अत्यधिक सुरक्षा जमा, असमान दंड, या अनुचित शुल्क जो उपभोक्ता को नुकसान पहुंचाते हैं।
triseva_answer: ‘अन्यायपूर्ण अनुबंध’ का अर्थ एक निर्माता या व्यापारी या सेवा प्रदाता और दूसरी ओर एक उपभोक्ता के बीच का ऐसा अनुबंध है, जिसमें ऐसी शर्तें हों जो ऐसे उपभोक्ता के अधिकारों में महत्वपूर्ण परिवर्तन का कारण बनती हों, जिनमें निम्नलिखित सम्मिलित हैं, यथा: (i) संविदात्मक दायित्वों के निष्पादन के लिए उपभोक्ता से स्पष्ट रूप से अत्यधिक सुरक्षा जमा राशि की मांग करना; (ii) अनुबंध के उल्लंघन के लिए उपभोक्ता पर ऐसी कोई भी दंड राशि थोपना जो दूसरे पक्ष को हुए नुकसान के पूर्णतः अनुपातहीन हो; (iii) लागू दंड का भुगतान करने पर भी ऋण के शीघ्र पुनर्भुगतान को स्वीकार करने से इनकार करना; (iv) किसी भी पक्ष को उचित कारण के बिना एकपक्षीय रूप से ऐसे अनुबंध को समाप्त करने का अधिकार देना; (v) एक पक्ष को उपभोक्ता की सहमति के बिना दूसरे पक्ष के नुकसान के लिए अनुबंध को सौंपने की अनुमति देना या उसका प्रभाव डालना; (vi) उपभोक्ता पर कोई भी अनुचित शुल्क, दायित्व या शर्त थोपना जो ऐसे उपभोक्ता को नुकसान की स्थिति में डालती हो। स्रोत: उपभोक्ता संरक्षण अधिनियम (कानूनी डेटाबेस)।

"अनुचित अनुबंध" (अनफेयर कॉन्ट्रैक्ट) शब्द का उल्लेख किसी भी दस्तावेज़ में नहीं किया गया है। ये दस्तावेज़ विशेष रूप से किसानों, स्वास्थ्य सेवा और आवास के लिए सरकारी कल्याणकारी योजनाओं के बारे में हैं।

Based on general medical knowledge, ankylosing spondylitis can affect daily activities in the following ways:

*   **Stiffness and Pain:** The primary symptoms are chronic pain and stiffness in the lower back and hips, which are often worse in the morning or after periods of rest. This can make it difficult to get out of bed, stand up straight, or perform simple movements like bending over to tie shoes.
*   **Reduced Flexibility:** Inflammation can limit the range of motion in the spine and other joints (like the hips and shoulders), making it hard to twist, reach for objects on a shelf, or participate in sports and hobbies.
*   **Fatigue:** Many people with ankylosing spondylitis experience significant fatigue, which can reduce energy levels and make it challenging to complete daily tasks or maintain a regular work schedule.
*   **Posture Changes:** Over time, the condition can cause the spine to fuse in a stooped-forward position, which can impact balance, make walking difficult, and potentially affect breathing.
*   **Difficulty with Daily Tasks:** Simple activities like dressing, driving, or sitting for long periods can become painful and challenging due to the stiffness and pain.

b3_contexts: arthritis is one type. Psoriatic arthritis affects people with psoriasis (itchy or sore scaly red and white skin patches). Gout is a painful type of arthritis that happens when too much uric acid builds up in your body. It often starts in the big toe. Other joints can also be affected. Ankylosing spondylitis is a type of arthritis of the spine that can cause stiffness and make it difficult to move and bend. What are the symptoms of arthritis? Pain, redness, warmth, and joint inflammation are common arthritis symptoms. You may not be able to move your joint as well as it should. Other symptoms could include fever , weight loss, breathing difficulties, or a rash. Symptoms often get worse as you age. Some symptoms of arthritis may be signs of other illnesses. Who is more likely to get arthritis? A few things that might increase your chance of getting arthritis include: Family history. You may be more likely to get certain types of arthritis if a member of your family has the disorder. Age. The risk of getting many types of arthritis increases with age. Sex. Certain types of arthritis are more common in women, while other types are more common in men. Other factors that might increase your risk of getting arthritis include having a previous joint injury, obesity , or lupus . How is arthritis diagnosed? To find out if you have arthritis, your health care provider may: Ask you about your medical history, including your symptoms.

Bimekizumab-bkzx injection is used to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (a skin disease in which red, scaly patches form on some areas of the body) in certain adults. It is also used to treat psoriatic arthritis (a condition that causes joint pain and swelling and scales on the skin) in adults. Bimekizumab-bkzx injection is also used to treat ankylosing spondylitis (a condition in which the body attacks the joints of the spine and other areas, causing pain and joint damage) in adults. It is also used to treat active non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (a condition in which the body attacks the joints of the spine and other areas causing pain and signs of swelling, but without changes seen on x-ray) in adults. Bimekizumab-bkzx is in a class of medications called monoclonal antibodies. It works by blocking the action of a certain natural substance in the body that causes the symptoms of psoriasis. How should this medicine be used? Bimekizumab-bkzx comes as a solution (liquid) in a prefilled syringe and as a prefilled autoinjector to inject subcutaneously (under the skin). To treat psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, or non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis, it is usually injected once every 4 weeks. question: How should wages be determined according to the State Government guidelines?
ground_truth: Wages shall be linked with the quantity of work done and paid according to the rural schedule of rates fixed after time and motion studies for different types of work and different seasons, revised periodically.
triseva_answer:
According to the State Government guidelines (as set out in the MGNREGA Act):
- The wage rate must be linked to the quantity of work performed and paid without gender bias, using the rural schedule of rates fixed after time‑and‑motion studies for different types of work and seasons, and revised periodically.
- The schedule of rates for unskilled labourers is set so that an adult working eight hours (including one hour of rest) earns a wage equal to the stipulated wage rate.
- The wage rate shall not be less than Rs 60 per day. If the Central Government has not fixed a rate for a particular area, the minimum wage fixed by the State Government under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 for agricultural labourers applies.

*   **Early Adopters:** Ve nayi technologies, seeds, ya farming practices ko adopt karne vale pehle log hote hain.
*   **Demonstration:** Ve model farmers ki tarah kaam karte hain, jisse doosre farmers ko nayi techniques ke benefits aur practical application samajhne mein help milti hai.
*   **Capacity Building:** Ve aksar apne communities mein doosre farmers ke liye training sessions aur knowledge-sharing activities lead karte hain.
*   **Feedback:** Ve scheme implementers ko nayi practices ki effectiveness aur challenges par valuable feedback provide karte hain.

It acts on the kidneys to help the body eliminate uric acid. Probenecid is also used to make certain antibiotics more effective by preventing the body from passing them in the urine. This medication is sometimes prescribed for other uses; ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. How should this medicine be used? Probenecid comes in a tablet to take by mouth. It usually is taken two times a day when prescribed for chronic gout or gouty arthritis and four times a day when prescribed with antibiotics to make them more effective. Follow the directions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist to explain any part you do not understand. Take probenecid exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more often than prescribed by your doctor. Probenecid may increase the frequency of gout attacks during the first 6 to 12 months that you take it, although it will eventually prevent them. Another drug, such as colchicine, may be prescribed to decrease this effect. What special precautions should I follow? Allopurinol is used to treat gout (a type of arthritis in which uric acid, a naturally occurring substance in the body, builds up in the joints and causes sudden attacks of redness, swelling, pain, and heat in one or more joints). Allopurinol is also used to treat high levels of uric acid that builds up in the blood as tumors break down in people with certain types of cancer who are being treated with chemotherapy medications. It is also used to treat kidney stones that have come back in people who have high levels of uric acid in their urine. Allopurinol is in a class of medications called xanthine oxidase inhibitors. It works by reducing the production of uric acid in the body. High levels of uric acid may cause gout attacks or kidney stones. Allopurinol is used to prevent gout attacks, not to treat them once they occur. How should this medicine be used? Allopurinol comes as a tablet to take by mouth. question: If a farmer receives a soil health card, what practical step should they take next?
ground_truth: The farmer should review the nutrient status information and follow the recommendations provided on the card regarding the appropriate dosage of nutrients to apply to their soil.
triseva_answer:
- Review the nutrient status and fertilizer recommendations printed on the Soil Health Card.
- Apply the recommended balanced fertilizers and soil amendments in the suggested quantities.
- Adjust crop selection according to the soil nutrient status indicated on the card.
- If any recommendation is unclear, consult the local agriculture officer or KVK for guidance.
triseva_contexts: Soil Health Card scheme provides farmers with soil nutrient status and fertilizer recommendations. question: Why is it important to see a doctor even if you don't have pain but notice other cancer symptoms?
ground_truth: Cancer may cause various symptoms but often doesn't cause pain. You shouldn't wait until you're having pain before seeing a healthcare provider, as early detection is important.
triseva_answer: Cancer may cause a variety of symptoms even when there is no pain. Because cancer often does not produce pain, waiting for pain can delay diagnosis and treatment. Early evaluation of symptoms such as blood in urine or stool, unexplained bleeding or bruising, a sore that does not heal, trouble swallowing, or a new or changing mole can lead to earlier detection and better outcomes. Seeing a doctor promptly when these signs appear—especially if they persist for a few weeks—allows for timely testing and intervention.
triseva_contexts: Blood in your urine (pee) or stool (poop) Bleeding or bruising for no known reason A sore that doesn't heal Trouble swallowing A new mole or a change to a mole you already have Cancer may cause various symptoms but often doesn't cause pain. Don't wait until you're having pain before seeing your health care provider. See your provider if you have symptoms that don't get better in a few weeks. How is cancer diagnosed? There is no single test that can diagnose cancer. The tests ordered are usually based on your symptoms. Your provider may: Ask about your medical history Ask about your family health history , including relatives who have had cancer Do a physical exam Do a screening test such as a mammogram , colonoscopy , or a Pap test Order blood tests or imaging tests To find out if you have cancer, your provider may order a biopsy . A biopsy is the procedure of removing and examining tissue, cells, or fluids from your body. What are the treatments for cancer? Treatment depends on the type of cancer and how advanced it is. Most treatment plans may include surgery, radiation , and/or chemotherapy . Some may involve hormone therapy, immunotherapy or other types of biological therapy, or stem cell transplantation . Can cancer be prevented? It's usually not possible to know exactly why cancer develops in some people but not others. There are some things that you can't control which may increase or decrease your risk

question: Official Gazette mein is Scheme ke liye jo notification publish hoti hai, uska legal significance kya hai?
ground_truth: Official Gazette mein publish hone waala notification ek formal aur legally binding announcement hai, jis se State Government is Act ke under employment guarantee Scheme ko establish aur modify karti hai.
triseva_answer:
The notification published in the Official Gazette is the official legal instrument that gives the scheme its enforceable status. Under the relevant Act, any rule, notification, or order issued under the scheme must be laid before Parliament and is deemed effective only after it is published in the Gazette. The Gazette publication therefore:
- Confers legal validity on the scheme’s provisions and any amendments.
- Serves as the official record that the Central Government has exercised its authority to create or modify the scheme.

question: What is the difference between inactive TB infection and TB disease?
ground_truth: Inactive TB infection means TB germs live in your body but don't make you sick, while TB disease (active TB) means the germs are growing and making you sick.
triseva_answer:
Inactive (latent) TB infection:
- TB germs are present in the body but are not active and do not make you sick.
- You have no symptoms and cannot spread TB to others.
- Treatment with antibiotics for three, four, six, or nine months is given to prevent future TB disease.

TB disease (active TB):
- TB germs are active, growing (multiplying) inside the body and cause illness.
- If the disease is in the lungs or throat, you can spread TB germs to other people.
- Symptoms may include general signs such as chills, fever, night sweats, weight loss, loss of appetite, and weakness or fatigue; lung‑specific symptoms include a cough lasting longer than three weeks, coughing up blood or sputum, and chest pain.
- Treatment with antibiotics for four, six, or nine months is required and can cure the disease if taken correctly.
- For TB disease in the lungs or throat, you need to stay home for a few weeks to avoid spreading it to others.

b2_answer:
### Inactive (latent) TB infection
- TB germs are present in the body but are not actively multiplying.
- The person has **no symptoms** and **cannot spread TB** to others.
- It can become active TB disease later if the immune system weakens (e.g., due to HIV, certain medications, or other conditions).
- Preventive treatment with antibiotics for several months (3, 4, 6, or 9 months) is recommended to stop progression to active disease.

### TB disease (active TB)
- TB germs are **active and multiplying**, causing illness.
- **Symptoms** may include:
  - Cough lasting longer than 3 weeks
  - Coughing up blood or sputum

*   **Contagious:** If the TB is in your lungs or throat, you can spread the germs to other people.
*   **Treatment:** It can almost always be cured with antibiotics, but it can be fatal if not treated properly.

The most common cause of anemia is not having enough iron . Your body needs iron to make hemoglobin. Hemoglobin is an iron-rich protein that gives the red color to blood. It carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body. Anemia has three main causes: blood loss, lack of red blood cell production, and high rates of red blood cell destruction. Conditions that may lead to anemia include: Heavy periods Pregnancy Ulcers Colon polyps or colon cancer Inherited disorders A diet that does not have enough iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 Blood disorders such as sickle cell anemia and thalassemia , or cancer Aplastic anemia , a condition that can be inherited or acquired G6PD deficiency , a metabolic disorder Anemia can make you feel tired, cold, dizzy, and irritable. You may be short of breath or have a headache. Your doctor will diagnose anemia with a physical exam and blood tests. Treatment depends on the kind of anemia you have.
