question: 2015 mein Soil Health Card Scheme launch karne ka kya significance tha?
ground_truth: Yeh scheme 2015 mein launch hui, usi saal International Year of Soils celebrate kiya gaya tha, isliye yeh ek timely initiative tha desh ke har farm holding ki nutrient status assess karne ke liye.
triseva_answer:
- Soil Health Card Scheme ko 19 February 2015 ko Suratgarh, Rajasthan mein Prime Minister Narendra Modi ne “Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa.” (Healthy Earth, Green Farm) ke slogan ke saath launch kiya tha.
- Yeh launch International Year of Soils 2015 ke saath hua tha, jo soil health par global focus ko highlight karta hai.
- Iss scheme ko introduce kiya gaya tha taaki State Governments ko desh ke sabhi farmers ko Soil Health Cards issue karne mein assist kiya ja sake, jo unki soil ke nutrient status aur soil health aur fertility improve karne ke liye appropriate nutrient dosages ki recommendations provide karte hain.
- Iska objective har do saal mein Soil Health Cards issue karna hai taaki fertilization practices mein nutrient deficiencies ko address karne ke liye ek basis provide kiya ja sake.
- Cards farmers ko yeh identify karne mein help karte hain ki unki soil mein kaun se nutrients ki kami hai, suitable crops select karne mein, aur sahi fertilizers apply karne mein, jisse soil fertility aur crop yields improve hoti hain.
- Yeh ensure karna ki vahi person ek farmer ke liye soil analysis kare, scheme ki effectiveness ko enhance karta hai.
- Yeh initiative integrated nutrient management aur “Sujalam, Suphalam” (well‑watered, fertile) land achieve karne ke vision ko support karta hai, jisse national food‑security goals mein contribute milta hai.

Khet Haraa.” – Healthy Earth. Green Farm. -Prime Minister Narendra Modi 1. Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. On the occasion, the Prime Minister gave the slogan: "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." - Healthy Earth, Green Farm. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. The International Year of Soils [5] was celebrated in 2015; the same year, the unique programme of soil health card was launched in India to assess the nutrient status of every farm holding in the country. 2. Objective s [6] : To issue soil health cards [7] every two years to all farmers, so as to provide a basis to address nutrient deficiencies in fertilization practices. *   **National Vision:** Prime Minister Narendra Modi ne ise ek "Sujalam, Suphalam" (well-watered, fertile land) vaali zameen ke sapne ko poora karne ki taraf ek step ke roop mein pesh kiya. Unhone "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." (Healthy Earth, Green Farm) ka slogan diya, jo soil health ko seedhe nation ki agricultural prosperity se jodta hai.
*   **Core Objective:** Iska primary goal sabhi farmers ko soil health cards issue karna tha taaki unhein unki soil ke nutrient status ke baare mein information mil sake aur soil health aur fertility improve karne ke liye appropriate nutrients apply karne ki recommendations mil saken.

However, based on general knowledge of Indian government schemes, a 5-year eligibility freeze is often implemented to ensure benefits reach new, eligible candidates over time. Such a freeze might be bypassed in exceptional circumstances, such as:

*   **Natural Calamities:** In the event of a severe drought, flood, or other natural disaster, the freeze might be lifted to provide immediate relief to affected farmers.
*   **Policy Amendments:** If the government amends the scheme to include a new category of beneficiaries (e.g., women farmers or landless laborers), the freeze might be bypassed for this new group.
*   **Court Orders:** A directive from a court or tribunal might require the government to include specific individuals or groups, overriding the freeze.
*   **Technical Errors:** If a large number of eligible beneficiaries were wrongly excluded due to a technical error in the database, the freeze might be temporarily bypassed to correct the data.

question: Who is responsible for issuing soil health cards to farmers under this scheme?
ground_truth: State Governments are responsible for issuing soil health cards to all farmers in the country under this scheme.
triseva_answer: State Governments are responsible for issuing soil health cards to farmers under the Soil Health Card Scheme.
triseva_contexts: to cover as many as all farmers under the scheme. The scheme will cover all the parts of the country. In the form of soil card, the farmers will get a report and this report will contain all the details about the soil of their particular farm. A farm will get the soil card once in every three years. 4. Benefits of the Soil Health Card Scheme [12] Under t he scheme, soil is tested and a formatted report provided to farmers. So, they can decide which crops they s hould cultivate and which ones they should skip. The authorities test the soil on a regular basis and they provide a report to farmers. So, farmers need not worry if the nature of the soil changes due to certain factors. Also, they always have updated data about their soil. The work of the government does not stop at listing down measures required to improve the quality of the soil. In fact, Government also employs experts to help the farmers in carrying out the corrective measures. Farmers get a proper soil health record, thanks to the scheme. Farmers can also study the soil management practices and plan the future of their crops and land accordingly. Generally, in government schemes, the person carrying out the study for a particular farmer gets changed, but in the Soil Health Card Scheme, the government is paying attention to see to it that the same person carries out soil analysis for a farmer. Khet Haraa.” – Healthy Earth. Green Farm. -Prime Minister Narendra Modi 1. Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. On the occasion, the Prime Minister gave the slogan: "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." - Healthy Earth, Green Farm. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. The International Year of Soils [5] was celebrated in 2015; the same year, the unique programme of soil health card was launched in India to assess the nutrient status of every farm holding in the country. 2. Objective s [6] : To issue soil health cards [7] every two years to all farmers, so as to provide a basis to address nutrient deficiencies in fertilization practices. To strengthen functioning of Soil Testing

question: मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड योजना किसने शुरू की?
ground_truth: प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड योजना की शुरुआत की।
triseva_answer: मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड योजना का शुभारंभ प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी द्वारा 19 फरवरी 2015 को सूरतगढ़, राजस्थान में किया गया था।
triseva_contexts: वेबसाइटें तथ्यों की जांच के बारे में तथ्यों की जांच के लिए जमा करें संख्याओं में तथ्य की जाँच Soil Health Card (Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare) January 17, 2022 “Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa.” – Healthy Earth. Green Farm. -Prime Minister Narendra Modi 1. Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. On the occasion, the Prime Minister gave the slogan: "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." - Healthy Earth, Green Farm. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. The International Year of Soils [5] was celebrated in 2015; the same year, the unique programme of soil health card was launched in India to assess the nutrient status of every farm holding in the country. 2. Objective s [6] : To issue soil health cards [7] every two years to all farmers, so as to provide a basis to address nutrient deficiencies in fertilization practices. To strengthen functioning of Soil Testing

ground_truth: The statement mentions penal provisions for failure to provide information as per law, though specific penalties are not detailed in this document.
triseva_answer:
Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, Section 19 provides that a Central or State Public Information Officer who fails to receive an application or furnish information within the prescribed time may be penalised **Rs 250 per day**, with the total penalty **not exceeding Rs 25,000**. If the officer persistently fails to receive an application, malafidely denies a request, gives incorrect/incomplete/misleading information, destroys requested information, or otherwise obstructs disclosure, the Central or State Information Commission may **recommend disciplinary action** against the officer under the applicable service rules.  

Under the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016:
- **Section 41 – Penalty for non‑compliance with intimation requirements**: an enrolling agency or requesting entity that fails to comply with the intimation provisions is liable to a penalty **up to Rs 1 lakh**; for a company, the penalty may extend to **Rs 10 lakh**.
- **Section 42 – General penalty**: any person who commits an offence under the Act for which no specific penalty is prescribed is punishable with **imprisonment up to three years** or a **fine up to Rs 25,000** (or up to Rs 1 lakh for a company), or both.

Source: Right to Information Act, 2005 (Section 19) and Aadhaar Act, 2016 (Sections 41 and 42).

question: What economic and environmental advantages does the Soil Health Card scheme offer to Indian farmers?
ground_truth: The scheme offers economic advantages through reduced fertilizer costs (8-10 per cent decrease) and increased crop yields (5-6 per cent increase), while providing environmental benefits by reducing chemical fertilizer application.
triseva_answer:
### Economic Advantages
- **Crop selection guidance:** The card tells farmers which crops are suitable for their soil and which ones to avoid, helping them invest in the right crops.
- **Targeted fertilizer use:** It provides specific fertilizer recommendations and quantities, reducing unnecessary fertilizer purchases and lowering input costs.
- **Improved planning:** Farmers receive a proper soil health record and can study soil management practices to plan future crops and land use for better yields.
- **Regular updates:** Soil is tested and a new card is issued every three years, giving farmers up‑to‑date data for informed decisions.

### Environmental Advantages
- **Soil health improvement:** The card indicates the nutrient status of the soil and the amendments needed, enabling corrective measures that enhance soil quality.
- **Balanced nutrient management:** By recommending the exact dosage of nutrients, the scheme helps prevent over‑application of fertilizers, protecting soil and surrounding ecosystems.
- **Sustainable farming:** Access to expert advice and soil management practices encourages practices that maintain long‑term soil fertility and health.

*   **Long-Term Planning and Risk Management:** Farmers receive a proper soil health record that is updated every three years. This allows them to plan for the future, manage changes in soil quality, and make more stable economic decisions for their land.

*   **Improved Soil Health:** The scheme's core function is to test the soil and provide recommendations for corrective measures and soil amendments. This helps farmers actively improve the quality and fertility of their soil over time.
*   **Reduced Chemical Overuse:** By advising farmers on the precise quantity of fertilizers needed, the scheme helps prevent the overuse of chemical inputs. This reduces the risk of fertilizer runoff polluting water sources and contributes to more sustainable agricultural practices.

*   **Improved Soil Health:** The primary objective is to improve the "health and its fertility" of the soil, moving towards the goal of a "Healthy Earth, Green Farm."
*   **Reduced Fertilizer Pollution:** By recommending the "appropriate dosage of nutrients," the scheme helps prevent the overuse of fertilizers, which can reduce chemical runoff into water bodies and soil contamination.
*   **Promotion of Sustainable Practices:** The scheme aims to popularize "balance and integrated nutrient management practices," which are more sustainable and environmentally friendly than conventional farming methods.
*   **Conservation of Resources:** Enhancing nutrient use efficiency means that the finite resources used to produce fertilizers are conserved.

*   **Wear a surgical mask** when around other people.

Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease that usually attacks the lungs. But it can also attack other parts of the body, including the kidneys, spine, and brain. Not everyone infected with TB bacteria (germs) becomes sick. So, there are two types of TB conditions: Inactive (latent) TB infection , where the TB germs live in your body but don't make you sick. TB disease (active TB) where you get sick from the TB germs. TB disease can almost always be cured with antibiotics . But if it's not treated properly, it can be fatal. TB is found in the U.S., but it is more common in certain other countries. What causes tuberculosis (TB)? TB is caused by bacteria (germs) called Mycobacterium tuberculosis . The germs spread from person to person through the air. People who have TB disease in their throat or lungs spread the germs in the air when they cough, sneeze, talk, or sing. That means the medicine may stop working and your TB may become hard to cure. For inactive TB infections , you need to take medicines for three, four, six, or nine months, depending on the treatment plan. Treatment helps make sure you don't get TB disease in the future. For active TB disease , you usually need to take medicines for four, six, or nine months, depending on the treatment plan. Treatment will almost always cure you if you take your pills the right way. For drug-resistant TB disease, which means that the TB germs are resistant to certain TB medicines, you will need to take special medicines. Treatment may take a long time, sometimes months or years. Wages must be linked to the quantity of work performed **without any gender bias**, ensuring that men and women receive equal pay for equal work. The MGNREGA Act explicitly requires that the State Government link wages, without gender bias, to the amount of work done and to pay according to the rural schedule of rates fixed after time‑and‑motion studies. It also provides for a separate schedule of rates for women, the elderly, and persons with disabilities to promote their participation, but the core principle remains gender‑neutral wage payment based on work done.

Source: MGNREGA Act – Section on wage payment (link wages without gender bias to quantity of work done).

question: मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्डों का उपयोग करने से रासायनिक उर्वरक का उपयोग कम करने में कैसे मदद मिलेगी?
ground_truth: मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड मृदा पोषक तत्वों की उपलब्धता के बारे में जानकारी प्रदान करते हैं, जिससे किसान अपनी मिट्टी की विशिष्ट आवश्यकताओं के आधार पर केवल आवश्यक मात्रा में उर्वरक लागू कर सकते हैं, जिससे अत्यधिक रासायनिक उर्वरक उपयोग कम हो जाता है।
triseva_answer: मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड किसानों को उनके खेत की मिट्टी की पोषक तत्वों की स्थिति (pH, कार्बनिक कार्बन, N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B) और सटीक उर्वरक अनुशंसाएँ प्रदान करते हैं। इन अनुशंसाओं का पालन करके, किसान केवल उन्हीं पोषक तत्वों का उपयोग करते हैं जिनकी आवश्यकता होती है, जिससे यूरिया जैसे रासायनिक उर्वरकों के अत्यधिक उपयोग से बचा जा सकता है। मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड योजना के अंतर्गत किए गए एक अध्ययन में यह पाया गया कि कार्ड की सलाह के अनुसार उर्वरकों का उपयोग करने से रासायनिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग में 8-10% की कमी आई है, जबकि फसल की पैदावार में 5-6% की वृद्धि हुई है।

Khet Haraa.” – Healthy Earth. Green Farm. -Prime Minister Narendra Modi 1. Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. On the occasion, the Prime Minister gave the slogan: "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." - Healthy Earth, Green Farm. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. The International Year of Soils [5] was celebrated in 2015; the same year, the unique programme of soil health card was launched in India to assess the nutrient status of every farm holding in the country. 2. Objective s [6] : To issue soil health cards [7] every two years to all farmers, so as to provide a basis to address nutrient deficiencies in fertilization practices. To strengthen functioning of Soil Testing

Soil Health Card scheme provides farmers with soil nutrient status and fertilizer recommendations. Key parameters include pH, organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and micronutrients. Farmers should apply balanced fertilizers based on SHC advice rather than using only urea, to improve yield and soil health.

Study on Impact of Soil Health Card Scheme by National Productivity Council [21] National Productivity Council (NPC) [22] carried out a study on ‘Soil Testing Infrastructure for Faster Delivery of Soil Health Card in India’ and submitted its report in February 2017. The study was conducted in 76 districts in 19 States covering 170 soil testing labs and 1700 farmers. Some of the findings of the study are as follows: More than 90 per cent of farmers surveyed informed that they have not got their soil tested before the implementation of this scheme. 92 per cent farmers reported not having used balanced fertilizer and micro nutrients in absence of information related to availability of nutrients in their soil. As a result of application of fertilizer and micro-nutrients as per the recommendations on the Soil Health Cards, it was reported that there has been a decrease of use of chemical fertilizer application in the range of 8-10 per cent. Overall increase in the yield of crops to the tune of 5-6 per cent was reported due to application of fertilizer and micro nutrients as per recommendations available in the Soil Health Cards. 9. यह प्रक्रिया निम्नलिखित रूप में कार्य करती है:

1. **लक्षित अनुप्रयोग (टारगेटेड एप्लीकेशन):** मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड किसानों को उनके मृदा में पोषक तत्वों की कमी के बारे में सूचित करता है। इससे उन्हें केवल यूरिया जैसे उर्वरकों के सामान्य प्रयोग के स्थान पर, मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड में दी गई सिफारिशों के आधार पर संतुलित उर्वरकों और सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्वों का उपयोग करने की सुविधा मिलती है।
2. **अति-उर्वरक प्रयोग में कमी:** मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड से पूर्व, 90% से अधिक किसानों ने अपने मृदा का परीक्षण नहीं कराया था और 92% किसानों ने संतुलित उर्वरकों का उपयोग नहीं किया था, क्योंकि उनके पास अपने मृदा में पोषक तत्वों की उपलब्धता के संबंध में जानकारी का अभाव था। मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड की सिफारिशों का पालन करके, किसान केवल उन्हीं पोषक तत्वों का प्रयोग कर सकते हैं जिनकी उनकी मृदा को आवश्यकता है, जिससे रासायनिक उर्वरकों के समग्र उपयोग में कमी आती है।

राष्ट्रीय उत्पादकता परिषद (नेशनल प्रोडक्टिविटी काउंसिल) द्वारा किए गए एक अध्ययन में यह पाया गया कि मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड की सिफारिशों के अनुसार उर्वरकों के प्रयोग के परिणामस्वरूप रासायनिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग में 8-10% की कमी आई है।

Khet Haraa.” – Healthy Earth. Green Farm. -Prime Minister Narendra Modi 1. Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. On the occasion, the Prime Minister gave the slogan: "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." - Healthy Earth, Green Farm. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. The International Year of Soils [5] was celebrated in 2015; the same year, the unique programme of soil health card was launched in India to assess the nutrient status of every farm holding in the country. 2. Objective s [6] : To issue soil health cards [7] every two years to all farmers, so as to provide a basis to address nutrient deficiencies in fertilization practices. To strengthen functioning of Soil Testing

Soil Health Card scheme provides farmers with soil nutrient status and fertilizer recommendations. Key parameters include pH, organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and micronutrients. Farmers should apply balanced fertilizers based on SHC advice rather than using only urea, to improve yield and soil health.

Study on Impact of Soil Health Card Scheme by National Productivity Council [21] National Productivity Council (NPC) [22] carried out a study on ‘Soil Testing Infrastructure for Faster Delivery of Soil Health Card in India’ and submitted its report in February 2017. The study was conducted in 76 districts in 19 States covering 170 soil testing labs and 1700 farmers. Some of the findings of the study are as follows: More than 90 per cent of farmers surveyed informed that they have not got their soil tested before the implementation of this scheme. 92 per cent farmers reported not having used balanced fertilizer and micro nutrients in absence of information related to availability of nutrients in their soil. As a result of application of fertilizer and micro-nutrients as per the recommendations on the Soil Health Cards, it was reported that there has been a decrease of use of chemical fertilizer application in the range of 8-10 per cent. Overall increase in the yield of crops to the tune of 5-6 per cent was reported due to application of fertilizer and micro nutrients as per recommendations available in the Soil Health Cards. 9. मैं दिए गए दस्तावेजों में इस प्रश्न का उत्तर खोजने में असमर्थ हूँ।

हालाँकि, सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर: मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड किसानों को उनके खेतों की मिट्टी की पोषक संरचना के बारे में विशिष्ट जानकारी प्रदान करके रासायनिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग को कम करने में सहायता करते हैं।

यह प्रक्रिया इस प्रकार कार्य करती है:

1.  **मृदा परीक्षण:** किसान की मिट्टी का परीक्षण किया जाता है ताकि उसमें नाइट्रोजन (N), फास्फोरस (P), पोटेशियम (K) और अन्य आवश्यक सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्वों की मात्रा का विश्लेषण किया जा सके।
2.  **सिफारिशें:** मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड इस विश्लेषण के परिणामों को संकलित करता है और किसान को इस बात की स्पष्ट सिफारिश प्रदान करता है कि फसल की उपज को अनुकूलित करने के लिए किन पोषक तत्वों की आवश्यकता है और कितनी मात्रा में आवश्यकता है।
3.  **लक्षित अनुप्रयोग:** सामान्य रूप से रासायनिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग के बजाय, किसान अब केवल उन्हीं पोषक तत्वों का उपयोग कर सकते हैं जिनकी उनके खेत में कमी है। इससे उन पोषक तत्वों के अत्यधिक उपयोग को रोका जा सकता है जो पहले से ही पर्याप्त मात्रा में मौजूद हैं।
4.  **लागत और पर्यावरणीय लाभ:** अनावश्यक उर्वरकों के उपयोग को रोककर, किसान उर्वरकों पर होने वाले अपने खर्च को कम करते हैं। यह अत्यधिक उर्वरक के बहाव के कारण होने वाले पर्यावरणीय नुकसान को भी कम करता है, जो जल स्रोतों को प्रदूषित कर सकता है और ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन में योगदान दे सकता है।

question: If you seized documents from a person and needed to return them after twenty days, what preliminary step must be completed?
ground_truth: Certified copies or extracts of the documents must be taken in the prescribed manner before the original documents are returned.
triseva_answer: Before returning seized documents after twenty days, the authority must first obtain certified copies or extracts of the documents from the person from whom they were seized, as required by law. Source: Legal provision stating that documents shall be returned within twenty days "after copies thereof or extracts therefrom certified by that person, in such manner as may be prescribed, have been taken."

ground_truth: Haan, carcinoma sabse common type of cancer hai. Ye bante hain epithelial cells se, jo cells hain jo aapke body ki andar aur bahar ki surfaces ko cover karte hain.
triseva_answer: Yes, carcinoma is the most common type of cancer. It originates from epithelial cells, which are the cells that line the internal and external surfaces of the body.

question: What does the official India.gov.in website indicate about the Soil Health Card scheme?
ground_truth: The India.gov.in website features a spotlight section on the Soil Health Card scheme, providing information about this government initiative to farmers.
triseva_answer:
According to the official India.gov.in spotlight on the Soil Health Card scheme:
- The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan, with the slogan "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." – Healthy Earth, Green Farm.
- Its objective is to issue a Soil Health Card to every farmer in the country, providing a report on the nutrient status of the soil and recommendations on the appropriate dosage of nutrients/fertilizers to improve soil health and fertility.
- The scheme aims to cover all parts of the country, and each farm receives a Soil Health Card once every three years (some sources note a two‑year interval for issuing cards).
- Benefits include helping farmers decide which crops to cultivate, which to avoid, and which fertilizers to apply, thereby supporting better soil management and increased productivity.
- The government has also strengthened soil testing infrastructure, sanctioning over 11,500 new labs (static, mobile, mini‑labs, and village‑level labs) and conducting numerous demonstrations, trainings, and farmer melas to promote proper fertilizer use.

According to the official India.gov.in spotlight page on the Soil Health Card scheme:

- **Launch**: The scheme was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan, with the slogan "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." – Healthy Earth, Green Farm.
- **Objective**: To issue Soil Health Cards to all farmers every two years, providing a basis to correct nutrient deficiencies in fertilisation practices.
- **Coverage**: The programme is intended to cover every part of the country and all farmers.
- **What the card provides**: A report detailing the nutrient status of the farmer’s soil and recommendations on the appropriate dosage of nutrients to improve soil health and fertility.
- **Benefits to farmers**: Enables informed decisions on which crops to cultivate and which fertilizers to apply; ensures regular, updated soil data; and offers expert guidance for corrective measures.
- **Implementation milestones**:
  - **Cards issued**: Cycle I (2015‑17) – 107,348,416 cards; Cycle II (2017‑19) – 119,773,040 cards.
  - **Laboratory infrastructure**: 11,531 new soil‑testing labs (491 static, 107 mobile, 8,811 minilabs, 2,122 village‑level labs) and strengthening of 829 existing labs.
  - **Extension activities**: Since 2015, about 6.04 lakh demonstrations, 36,928 farmer trainings, and 7,425 farmer melas have been organized, involving Krishi Sakhis, Pasu Sakhis and other village‑level workers.
- **Financial progress**: Funds released from 2014‑15 to 2019‑20 total Rs 751.42 crore.

These points reflect the information presented on the India.gov.in website regarding the Soil Health Card scheme.

*   **Recommendations:** Based on the soil analysis, the card provides specific, scientific recommendations on the dosage of nutrients needed, the types and quantities of fertilizers to apply, and any necessary soil amendments.
*   **Benefits:** It helps farmers make informed decisions about which crops to cultivate, how to manage their land, and how to apply fertilizers in a balanced way, leading to optimal yields and cost savings.
*   **Coverage:** The scheme aims to cover all farmers across the country, with soil cards being issued to each farmer's holding every three years.

question: Which medical conditions increase the risk of developing kidney disease?
ground_truth: Having diabetes, high blood pressure, or a close family member with kidney disease increases the risk of kidney disease.

- Diabetes
- High blood pressure (hypertension)
- Genetic problems or a close family member with kidney disease
- Injuries or exposure to certain medicines (as noted as general causes)

They are near the middle of your back, just below the rib cage. Inside each kidney there are about a million tiny structures called nephrons. They filter your blood. They remove wastes and extra water, which become urine. The urine flows through tubes called ureters. It goes to your bladder, which stores the urine until you go to the bathroom. Most kidney diseases attack the nephrons. This damage may leave kidneys unable to remove wastes. Causes can include genetic problems, injuries, or medicines. You have a higher risk of kidney disease if you have diabetes , high blood pressure , or a close family member with kidney disease. Chronic kidney disease damages the nephrons slowly over several years. Other kidney problems include: Cancer Cysts Stones Infections Your doctor can do blood and urine tests to check if you have kidney disease. The risk for developing PTLD is higher if you have not been exposed to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV, a virus causing mononucleosis or ''mono'') or if you have cytomegalovirus infection (CMV) or have received other treatments that lower amounts of T lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell) in your blood. Your doctor will order certain lab tests to check for these conditions before you begin treatment with this medication. If you have not been exposed to Epstein-Barr virus, your doctor will probably not give you belatacept injection. If you experience any of the following symptoms after receiving belatacept injection, call your doctor immediately: confusion, difficulty thinking, problems with memory, changes in mood or your usual behavior, changes in the way you walk or talk, decreased strength or weakness on one side of your body, or changes in vision. Receiving belatacept injection may also increase the risk for developing cancers, including skin cancer, and serious infections, including tuberculosis (TB, a bacterial lung infection) and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML, a rare, serious brain infection). question: When was the Soil Health Card scheme launched by the Prime Minister?
ground_truth: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February, 2015.
triseva_answer: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan.

Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. b3_contexts: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) provides income support of Rs 6000 per year to farmer families in three equal instalments. Eligibility: small and marginal farmer families with combined landholding up to 2 hectares. Exclusions: institutional landholders, farmer families holding constitutional posts, serving or retired government employees with monthly pension above Rs 10000, income tax payers.

Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) provides health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation. Eligible families are based on SECC 2011 database. Documents required: Aadhaar card, ration card, income certificate. Over 1700 treatment packages covered. No premium to be paid by beneficiary.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) aims to provide affordable housing for all. Urban component provides interest subsidy on home loans. EWS category (income up to Rs 3 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. LIG category (income Rs 3-6 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. MIG-I (income Rs 6-12 lakh): 4% subsidy. MIG-II (income Rs 12-18 lakh): 3% subsidy.

question: Explain why an Indian woman of Hispanic/Latino ethnicity and age 36 who is overweight should be concerned about developing Type 2 diabetes.

question: सार्वजनिक पहुँच सुनिश्चित करने के लिए जानकारी का प्रसार करते समय किन कारकों पर विचार किया जाना चाहिए?
ground_truth: सार्वजनिक प्राधिकरणों को लागत प्रभावशीलता, स्थानीय भाषा और उस स्थानीय क्षेत्र में संचार के सबसे प्रभावी तरीके पर विचार करना चाहिए ताकि जानकारी यथासंभव आसानी से उपलब्ध हो।
triseva_answer:
सार्वजनिक पहुँच सुनिश्चित करने के लिए जानकारी प्रसारित करते समय, निम्नलिखित कारकों पर विचार किया जाना चाहिए:

- **लागत-प्रभावशीलता**: प्रसार ऐसी लागत पर किया जाना चाहिए जो उचित और वहनीय हो।
- **स्थानीय भाषा**: जानकारी स्थानीय स्तर पर बोली जाने वाली भाषा (भाषाओं) में प्रदान की जानी चाहिए ताकि इसे समझा जा सके।
- **सबसे प्रभावी संचार विधि**: उस माध्यम का उपयोग करें जो विशिष्ट क्षेत्र में सबसे अच्छा काम करता है (जैसे, रेडियो, सामुदायिक बैठकें, स्थानीय समाचार पत्र)।
- **इलेक्ट्रॉनिक प्रारूप**: जहाँ संभव हो, आसान पहुँच की सुविधा के लिए जानकारी इलेक्ट्रॉनिक प्रारूप में प्रदान करें।
- **व्यापक प्रसार**: नोटिस बोर्ड, समाचार पत्रों, सार्वजनिक घोषणाओं, मीडिया प्रसारण और इंटरनेट जैसे कई माध्यमों से जानकारी को व्यापक रूप से ज्ञात कराएं।
- **पहुँच में सुगमता**: प्रसार का स्वरूप और तरीका जनता के लिए आसानी से सुलभ होना चाहिए।
- **नियमित अंतराल**: नागरिकों को सूचना का अधिकार (RTI) अधिनियम के तहत इसकी मांग करने की आवश्यकता को कम करने के लिए नियमित अंतराल पर सक्रिय रूप से जानकारी प्रदान करें।

However, based on general knowledge, here are some key factors to consider when disseminating information to ensure public accessibility:

*   **Language and Simplicity:** Use simple, clear language and avoid jargon. Information should be available in multiple local languages to cater to a diverse population.
*   **Choice of Medium:** Utilize a variety of communication channels to reach different demographics. This can include traditional media (TV, radio, newspapers), digital platforms (social media, websites), community outreach (meetings, local announcements), and SMS alerts.
*   **Target Audience:** Tailor the message and the channel to the specific target audience. For example, information for farmers might be best disseminated through agricultural offices or local cooperatives, while information for urban youth might be more effective on social media.
*   **Accessibility for People with Disabilities:** Ensure that information is accessible to individuals with disabilities. This could involve providing content in Braille, using sign language in videos, or ensuring websites are compatible with screen readers.
*   **Clarity and Actionability:** The information should be easy to understand and should clearly state the next steps a person needs to take, such as which documents are required and where to apply.
*   **Proactive Communication:** Don't just wait for people to seek information. Proactively disseminate details about schemes and services through various channels.
*   **Feedback Mechanism:** Establish a clear and accessible way for the public to ask questions, seek clarification, or provide feedback. This could be a helpline number, a dedicated email address, or a physical help desk.

Eligible families are based on SECC 2011 database. Documents required: Aadhaar card, ration card, income certificate. Over 1700 treatment packages covered. No premium to be paid by beneficiary.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) aims to provide affordable housing for all. Urban component provides interest subsidy on home loans. EWS category (income up to Rs 3 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. LIG category (income Rs 3-6 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. MIG-I (income Rs 6-12 lakh): 4% subsidy. MIG-II (income Rs 12-18 lakh): 3% subsidy.

question: What is the primary purpose of a Soil Health Card?
ground_truth: The Soil Health Card provides farmers with a report containing details about their farm's soil, including fertilizer recommendations and soil amendments needed to realize optimal yields.
triseva_answer: The primary purpose of a Soil Health Card is to provide farmers with a detailed report of their soil’s nutrient status (including macro‑ and micronutrients, pH, organic carbon, etc.) and specific fertilizer or soil amendment recommendations, enabling balanced nutrient management to improve crop yields and soil health.

*   Plan soil management practices for their land.
*   Improve their soil health and crop yield.

Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. On the occasion, the Prime Minister gave the slogan: "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." - Healthy Earth, Green Farm. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. The International Year of Soils [5] was celebrated in 2015; the same year, the unique programme of soil health card was launched in India to assess the nutrient status of every farm holding in the country. 2. question: What is the main symptom of dengue infection?
ground_truth: The main symptom is a high fever, along with nausea, vomiting, rash, and aches and pains (especially eye pain behind the eyes and pain in muscles, joints, or bones).
triseva_answer:
The primary symptom of dengue infection is a **high fever**. Other common symptoms include:
- Nausea and vomiting
- Rash
- Aches and pains (especially behind the eyes, and in muscles, joints, or bones)

Dengue is a viral infection . It can be caused by four related viruses. You can get it if an infected mosquito bites you. It is common in warm, wet areas of the world. Although rare, it can be found in some parts of the United States. Outbreaks are more common during rainy seasons. How does dengue spread? Dengue spreads to people through the bite of an infected mosquito. It does not spread directly from person to person. However, the infection can be passed to the baby during pregnancy. In rare cases, it can spread through a blood transfusion , organ transplant , or needle stick injury (an accidental injury from a used needle).. What are the symptoms of dengue and severe dengue? About one in four people infected with dengue will get sick. For those who do get sick, the infection can be mild or severe. The symptoms of dengue include: A high fever Nausea and vomiting Rash Aches and pains (eye pain, usually behind the eyes, and pain in the muscles, joints, or bones) The symptoms usually last two to seven days. Severe dengue is a serious form of the illness. About 1 in

the eyes, and pain in the muscles, joints, or bones) The symptoms usually last two to seven days. Severe dengue is a serious form of the illness. About 1 in 20 people who get sick with dengue will develop severe dengue. It can cause shock , internal bleeding, and even death. People are more likely to develop severe dengue if they have had dengue before, are pregnant, or are infants. Watch for signs and symptoms of severe dengue. Warning signs usually begin about 24 - 48 hours after your fever has gone away. If you or your family member have these signs, get immediate medical care: Severe abdominal (belly) pain and tenderness Vomiting at least 3 times in 24 hours Bleeding from the nose or gums Vomiting blood, or blood in the stool (poop) Feeling tired, restless, or irritable How is dengue diagnosed? There is a blood test which can show if you have been infected with dengue. What are the treatments for dengue? There is no specific medicine to treat dengue. Most people will get better after about a week. But if you think you might have dengue: See a health care provider and mention any recent travel. Rest as much as possible. Take acetaminophen to control fever and relieve pain. But do not take aspirin or ibuprofen. Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration . Severe dengue often requires care at a hospital. plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration . Severe dengue often requires care at a hospital. Can dengue be prevented? In the United States, a dengue vaccine is approved for children who are ages 9 - 16. They must also have previously had dengue and live in areas where dengue is common. You can also help prevent dengue by avoiding mosquito bites: Wear insect repellent with DEET or another U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)-registered insect repellent. question: Infer the purpose of requiring SMS notification to beneficiaries and crediting accounts periodically through the scheme.
ground_truth: The SMS notification and periodic crediting system ensures transparency, accountability, and timely communication with beneficiaries, reducing delays and providing real-time updates on fund transfers.
triseva_answer:
The PM‑Kisan (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi) scheme mandates SMS notifications and periodic crediting of benefits to achieve the following purposes:
- **Informing beneficiaries**: A system‑generated SMS alerts the farmer that the amount has been credited to his/her bank account, ensuring the beneficiary knows when the benefit is received.
- **Transparency and accountability**: Periodic crediting combined with SMS alerts creates a clear audit trail, allowing both the beneficiary and the administering authority to verify that payments are made as scheduled.
- **Facilitating grievance redressal**: If a transaction fails or the beneficiary does not receive the amount, the SMS record serves as evidence for the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DAC&FW) and State/UT governments to investigate and resolve complaints promptly.
- **Detecting and correcting errors**: The banking system reports successful and failed transactions back to DAC&FW, enabling timely identification of discrepancies and reprocessing of failed payments.
- **Ensuring timely receipt of benefits**: Regular crediting cycles (e.g., per trimester) guarantee that eligible farmers receive the income support on a predictable schedule, reducing delays and uncertainty.

Source: PM‑Kisan Operational Guidelines (SMS intimation and periodic credit provisions).

The context indicates that SMS notification serves several key purposes:

*   **Direct Intimation and Transparency:** The documents state that "Beneficiary would be intimated about credit of amount to his account by Short Messaging Service (SMS)." This ensures the beneficiary receives direct and immediate confirmation that the funds have been credited, which is part of a larger system to ensure "greater transparency and information."
*   **Grievance Redressal:** The scheme includes a process for addressing "complaints / grievances." The SMS notification acts as a formal trigger for this process. If a beneficiary is notified but does not receive the funds or has an issue, they have a clear point of reference to raise a complaint.

**Purpose of Periodic Crediting:**

The provided documents state that "The beneficiary account is to be credited periodically after the issuance of the Sanction Order," but they do not explicitly state the reason for this periodic nature.

However, based on general knowledge of such government schemes, the purpose of periodic crediting is typically to:

*   Provide beneficiaries with a regular and predictable income stream to manage their financial needs, such as purchasing agricultural inputs or covering household expenses.
*   Allow the administering bodies and banks to process and transfer funds in an organized and efficient manner, handling large volumes of transactions in batches.

question: What advantage does knowing soil nutrient status provide to a farmer?
ground_truth: Knowing soil nutrient status allows farmers to make informed decisions about crop selection, apply appropriate fertilizer dosages, and undertake necessary soil amendments to maximize yields.
triseva_answer:
Knowing the soil nutrient status provides the following advantages to a farmer:
- Helps decide which crops to cultivate and which to avoid based on soil suitability.
- Provides specific fertilizer recommendations and the exact dosage of each nutrient needed.
- Advises on the types and quantities of fertilizers to apply, as well as any required soil amendments.
- Enables balanced and integrated nutrient management, improving both yield and long‑term soil health.
- Allows the farmer to plan future cropping and land‑management practices with updated, reliable soil data.

question: How does dengue spread from one person to another?
ground_truth: Dengue does not spread directly from person to person. It spreads through the bite of an infected mosquito. However, it can be passed to a baby during pregnancy or rarely through blood transfusion, organ transplant, or needle stick injury.
triseva_answer:
Dengue is transmitted to people primarily through the bite of an infected mosquito. It does not spread directly from person to person. However, in rare cases the virus can be passed from one individual to another through:
- Mother to baby during pregnancy
- Blood transfusion
- Organ transplant
- Needle‑stick injury (accidental puncture with a used needle)

प्रदत्त दस्तावेज़ों में मुझे इस बात की जानकारी नहीं मिली कि किसान संतुलित उर्वरकों का उपयोग क्यों नहीं कर रहे थे।

सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर, किसानों द्वारा संतुलित उर्वरकों का उपयोग न करने के मुख्य कारण निम्नलिखित हो सकते हैं:

*   **लागत:** संतुलित उर्वरक, जिनमें नाइट्रोजन (N), फास्फोरस (P) और पोटेशियम (K) का सही अनुपात होता है, वे एकल-पोषक तत्वों वाले उर्वरकों की तुलना में अधिक महंगे हो सकते हैं।
*   **जागरूकता का अभाव:** किसानों के पास संतुलित उर्वरकों के लाभों या अपनी विशिष्ट मृदा और फसल की आवश्यकताओं के लिए NPK अनुपात के महत्व के बारे में पर्याप्त जानकारी या प्रशिक्षण की कमी हो सकती है।
*   **विषम सब्सिडी:** सरकारी नीतियां और सब्सिडी कभी-कभी कुछ पोषक तत्वों, जैसे कि यूरिया (जिसमें नाइट्रोजन होता है) के पक्ष में होती हैं, जिससे वे कृत्रिम रूप से सस्ते हो जाते हैं और किसानों को असंतुलित उपयोग की ओर प्रेरित करते हैं।

दिए गए दस्तावेज़ निम्नलिखित हैं:
*   एक निर्देशिका पृष्ठ जिसमें पी आई बी (PIB) कार्यालयों और अन्य सरकारी मंत्रालयों के लिंक दिए गए हैं।
*   पी आई बी (PIB) वेबसाइट का एक नेविगेशन मेनू।
*   किसानों के लिए प्रमाणपत्र की वैधता अवधि के बारे में एक सूचना।

इनमें से किसी भी दस्तावेज़ में इस बात की व्याख्या नहीं की गई है कि किसान संतुलित उर्वरकों का उपयोग क्यों नहीं कर रहे थे।

**सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर:**

किसानों द्वारा संतुलित उर्वरकों का उपयोग न करने का एक मुख्य कारण **मृदा परीक्षण के प्रति जागरूकता का अभाव** है। पारंपरिक रूप से, किसान अपनी विशिष्ट मृदा पोषक तत्वों की आवश्यकताओं को जाने बिना ही उर्वरकों का उपयोग करते थे, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप वे अक्सर केवल नाइट्रोजन (जैसे यूरिया) का उपयोग करते थे और फास्फोरस तथा पोटेशियम की उपेक्षा कर देते थे। भारत में शुरू की गई 'मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड' (Soil Health Card) योजना विशेष रूप से किसानों को उनकी मृदा की पोषक स्थिति के बारे में जानकारी प्रदान करके इस समस्या के समाधान के लिए बनाई गई थी। एक अन्य महत्वपूर्ण कारक **संतुलित उर्वरकों की उच्च लागत** है, जबकि यूरिया जैसे एकल-पोषक तत्व वाले उर्वरकों पर भारी सब्सिडी उपलब्ध है।

question: How do TB germs spread from one person to another?
ground_truth: TB germs spread from person to person through the air when people with TB disease in their throat or lungs cough, sneeze, talk, or sing.
triseva_answer: TB germs spread from person to person through the air. When a person with active TB disease in the throat or lungs coughs, sneezes, talks, or sings, the germs become airborne. Breathing in this contaminated air can lead to infection. TB is not transmitted by touching, kissing, or sharing food or dishes.

Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease that usually attacks the lungs. But it can also attack other parts of the body, including the kidneys, spine, and brain. Not everyone infected with TB bacteria (germs) becomes sick. So, there are two types of TB conditions: Inactive (latent) TB infection , where the TB germs live in your body but don't make you sick. TB disease (active TB) where you get sick from the TB germs. TB disease can almost always be cured with antibiotics . But if it's not treated properly, it can be fatal. TB is found in the U.S., but it is more common in certain other countries. What causes tuberculosis (TB)? TB is caused by bacteria (germs) called Mycobacterium tuberculosis . The germs spread from person to person through the air. People who have TB disease in their throat or lungs spread the germs in the air when they cough, sneeze, talk, or sing. Anyone who is near a person with TB disease can get infected with the germs. question: Where was the Soil Health Card Scheme launched?
ground_truth: The scheme was launched at Suratgarh, Rajasthan.
triseva_answer: The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan.
triseva_contexts: वेबसाइटें तथ्यों की जांच के बारे में तथ्यों की जांच के लिए जमा करें संख्याओं में तथ्य की जाँच Soil Health Card (Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare) January 17, 2022 “Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa.” – Healthy Earth. Green Farm. -Prime Minister Narendra Modi 1. Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. On the occasion, the Prime Minister gave the slogan: "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." - Healthy Earth, Green Farm. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. The International Year of Soils [5] was celebrated in 2015; the same year, the unique programme of soil health card was launched in India to assess the nutrient status of every farm holding in the country. 2. Objective s [6] : To issue soil health cards [7] every two years to all farmers, so as to provide a basis to address nutrient deficiencies in fertilization practices. To strengthen functioning of Soil Testing

at listing down measures required to improve the quality of the soil. In fact, Government also employs experts to help the farmers in carrying out the corrective measures. Farmers get a proper soil health record, thanks to the scheme. Farmers can also study the soil management practices and plan the future of their crops and land accordingly. Generally, in government schemes, the person carrying out the study for a particular farmer gets changed, but in the Soil Health Card Scheme, the government is paying attention to see to it that the same person carries out soil analysis for a farmer. Such efforts are helping to enhance the effectiveness of the scheme. The soil card gives the farmers a proper idea of which nutrients their soil is lacking, and hence, which crops they should invest in. It also tells the farmers which fertilizers they need. 5. Who is at risk for asthma? Asthma affects people of all ages, but it often starts during childhood. Certain factors can raise your risk of having asthma: Being exposed to secondhand smoke when your mother is pregnant with you or when you are a small child Being exposed to certain substances at work , such as chemical irritants or industrial dusts Genetics and family history. You are more likely to have asthma if one of your parents has it, especially if it's your mother. Race or ethnicity. In teens and adults, it is more common in women. What are the symptoms of asthma? question: Ek farmer ko soil card report kaise use karna chahiye apne kheti-baadi ke kaam plan karne ke liye?
ground_truth: Ek farmer ko report ki soil nutrient information aur recommendations use karke ye decide karna chahiye ki kaun si fasal ugani hai, kitna aur kaun sa fertilizer lagana hai, aur optimal farm productivity ke liye zaroori soil treatment plan karna chahiye.
triseva_answer:
- Soil Health Card (SHC) par diye gaye soil parameters (pH, organic carbon, N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, EC) ko review karen.
- Har parameter ko card par di gayi recommended levels se compare karen.
- Card par bataye gaye balanced fertilizers ko unki recommended dosages ke hisaab se apply karen, aur sirf urea use karne ke bajaay SHC advice follow karen.
- Card par suggested soil amendments (jaise ki pH adjust karne ke liye lime, organic matter) add karen.
- SHC advisory ke basis par, un crops ko select karen jo soil ke liye suitable hon aur jinhe avoid karna chahiye.
- Optimal yields paane ke liye sowing ya planting se pehle fertilizers aur amendments apply karne ka timing follow karen.
- Har teen saal mein ya jab bhi soil condition change ho, tab card ko update karen aur nayi recommendations ke hisaab se practices adjust karen.

question: What is a stroke and why is it dangerous?
ground_truth: A stroke occurs when there is a loss of blood flow to part of the brain, preventing brain cells from getting oxygen and nutrients. Brain cells start dying within minutes, which can cause lasting brain damage, long-term disability, or death.
triseva_answer:
A stroke occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is interrupted, depriving brain cells of oxygen and nutrients. Without blood, brain cells begin to die within minutes, which can lead to lasting brain damage, long‑term disability, or death. The two main types are:
- **Ischemic stroke** – caused by a blood clot that blocks a brain vessel (about 80% of strokes).
- **Hemorrhagic stroke** – caused by a ruptured blood vessel that bleeds into the brain.

Because brain tissue is highly dependent on a constant supply of oxygen, the rapid loss of blood flow makes a stroke dangerous, potentially causing permanent neurological deficits or fatal outcomes.

question: Kya seller kisi product ki usual price ke baare mein public ko mislead kar sakta hai? Passage iske baare mein kya kehta hai?
ground_truth: Nahi, passage ke according, public ko product ya uske jaise products ki normal price ke baare mein mislead karna ek unfair trade practice hai.
triseva_answer:
Consumer Protection Act, 2019 ke under, ek seller kisi product ki usual price ke baare mein public ko mislead nahi kar sakta. Act ek **misleading advertisement** ko aise advertisement ke roop mein define karta hai jo—
- product ya service ko falsely describe karta hai, ya
- ek false guarantee deta hai, ya
- aisa express ya implied representation deta hai jo nature, substance, quantity, quality, ya **price** ke baare mein consumer ko mislead kar sakta hai, ya
- important information ko deliberately conceal karta hai.

b2_answer: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a seller may not mislead the public about the usual price of a product. The Act defines a "misleading advertisement" as one that "falsely describes such product or service" or "deliberately conceals important information" (Source 4). Consequently, any advertisement that gives a false impression of the usual price is considered a misleading advertisement. The Central Consumer Protection Authority is empowered to issue directions to discontinue or modify such advertisements and can impose penalties of up to ₹10 lakh (and higher for repeat offences) on the manufacturer or endorser (Source 5).

question: What administrative responsibility is placed on land revenue officials regarding mutations?
ground_truth: Officials responsible for undertaking mutation of land records must have clear-cut responsibility to ensure proper eligibility determination and timely updates in the PM-KISAN portal.
triseva_answer:
Under the PM‑KISAN Operational Guidelines, State Governments must establish an administrative mechanism based on the existing land‑revenue system. Clear‑cut responsibility is assigned to the officials who carry out mutations of land records. Their duties include:
- Updating land records to reflect changes in ownership due to inheritance, sale, partition, gift, etc., in a time‑bound manner.
- Determining the eligibility of families for PM‑KISAN benefits based on the corrected land‑record entries.
- Updating the PM‑KISAN portal when a family becomes ineligible or newly eligible after a mutation, so that benefits are discontinued or started accordingly.
- Ensuring that any correction of land records for ownership accrued due to inheritance before 01.12.2018 is processed promptly and that eligibility is assessed according to the scheme’s exclusion clauses.

Source: PM‑KISAN Revised Operational Guidelines (English).

question: How many types of cancer exist and how are they named?
ground_truth: There are more than 100 different types of cancer. Most cancers are named for where they start, such as lung cancer starting in the lung or breast cancer starting in the breast.
triseva_answer:
There are more than 100 different types of cancer. Most cancers are named for the organ or tissue where they originate (e.g., lung cancer, breast cancer). They may also be described by the type of cell that formed the tumor, such as:
- **Carcinoma** – cancers arising from epithelial cells that line body surfaces and organs.
- **Sarcoma** – cancers that begin in bone, muscle, or other connective (soft) tissues.
These naming conventions help identify the cancer’s primary site and cell type.

Cancer is not just one disease but many diseases. Cancer begins in your cells, which are the building blocks of your body. Usually, your body forms new cells as needed, replacing old cells that die. Sometimes this process goes wrong. New cells grow even when you don't need them, and old cells don't die when they should. These extra cells can form a mass called a tumor. Tumors can be benign or malignant. Benign tumors aren't cancer, while malignant ones are. Cells from malignant tumors can invade nearby tissues. Symptoms and treatment depend on the type of cancer and how advanced it is. What are the types of cancer? There are more than 100 different types of cancer. Cancer can start almost anywhere in your body. Most cancers are named for where they start. For example, lung cancer starts in the lung, and breast cancer starts in the breast. cancers are named for where they start. For example, lung cancer starts in the lung, and breast cancer starts in the breast. Cancer may also be described by the type of cell that formed it, such as sarcoma if cancer begins in your bone and soft tissue. Carcinoma is the most common type of cancer. It is formed by epithelial cells, the cells that cover the inside and outside surfaces of your body. How does cancer develop? Cancer is a genetic disease. That means changes in your genes cause it. Changes in your genes are also called gene variants or mutations. Genes are parts of DNA in your cells that you inherit from your parents. However, only some cancers are caused by genes passed down from your parents. Genetic changes can occur to your genes over your lifetime that affect how your cells function. Usually, your body gets rid of damaged cells before they turn cancerous, but this ability goes down as you age. Other factors that may affect your risk of developing cancer can include: Exposure to ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun Smoking Your diet Physical inactivity What are the symptoms of cancer? Blood in your urine (pee) or stool (poop) Bleeding or bruising for no known reason A sore that doesn't heal Trouble swallowing A new mole or a change to a mole you already have Cancer may cause various symptoms but often doesn't cause pain. Don't wait until you're having pain before seeing your health care provider. See your provider if you have symptoms that don't get better in a few weeks. How is cancer diagnosed? There is no single test that can diagnose cancer. The tests ordered are usually based on your symptoms. Your provider may: Ask about your medical history Ask about your family health history , including relatives who have had cancer Do a physical exam Do a screening test such as a mammogram , colonoscopy , or a Pap test Order blood tests or imaging tests To find out if you have cancer, your provider may order a biopsy . A biopsy is the procedure of removing and examining tissue, cells, or fluids from your body. What are the treatments for cancer? Treatment depends on the type of cancer and how advanced it is. Most treatment plans may include surgery, radiation , and/or chemotherapy . Some may involve hormone therapy, immunotherapy or other types of biological therapy, or stem cell transplantation . Can cancer be prevented? It's usually not possible to know exactly why cancer develops in some people but not others. There are some things that you can't control which may increase or decrease your risk

question: How might the Soil Health Card scheme help address regional variations in soil fertility across India?
ground_truth: By using standardized sampling and analysis procedures uniformly across states and designing targeted block-level fertilizer recommendations for specific districts, the scheme can address region-specific soil fertility constraints.
triseva_answer:
The Soil Health Card (SHC) scheme tackles regional differences in soil fertility by:

- Conducting uniform soil sampling and analysis across all states using standardized procedures, ensuring that each farm’s nutrient profile is accurately measured.
- Providing a printed report for each holding that lists the status of 12 key parameters (N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC, OC) and gives specific fertilizer and amendment recommendations tailored to that farm’s soil condition.
- Guiding farmers on which crops are best suited to their soil’s nutrient status, helping them align cropping choices with local fertility levels.
- Delivering block‑ and taluka‑level fertilizer recommendations, allowing region‑specific nutrient management plans.
- Enabling corrective actions (e.g., targeted fertilizer application, soil amendments) that reduce excess chemical fertilizer use by 8‑10 % and raise yields by 5‑6 % where the recommendations are followed.
- Supporting capacity‑building through demonstrations, trainings, and involvement of Krishi Sakhis/Pasu Sakhis to ensure farmers understand and apply the SHC advice correctly.
- Establishing a network of new and strengthened soil testing laboratories (static, mobile, mini‑labs, village‑level labs) to provide timely, reliable data for every region.
- Ensuring continuity by having the same analyst conduct repeated tests for a farmer, improving consistency of recommendations over time.

Together, these elements allow the SHC scheme to address the diverse soil fertility conditions found across India’s varied agro‑ecological zones.

ground_truth: If you don't follow the directions, TB germs could change and become antibiotic resistant, meaning the medicine may stop working and TB may become hard to cure.
triseva_answer:
Following the prescribed directions for tuberculosis (TB) medication is crucial because:
- If you do not take the medicine exactly as directed, the TB bacteria can change and become antibiotic‑resistant, making the infection harder to cure.
- Proper adherence ensures the treatment works effectively and almost always cures TB when taken correctly.
- Completing the full course (which may last three, four, six, or nine months depending on the regimen) prevents the disease from returning and reduces the risk of spreading it to others.

ground_truth: A doctor diagnoses anemia through a physical exam and blood tests.

A doctor diagnoses anemia with a physical exam and blood tests. The blood tests that may be ordered include:
- Complete blood count (CBC)
- Reticulocyte count
- Blood smear
- Iron tests (serum iron, ferritin, total iron‑binding capacity)
- Haptoglobin (HP) test
- Hemoglobin electrophoresis
- Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) test (including LDH isoenzymes)
- Red blood cell (RBC) indices
- Vitamin B test
- Vitamin B12 level test
- Bone marrow tests (bone marrow biopsy) if needed

Anemia Also called: Iron poor blood On this page Basics Summary Start Here Symptoms Diagnosis and Tests Prevention and Risk Factors Treatments and Therapies Learn More Related Issues Specifics Genetics See, Play and Learn No links available Research Statistics and Research Clinical Trials Journal Articles Resources Find an Expert For You Children Women Older Adults Patient Handouts Summary If you have anemia, your blood does not carry enough oxygen to the rest of your body. The most common cause of anemia is not having enough iron . Your body needs iron to make hemoglobin. Hemoglobin is an iron-rich protein that gives the red color to blood. It carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body. Anemia has three main causes: blood loss, lack of red blood cell production, and high rates of red blood cell destruction. Conditions that may lead to anemia include: Heavy periods Pregnancy Ulcers Colon polyps or colon cancer Inherited disorders A diet that does not have enough iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 Blood disorders such as sickle cell anemia and thalassemia , or cancer Aplastic anemia , a condition that can be inherited or acquired G6PD deficiency , a metabolic disorder Anemia can make you feel tired, cold, dizzy, and irritable. You may be short of breath or have a headache. Your doctor will diagnose anemia with a physical exam and blood tests. Treatment depends on the kind of anemia you have. b2_answer:
A doctor diagnoses anemia through a physical examination and a series of blood tests. The key diagnostic steps include:

- **Physical exam** to assess signs such as pallor, fatigue, or rapid heart rate.
- **Complete Blood Count (CBC)** to measure hemoglobin and hematocrit levels.
- **Red Blood Cell (RBC) indices** to evaluate size and color of red cells.
- **Reticulocyte count** to check bone marrow response.
- **Blood smear** to examine the shape of red blood cells.
- **Iron studies** (serum iron, total iron‑binding capacity, ferritin) to assess iron status.
- **Vitamin B12 and folate tests** to detect deficiencies.
- **Haptoglobin test** and **lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) test** for hemolysis.
- **Hemoglobin electrophoresis** when hemoglobin disorders are suspected.
- **Bone marrow biopsy** in selected cases to evaluate production problems.

These tests together help determine the type and cause of anemia.

question: Kya pata chalta hai ki kidney ki bimari khatarnak kyu hai agar ilaaj na kiya jaaye?
ground_truth: Agar kidney ki bimari nephrons ko damage kar de, toh kidney body se waste nikaal nahi paati, aur agar kidney poori tarah fail ho jaayein, toh insaan ko jeene ke liye dialysis ya kidney transplant ki zaroorat padti hai.
triseva_answer:
Kidney disease becomes dangerous when it is not treated because:
- The kidneys can no longer filter waste products and excess fluid from the blood, leading to a buildup of toxins in the body.
- Over time, the damage can progress to kidney failure, at which point the patient will need dialysis or a kidney transplant to survive.
- Chronic kidney disease slowly destroys the tiny filtering units (nephrons) in the kidneys, worsening the loss of function if left untreated.

However, based on general knowledge, kidney disease is dangerous if left untreated because the kidneys are responsible for filtering waste products and excess fluid from the blood. When they fail to do this effectively, several serious health problems can occur:

*   **Buildup of Toxins:** Harmful waste products, like urea, build up in the bloodstream, a condition called uremia. This can poison the body and affect the brain, heart, and other organs.
*   **Fluid Retention:** The body cannot remove excess fluid, leading to swelling (edema) in the legs, hands, and feet, and potentially fluid in the lungs (pulmonary edema), which can cause severe shortness of breath.
*   **Kidney Failure:** Untreated kidney disease can progress to complete kidney failure (end-stage renal disease). At this point, the kidneys have lost almost all function.
*   **Need for Dialysis or Transplant:** To survive with kidney failure, a person requires regular dialysis (a treatment that artificially filters the blood) or a kidney transplant.
*   **Increased Risk of Heart Disease and Stroke:** Kidney disease is a major risk factor for cardiovascular problems. The strain on the body from kidney dysfunction significantly increases the risk of heart attack and stroke.

Most travelers do not need cholera vaccine. If you are an adult 18 through 64 years old traveling to an area where people are getting infected with cholera, your health care provider might recommend the vaccine for you. In clinical studies, cholera vaccine was very effective in preventing severe or life-threatening cholera. However, it is not 100% effective against cholera and does not protect from other foodborne or waterborne diseases. Cholera vaccine is not a substitute for being careful about what you eat or drink. Who should not receive the cholera vaccine? Tell the person who is giving you the vaccine: If you have any severe, life-threatening allergies. If you have ever had a life-threatening allergic reaction after a previous dose of any cholera vaccine, or if you have a severe allergy to any ingredient in this vaccine, you should not get the vaccine. Tell your health care provider if you have any severe allergies that you know of. He or she can tell you about the vaccine's ingredients. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Not much is known about the potential risks of this vaccine for a pregnant or breastfeeding woman. A registry has been set up to learn more about vaccination during pregnancy. However, based on general knowledge:

The Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme and the Soil Health Card (SHC) programme are designed to work together to promote balanced fertilizer use in Indian agriculture.

*   The **Soil Health Card programme** provides farmers with a scientific analysis of their soil's nutrient status. It gives them a report with specific recommendations on what nutrients their soil needs and in what quantities.
*   The **Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme** provides a subsidy on the nutrients themselves (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, and Sulphur) rather than on specific fertilizer products. This makes it financially viable for farmers to purchase the specific nutrients their soil is deficient in, as recommended by their Soil Health Card.

In essence, the SHC scheme tells the farmer *what* to apply, and the NBS scheme helps make it affordable to apply the right nutrients, thereby encouraging the move away from imbalanced fertilizer use (like over-applying urea) towards more balanced and integrated nutrient management.

ground_truth: The primary purpose is to provide a basis to address nutrient deficiencies in fertilization practices and to develop soil test-based nutrient management for enhancing nutrient use efficiency.
triseva_answer:
The primary purpose of issuing Soil Health Cards is to provide farmers with a detailed report of their soil’s nutrient status and specific fertilizer/soil‑amendment recommendations, enabling balanced nutrient management, improved soil health, and higher yields.

- Shows the levels of macro‑nutrients (N, P, K), secondary nutrients (S), micro‑nutrients (Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B) and physical parameters (pH, EC, OC).

- Helps farmers avoid indiscriminate use of urea and adopt balanced, integrated nutrient management practices.

question: What restrictions are placed on the Chairperson or Members of the Authority after their term ends?
ground_truth: Section 16 imposes restrictions on the Chairperson or Members regarding employment after cessation of office, though specific details of these restrictions are not provided in the passage.
triseva_answer:
After ceasing to hold office, the Chairperson or a Member of the Authority is restricted from:
- Accepting any employment in, or being connected with the management of any organization, company, or other entity that has been associated with any work done or contracted out by the Authority (directly or indirectly) during their tenure, for a period of three years from the date they cease to hold office, **unless** they obtain prior approval from the Central Government.
- The restriction does **not** apply to employment under the Central Government, a State Government, a local authority, any statutory authority, or any corporation established by or under a Central, State, or provincial Act, or a Government Company as defined in the Companies Act, 2013.

Source: Section 16 – "Restrictions on Chairperson or Members on employment after cessation of office" of the Authority Act (as provided in the legal database).

question: What is the time window for administering tPA medicine after stroke symptoms begin?
ground_truth: tPA (tissue plasminogen activator) can only be given within 4 hours of when stroke symptoms started. The sooner it is administered, the better the chance of recovery.

question: How would you categorise the organisations in this schedule, and what does the Central Bureau of Investigation's inclusion tell us about its status?
ground_truth: The organisations can be categorised into intelligence, border security, and investigation agencies. The CBI's inclusion indicates it is recognised as a central intelligence and security organisation by the government.
triseva_answer:
The organisations listed in the Second Schedule of the Right to Information Act, 2005 are **intelligence and security organisations established by the Central Government**. They are grouped together as a single category of agencies that are exempt from the RTI Act’s disclosure requirements (subject to specific exceptions for corruption and human‑rights violations). The inclusion of the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** in this schedule indicates that, under the RTI Act, the CBI is classified as an intelligence and security organisation. Consequently, the CBI is exempt from the general provisions of the RTI Act, though information pertaining to allegations of corruption or human‑rights violations must still be disclosed after approval by the Central Information Commission.

**Key points**:
- Category: Intelligence and security organisations established by the Central Government.
- CBI’s inclusion: Confirms its status as an intelligence/security agency for RTI purposes, granting it exemption from routine RTI disclosures.

question: How does the time period for calculating the thirty-day deadline change when additional fees are charged?
ground_truth: The period between the dispatch of the fee intimation and the payment of fees is excluded from the thirty-day calculation, effectively extending the deadline.
triseva_answer:
When a Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) or State Public Information Officer (SPIO) decides that additional fees are required to provide the information, they must send an intimation to the applicant detailing the further fees and the calculations. **The period between the dispatch of this intimation and the payment of the fees is excluded from the calculation of the thirty‑day deadline** for providing the information. Consequently, the thirty‑day period starts only after the applicant has paid the additional fees.

Source: Right to Information Act, Section 7(3)(a) – "the period intervening between the despatch of the said intimation and payment of fees shall be excluded for the purpose of calculating the period of thirty days referred to in that sub‑section."

question: What is diabetes and how does it affect blood glucose levels?
ground_truth: Diabetes is a disease in which blood glucose (blood sugar) levels are too high. In diabetes, the body can't make insulin, can't use insulin properly, or both, causing too much glucose to stay in the blood instead of reaching cells for energy.
triseva_answer: Diabetes, also called diabetes mellitus, is a disease in which blood glucose (blood sugar) levels become too high. Glucose is the body’s main source of energy and comes from food and the body’s own production. Insulin, a hormone made by the pancreas, helps move glucose from the bloodstream into cells where it can be used for energy. In diabetes, the body either cannot make insulin, cannot use insulin effectively, or both. As a result, excess glucose remains in the blood instead of entering cells, leading to elevated blood glucose levels. Normal fasting blood glucose is 70‑100 mg/dL; a fasting level above 126 mg/dL is considered diabetic.

Diabetes, also known as diabetes mellitus, is a disease in which your blood glucose , or blood sugar, levels are too high. Glucose is your body's main source of energy. Your body can make glucose, but it also comes from the food you eat. Insulin is a hormone made by your pancreas. Insulin helps move glucose from your bloodstream into your cells, where it can be used for energy. If you have diabetes, your body can't make insulin, can't use insulin as well as it should, or both. Too much glucose stays in your blood and doesn't reach your cells. This can cause glucose levels to get too high. Over time, high blood glucose levels can lead to serious health conditions . Can diabetes be prevented? Type 1 diabetes can't be prevented.
