Why get vaccinated? Cholera is a disease that can cause severe diarrhea and vomiting. If it isn't treated quickly, it can lead to dehydration and even death. About 100,000-130,000 people are thought to die from cholera each year, almost all of them in countries where the disease is common. Cholera is caused by bacteria and spread through contaminated food or water. It isn't usually spread directly from person to person, but it can be spread through contact with the feces of an infected person. Cholera is very rare among U.S. citizens. It is a risk mostly to people traveling in countries where the disease is common (mainly Haiti, and parts of Africa, Asia, and the Pacific). It has also occurred in the United States among people eating raw or undercooked seafood from the Gulf Coast. Being careful about what you eat and drink while traveling and practicing good personal hygiene, can help prevent waterborne and foodborne diseases, including cholera. For someone who has been infected, rehydration (replacing water and chemicals lost through diarrhea or vomiting) can greatly reduce the chance of dying. Vaccination can reduce the risk of getting sick from cholera. Cholera vaccine The cholera vaccine used in the United States is an oral (swallowed) vaccine. Only one dose is needed. Booster doses are not recommended at this time. Most travelers do not need cholera vaccine. triseva_answer: मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड योजना ने 19 फरवरी 2020 को 5 वर्ष पूरे कर लिए थे।

Khet Haraa.” – Healthy Earth. Green Farm. -Prime Minister Narendra Modi 1. Introduction The Soil Health Card Scheme [1] was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi [2] on 19.02.2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan. On the occasion, the Prime Minister gave the slogan: "Swasth Dharaa. Khet Haraa." - Healthy Earth, Green Farm. Referring to the song "Vande Mataram," he said that in order to achieve a land that is truly "Sujalam, Suphalam," it is necessary to nurture the soil. PM Modi added that soil health card scheme is a step towards fulfilling this dream. The scheme [3] has been introduced to assist State Governments to issue soil health cards [4] to all farmers in the country. Soil health card provides information to farmers on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendation on appropriate dosage of nutrients to be applied for improving soil health and its fertility. The International Year of Soils [5] was celebrated in 2015; the same year, the unique programme of soil health card was launched in India to assess the nutrient status of every farm holding in the country. 2. Objective s [6] : To issue soil health cards [7] every two years to all farmers, so as to provide a basis to address nutrient deficiencies in fertilization practices. To strengthen functioning of Soil Testing

Study on Impact of Soil Health Card Scheme by National Productivity Council [21] National Productivity Council (NPC) [22] carried out a study on ‘Soil Testing Infrastructure for Faster Delivery of Soil Health Card in India’ and submitted its report in February 2017. The study was conducted in 76 districts in 19 States covering 170 soil testing labs and 1700 farmers. Some of the findings of the study are as follows: More than 90 per cent of farmers surveyed informed that they have not got their soil tested before the implementation of this scheme. 92 per cent farmers reported not having used balanced fertilizer and micro nutrients in absence of information related to availability of nutrients in their soil. As a result of application of fertilizer and micro-nutrients as per the recommendations on the Soil Health Cards, it was reported that there has been a decrease of use of chemical fertilizer application in the range of 8-10 per cent. Overall increase in the yield of crops to the tune of 5-6 per cent was reported due to application of fertilizer and micro nutrients as per recommendations available in the Soil Health Cards. 9. ground_truth: Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease that usually attacks the lungs, but it can also attack other parts of the body, including the kidneys, spine, and brain.

Why is this medication prescribed? Insulin glulisine is used to treat type 1 diabetes (condition in which the body does not make insulin and therefore cannot control the amount of sugar in the blood). It is also used to treat people with type 2 diabetes (condition in which the blood sugar is too high because the body does not produce or use insulin normally) who need insulin to control their diabetes. In patients with type 1 diabetes, insulin glulisine is usually used with another type of insulin, unless it is used in an external insulin pump. In patients with type 2 diabetes, insulin glulisine also may be used with another type of insulin or with oral medication(s) for diabetes. Insulin glulisine is a short-acting, synthetic version of human insulin. Insulin glulisine works by replacing the insulin that is normally produced by the body and by helping move sugar from the blood into other body tissues where it is used for energy. It also stops the liver from producing more sugar. Over time, people who have diabetes and high blood sugar can develop serious or life-threatening complications, including heart disease, stroke, kidney problems, nerve damage, and eye problems. Using medication(s), making lifestyle changes (e.g., diet, exercise, quitting smoking), and regularly checking your blood sugar may help to manage your diabetes and improve your health. This therapy may also decrease your chances of having a heart attack, stroke, or other diabetes-related complications such as kidney failure, nerve damage (numb, cold legs or

Why is this medication prescribed? Fluoxymesterone is used to treat symptoms of low testosterone in adult men who have hypogonadism (a condition in which the body does not produce enough natural testosterone). Fluoxymesterone is used only for men with low testosterone levels caused by certain medical conditions, including disorders of the testicles, pituitary gland, (a small gland in the brain) or hypothalamus (a part of the brain) that cause hypogonadism. Fluoxymesterone is also used to stimulate puberty in men with delayed puberty. Fluoxymesterone may also be used alone or along with other medications in certain women with breast cancer that has spread to other parts of the body and can not be removed with surgery. Fluoxymesterone is in a class of medications called androgenic hormones. It works by supplying testosterone to replace the testosterone that is normally produced naturally in the body. Testosterone is a hormone produced by the body that contributes to the growth, development, and functioning of the male sexual organs and typical male characteristics. When used to treat breast cancer, testosterone works by blocking the release of estrogen to stop or slow the growth of breast cancer.. How should this medicine be used? Fluoxymesterone comes as a tablet to take by mouth. It usually is taken with or without food once a day or three or four times a day. Follow the directions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist to explain any part you do not understand. Take fluoxymesterone exactly as directed.

question: What information must be displayed at each worksite according to the Janata Information System?

प्रदत्त संदर्भ 'भारतीय न्याय संहिता, 2023' से संबंधित है, जो विभिन्न आपराधिक अपराधों और उनके दंडों की रूपरेखा तैयार करता है। इसमें "अनुबंध" (कॉन्ट्रैक्ट) का एकमात्र उल्लेख खंड 355 में है, जो "सहायक व्यक्ति की आवश्यकताओं की पूर्ति के लिए उपस्थित होने के अनुबंध के उल्लंघन" से संबंधित है, न कि अनुबंध के भीतर अनुचित शर्तों से।

मैं दिए गए दस्तावेजों में इस प्रश्न का उत्तर नहीं खोज पा रहा हूँ।

दिए गए दस्तावेज तीन सरकारी कल्याणकारी योजनाओं (PM-KISAN, आयुष्मान भारत और PMAY) का वर्णन करते हैं और इनमें किसी भी अनुबंध की शर्तों का उल्लेख नहीं है, चाहे वे निष्पक्ष हों या अनुचित।

हालाँकि, सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर, यहाँ अनुचित अनुबंध शर्तों के तीन उदाहरण दिए गए हैं जो विभिन्न समझौतों में दिखाई दे सकते हैं:

1. **एकाधिकार समाप्ति खंड (Unilateral Termination Clauses):** ये खंड एक पक्ष (आमतौर पर अधिक शक्तिशाली पक्ष, जैसे कि कोई कंपनी) को बिना किसी दंड या सूचना के दूसरे पक्ष के साथ अनुबंध समाप्त करने की अनुमति देते हैं, जबकि दूसरे पक्ष के पास ऐसा कोई समान अधिकार नहीं होता।
2. **अत्यधिक दंड खंड (Excessive Penalty Clauses):** ये खंड अनुबंध के मामूली उल्लंघन के लिए दूसरे पक्ष पर अत्यधिक वित्तीय दंड लगाते हैं, जो वास्तविक नुकसान की तुलना में बहुत अधिक होता है।
3. **छिपी हुई फीस या अस्पष्ट भाषा:** ये शर्तें स्पष्ट रूप से प्रकट नहीं की जाती हैं या ऐसी जटिल कानूनी भाषा में लिखी जाती हैं जिसे समझना आम व्यक्ति के लिए कठिन हो, जिससे अप्रत्याशित शुल्क या बाध्यताएं उत्पन्न होती हैं।

Eligibility: small and marginal farmer families with combined landholding up to 2 hectares. Exclusions: institutional landholders, farmer families holding constitutional posts, serving or retired government employees with monthly pension above Rs 10000, income tax payers.

Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) provides health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation. Eligible families are based on SECC 2011 database. Documents required: Aadhaar card, ration card, income certificate. Over 1700 treatment packages covered. No premium to be paid by beneficiary.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) aims to provide affordable housing for all. Urban component provides interest subsidy on home loans. EWS category (income up to Rs 3 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. LIG category (income Rs 3-6 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. MIG-I (income Rs 6-12 lakh): 4% subsidy. MIG-II (income Rs 12-18 lakh): 3% subsidy.

question: Arthritis kya hota hai?
ground_truth: Arthritis koi bhi disorder hota hai jo joints ko affect karta hai, jo woh jagahein hoti hain jahan do bones ek dusre se milte hain. Isse commonly joint mein pain aur inflammation (swelling) hota hai, aur time ke saath ek swollen joint bahut severely damage ho sakta hai.
triseva_answer: Arthritis is any disorder that affects the joints. Joints are places where two bones meet, such as the elbow or knee. Most types of arthritis cause joint pain and inflammation (swelling). Over time, a swollen joint can become severely damaged. Some kinds of arthritis can also cause problems in organs such as the eyes or skin.

arthritis is one type. Psoriatic arthritis affects people with psoriasis (itchy or sore scaly red and white skin patches). Gout is a painful type of arthritis that happens when too much uric acid builds up in your body. It often starts in the big toe. Other joints can also be affected. Ankylosing spondylitis is a type of arthritis of the spine that can cause stiffness and make it difficult to move and bend. What are the symptoms of arthritis? Pain, redness, warmth, and joint inflammation are common arthritis symptoms. You may not be able to move your joint as well as it should. Other symptoms could include fever , weight loss, breathing difficulties, or a rash. Symptoms often get worse as you age. Some symptoms of arthritis may be signs of other illnesses. Who is more likely to get arthritis? A few things that might increase your chance of getting arthritis include: Family history. You may be more likely to get certain types of arthritis if a member of your family has the disorder. Age. The risk of getting many types of arthritis increases with age. Sex. Certain types of arthritis are more common in women, while other types are more common in men. Other factors that might increase your risk of getting arthritis include having a previous joint injury, obesity , or lupus . How is arthritis diagnosed? To find out if you have arthritis, your health care provider may: Ask you about your medical history, including your symptoms.

arthritis is one type. Psoriatic arthritis affects people with psoriasis (itchy or sore scaly red and white skin patches). Pain, redness, warmth, and joint inflammation are common arthritis symptoms. You may not be able to move your joint as well as it should. Other symptoms could include fever , weight loss, breathing difficulties, or a rash. Symptoms often get worse as you age. Some symptoms of arthritis may be signs of other illnesses. Who is more likely to get arthritis? A few things that might increase your chance of getting arthritis include: Family history. You may be more likely to get certain types of arthritis if a member of your family has the disorder. Age. The risk of getting many types of arthritis increases with age. Sex. Certain types of arthritis are more common in women, while other types are more common in men. Other factors that might increase your risk of getting arthritis include having a previous joint injury, obesity , or lupus . How is arthritis diagnosed? To find out if you have arthritis, your health care provider may: Ask you about your medical history, including your symptoms.

question: What is the connection between soil health cards and fertilizer management?
ground_truth: The soil health card identifies nutrient deficiencies in the soil and recommends specific fertilizers needed, enabling farmers to apply fertilizers more efficiently and avoid unnecessary or excessive use.
triseva_answer:
The Soil Health Card (SHC) links directly to fertilizer management by:
- Providing a report of the soil’s nutrient status (N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC, OC) for each holding.
- Indicating the specific fertilizer recommendations and soil amendments required for the farm based on that status.
- Showing the recommended dosage of each nutrient needed.
- Advising the farmer on the types and quantities of fertilizers to apply to achieve optimal yields.
- When farmers follow the SHC recommendations, chemical fertilizer use decreases by 8‑10 % and crop yields increase by 5‑6 %.

- Being issued every two to three years, ensuring that fertilizer plans are updated with the latest soil health information.

question: What is the primary method of diagnosing dengue?
ground_truth: A blood test can show if a person has been infected with dengue.
triseva_answer: The primary method of diagnosing dengue is a blood test that can show if you have been infected with dengue.

About 1 in 20 people who get sick with dengue will develop severe dengue. It can cause shock , internal bleeding, and even death. People are more likely to develop severe dengue if they have had dengue before, are pregnant, or are infants. Watch for signs and symptoms of severe dengue. Warning signs usually begin about 24 - 48 hours after your fever has gone away. If you or your family member have these signs, get immediate medical care: Severe abdominal (belly) pain and tenderness Vomiting at least 3 times in 24 hours Bleeding from the nose or gums Vomiting blood, or blood in the stool (poop) Feeling tired, restless, or irritable How is dengue diagnosed? There is a blood test which can show if you have been infected with dengue. What are the treatments for dengue? There is no specific medicine to treat dengue. Most people will get better after about a week. But if you think you might have dengue: See a health care provider and mention any recent travel. Rest as much as possible. Take acetaminophen to control fever and relieve pain. But do not take aspirin or ibuprofen. Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration . Severe dengue often requires care at a hospital. question: What multi-stakeholder approach is evident in the implementation of this soil health programme?
ground_truth: The programme involves state/district agriculture departments, panchayats, village-level workers (Krishi Sakhis, Pasu Sakhis), and rural development workers to create a comprehensive network for farmer education and soil health management.
triseva_answer:
The Soil Health Card Scheme involves a coordinated multi‑stakeholder implementation model that includes:

- **Central and State Governments** – jointly fund up to 75 % of laboratory costs and sanction new and strengthened soil testing labs across states.
- **Village Youth, Farmers, Self‑Help Groups, Farmers’ Cooperative Societies, Farmers’ Groups and Agricultural Producing Organisations** – eligible to set up Soil Health Laboratories and conduct testing.
- **Panchayats and State/District Agriculture Machinery** – work with village‑level workers to roll out the programme.
- **Village‑level Rural Development Workers** – Krishi Sakhis and Pasu Sakhis educate farmers on the correct use of fertilizers.
- **Demonstration, Training and Farmer Melas** – organized at scale (≈6 lakh demonstrations, 37 k trainings, 7.4 k melas) to disseminate soil health information and best practices.
- **Soil Testing Infrastructure** – establishment of 11,531 new labs (static, mobile, mini‑labs, village‑level labs) and strengthening of 829 existing labs to support testing and card issuance.

question: What diagnostic methods does a doctor use to confirm anemia?
ground_truth: A doctor diagnoses anemia with a physical exam and blood tests.
triseva_answer:
Doctors confirm anemia using a combination of physical examination and laboratory tests. Common diagnostic methods include:

- Physical exam
- Complete blood count (CBC)
- Blood smear (peripheral smear)
- Red blood cell (RBC) indices
- Reticulocyte count
- Ferritin blood test
- Iron tests (serum iron, total iron binding capacity)
- Haptoglobin test
- Hemoglobin electrophoresis
- Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) test
- Vitamin B12 and folate tests
- Bone marrow biopsy (bone marrow test)
- Additional specific tests such as serum free hemoglobin, stool guaiac test, and others as indicated

However, based on general medical knowledge, doctors use several methods to diagnose and confirm anemia. The primary diagnostic tool is a blood test called a **Complete Blood Count (CBC)**. This test measures:

*   **Hemoglobin:** The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. Low hemoglobin is a key indicator of anemia.
*   **Hematocrit:** The percentage of your blood volume composed of red blood cells. A low hematocrit level also suggests anemia.
*   **Red Blood Cell (RBC) Count:** The total number of red blood cells in your blood.

To determine the cause of the anemia, a doctor may order additional tests, such as:

*   **Reticulocyte Count:** Measures the number of young red blood cells to see if the bone marrow is producing enough.
*   **Iron Studies:** Measures levels of iron, ferritin, and total iron-binding capacity to diagnose iron-deficiency anemia.
*   **Vitamin B12 and Folate Levels:** To check for deficiencies that can cause certain types of anemia.
*   **Peripheral Blood Smear:** A sample of blood is examined under a microscope to look at the size, shape, and color of the red blood cells.

question: What makes the Soil Health Card Scheme unique compared to other agricultural initiatives?
ground_truth: The scheme is unique because it aims to assess the nutrient status of every individual farm holding in the country and provide personalized nutrient dosage recommendations, making it a comprehensive and farm-specific approach to soil management.
triseva_answer:
- The Soil Health Card Scheme provides each farmer with a printed soil health report for each holding, containing details about the soil and specific fertilizer and soil‑amendment recommendations.
- The scheme ensures continuity by having the same person conduct the soil analysis for a farmer over time.
- It aims to cover all farmers across the country, issuing a card once every three years (or every two years in some states).
- The card includes advisory based on the soil nutrient status, indicating which nutrients are lacking and which crops to invest in.
- Farmers receive financial assistance to apply corrective measures for identified deficiencies.
- The scheme has led to the establishment of over 11,500 new soil‑testing labs (static, mobile, mini‑labs and village‑level labs) and strengthening of existing labs.
- Extension workers such as Krishi Sakhis and Pasu Sakhis are involved in educating farmers on the right use of fertilizers.
- It organizes demonstrations, trainings and farmer melas to promote soil‑test‑based nutrient management.

The Soil Health Card Scheme stands out from other agricultural initiatives in the following ways:
- It provides a **printed soil health card for each farm holding**, containing a detailed report of the soil’s status.
- The card reports the **status of the soil with respect to 12 parameters**: N (Nitrogen), P (Phosphorus), K (Potassium) – macro‑nutrients; S (Sulphur) – secondary nutrient; Zn (Zinc), Fe (Iron), Cu (Copper), Mn (Manganese), B (Boron) – micro‑nutrients; and pH, EC, OC (Physical parameters).
- Based on these results, the card **indicates specific fertilizer recommendations and soil‑amendment measures** needed for the farm, including dosage of different nutrients and quantities of fertilizers to apply.
- It delivers an **advisory tailored to the soil nutrient status** of the farmer’s holding, helping decide which crops to cultivate and which to avoid.
- The scheme aims to **cover all farmers across the entire country**, with a nationwide rollout.
- A farm receives a new soil health card **once every three years** (some sources mention every two years), ensuring regular updates.
- The same analyst conducts the soil analysis for a farmer across cycles, maintaining continuity.
- It includes **capacity‑building for soil testing laboratories**, involvement of agriculture students, and linkage with ICAR/State Agricultural Universities.
- Standardized procedures for **uniform sampling, analysis, and taluka/block‑level fertilizer recommendations** are established.
- The government provides **financial assistance to farmers** to apply corrective measures and promotes balanced, integrated nutrient management practices.

b1_answer:
Based on the provided context, the significance of Section 52, titled 'Protection of action taken in good faith', is that it provides legal immunity to specific individuals and entities.

The section states: "No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Central Government or the Authority or the Chairperson or any Member or any officer, or other employees of the Authority for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Act or under any rule or order made thereunder."

The significance of this section is:

*   **It protects officials from legal action:** It shields the Central Government, the Authority, its Chairperson, Members, officers, and employees from being sued, prosecuted, or facing other legal proceedings.
*   **The protection is conditional:** This immunity only applies when the actions are taken "in good faith" while performing duties under the Act. This means the protection is not absolute and does not cover malicious, dishonest, or knowingly illegal actions.
*   **It ensures smooth functioning:** By providing this protection, the law encourages officials to carry out their responsibilities without the constant fear of litigation, thereby facilitating the effective implementation of the Act.

question: उल्लिखित पारदर्शिता उपायों के आधार पर, एक नागरिक को अपने गाँव में नौकरी कार्ड धारकों को सही मजदूरी भुगतान किया गया था या नहीं, इसकी पुष्टि करने के लिए किन कदमों को उठाने की आवश्यकता होगी?
ground_truth: एक नागरिक नौकरी कार्ड की सूची, प्रदान किए गए काम के दिनों की संख्या और प्रत्येक नौकरी कार्ड धारक को भुगतान किए गए वेतन की जांच कर सकता है, और गाँव में प्रमुख दीवारों या सार्वजनिक बोर्डों पर प्रदर्शित प्रत्येक नौकरी कार्ड धारक को भुगतान किए गए वेतन की जांच कर सकता है और गाँव संगठनों द्वारा आयोजित समवर्ती मासिक सामाजिक ऑडिट से रिपोर्ट भी प्राप्त कर सकता है।
triseva_answer:
MGNREGA पारदर्शिता प्रावधानों के अनुसार, एक नागरिक निम्नलिखित कदम उठाकर यह सत्यापित कर सकता है कि जॉब कार्ड धारकों को सही मजदूरी का भुगतान किया गया है:

- **कार्यस्थल का दौरा करें**: कार्यस्थल पर प्रदर्शित 'जनता' अनुमान (कार्य का विवरण, अनुमानित श्रम दिवस, सामग्री की मात्रा और लागत) का निरीक्षण करें और मस्टर रोल देखें, जो सार्वजनिक रूप से उपलब्ध कराया जाना अनिवार्य है।
- **ग्राम सार्वजनिक बोर्ड की जाँच करें**: गाँव की किसी प्रमुख दीवार या सार्वजनिक बोर्ड पर जॉब कार्ड धारकों की सूची, प्रदान किए गए कार्य के दिनों की संख्या और प्रत्येक धारक को भुगतान की गई मजदूरी देखें।
- **ग्राम पंचायत कार्यालय जाएँ**: अनुमोदित परियोजनाओं, वर्ष-वार पूर्ण किए गए कार्यों, प्रदान किए गए रोजगार, प्राप्त निधियों और व्यय, उपयोग की गई सामग्री की सूची और खरीद दरों को दर्शाने वाले बोर्ड की समीक्षा करें।
- **वेबसाइट एक्सेस करें**: ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय या राज्य ग्रामीण विकास विभाग की वेबसाइट पर जाएँ, जहाँ अधिनियम और संबंधित जानकारी डाउनलोड करने योग्य इलेक्ट्रॉनिक प्रारूप में उपलब्ध कराई जाती है।
- **मस्टर रोल एक्सेस का अनुरोध करें**: कार्य के घंटों के दौरान किसी भी दिन कार्यस्थल पर मस्टर रोल देखने की मांग करें, क्योंकि किसी भी व्यक्ति को मांग पर मस्टर रोल एक्सेस करने की अनुमति है।
- **मासिक सामाजिक अंकेक्षण (सोशल ऑडिट) में भाग लें**: कार्यक्रम अधिकारी द्वारा आयोजित मासिक सामाजिक अंकेक्षण में भाग लें या उसका अनुरोध करें, जहाँ पिछले महीने के कार्यों और व्यय का विवरण नागरिकों और भारत निर्माण स्वयंसेवकों के लिए निःशुल्क उपलब्ध कराया जाता है।

प्रदत्त दस्तावेजों में उल्लिखित पारदर्शिता उपायों के आधार पर, एक नागरिक निम्नलिखित चरणों के माध्यम से यह सत्यापित कर सकता है कि क्या नौकरी कार्ड धारकों को सही मजदूरी का भुगतान किया गया था:

1. **नौकरी कार्ड पर विवरण की जाँच करें:** दस्तावेजों के अनुसार, नौकरी कार्ड में नियमित रूप से अद्यतन (अपडेट) किए जाने वाले प्रमुख विवरणों की एक सूची होती है। एक नागरिक को अपने नौकरी कार्ड पर निम्नलिखित जानकारी देखनी चाहिए:
    * **"भुगतान की गई मजदूरी की तिथि-वार राशि"**
    * **"कार्य की तिथियाँ और कार्य के दिनों की संख्या"**
    * **"कार्य आवंटन का विवरण और muster roll (हाजिरी बही) संख्या"**

2. **आधिकारिक हाजिरी बही (मस्टर रोल) के साथ मिलान करें:** नौकरी कार्ड पर उल्लिखित muster roll संख्या एक महत्वपूर्ण जानकारी है। नागरिक को इस संख्या का उपयोग ग्राम पंचायत से आधिकारिक हाजिरी बही प्राप्त करने के लिए करना चाहिए। इसके पश्चात, उन्हें हाजिरी बही में दर्ज विवरणों (जैसे कि कार्य के दिन और आवंटित कार्य) की तुलना अपने नौकरी कार्ड पर मुद्रित विवरणों से करनी चाहिए ताकि यह सुनिश्चित हो सके कि भुगतान की गई मजदूरी सही है।

MGNREGA पारदर्शिता उपायों के अंतर्गत, एक नागरिक अपने गाँव में जॉब-कार्ड धारकों को सही मजदूरी भुगतान की पुष्टि करने के लिए निम्नलिखित कदम उठा सकता है:

- **मस्टर रोल का सार्वजनिक प्रदर्शन**: ग्राम पंचायत कार्यालय में प्रदर्शित मस्टर रोल (उपस्थिति रजिस्टर) की जाँच करें। इसमें श्रमिकों के नाम, जॉब-कार्ड नंबर, कार्य के दिन और भुगतान की गई मजदूरी की राशि सूचीबद्ध होती है।
- **MGNREGA पोर्टल पर सत्यापन**: आधिकारिक MGNREGA वेबसाइट (https://nrega.nic.in) पर जाएँ और 'मस्टर रोल' अनुभाग में अपने गाँव का चयन करें। जॉब-कार्ड नंबर दर्ज करके भुगतान की गई मजदूरी की राशि और तिथि देखें।
- **मोबाइल ऐप का उपयोग**: MGNREGA मोबाइल ऐप डाउनलोड करें, जॉब-कार्ड नंबर दर्ज करें और भुगतान की स्थिति (पेमेंट स्टेटस) देखें।
- **बैंक विवरण की जाँच**: जॉब-कार्ड धारक के बैंक खाते में जमा हुई मजदूरी की राशि की तुलना मस्टर रोल में दर्ज राशि से करें।
- **सामाजिक अंकेक्षण (सोशल ऑडिट) में भागीदारी**: ग्राम सभा द्वारा आयोजित सामाजिक अंकेक्षण बैठकों में भाग लें, जहाँ मस्टर रोल और भुगतान रिकॉर्ड की सार्वजनिक रूप से समीक्षा की जाती है।
- **RTI आवेदन**: यदि जानकारी सार्वजनिक रूप से उपलब्ध नहीं है, तो ग्राम पंचायत या MGNREGA कार्यालय के जन सूचना अधिकारी (PIO) को सूचना का अधिकार (RTI) आवेदन भेजकर मस्टर रोल और भुगतान विवरण की प्रति प्राप्त करें।

question: What burden of proof applies when a seller claims their warranty is based on proper testing?
ground_truth: The burden of proof lies on the person raising the defence to demonstrate that the warranty or guarantee is based on adequate or proper testing.
triseva_answer: When a seller asserts that a warranty or guarantee is based on an adequate or proper test, the burden of proof for that defence lies on the seller (the person raising the defence). The seller must demonstrate that the warranty is indeed founded on proper testing. Source: Consumer Protection provisions (see clause on warranties not based on adequate or proper test).

ground_truth: Over time, a swollen joint can become severely damaged. Additionally, some kinds of arthritis can cause problems in organs such as the eyes or skin, indicating progressive complications.

- Some types of arthritis may also cause problems in other organs, such as the eyes or skin.
- Symptoms often worsen as a person ages, indicating progression of the disease.

arthritis is one type. Psoriatic arthritis affects people with psoriasis (itchy or sore scaly red and white skin patches). Gout is a painful type of arthritis that happens when too much uric acid builds up in your body. It often starts in the big toe. Other joints can also be affected. Ankylosing spondylitis is a type of arthritis of the spine that can cause stiffness and make it difficult to move and bend. What are the symptoms of arthritis? Pain, redness, warmth, and joint inflammation are common arthritis symptoms. You may not be able to move your joint as well as it should. Other symptoms could include fever , weight loss, breathing difficulties, or a rash. Symptoms often get worse as you age. Some symptoms of arthritis may be signs of other illnesses. Who is more likely to get arthritis? A few things that might increase your chance of getting arthritis include: Family history. You may be more likely to get certain types of arthritis if a member of your family has the disorder. Age. The risk of getting many types of arthritis increases with age. Sex. Certain types of arthritis are more common in women, while other types are more common in men. Other factors that might increase your risk of getting arthritis include having a previous joint injury, obesity , or lupus . How is arthritis diagnosed? To find out if you have arthritis, your health care provider may: Ask you about your medical history, including your symptoms.

Why is this medication prescribed? Secukinumab injection is used to treat the following: plaque psoriasis (a skin disease in which red, scaly patches form on some areas of the body) psoriatic arthritis (a condition that causes joint pain and swelling and scales on the skin) ankylosing spondylitis (a condition in which the body attacks the joints of the spine and other areas causing pain and joint damage) axial spondyloarthritis (a condition in which the body attacks the joints of the spine and other areas, causing pain and signs of swelling, but without changes seen on x-ray) enthesitis-related arthritis (a condition in which the body attacks its own joints, causing pain, swelling, and loss of function) hidradenitis suppurativa (a skin disease that causes small, painful lumps to form under the skin) Secukinumab injection is in a class of medications called interleukin-17A (IL-17A) receptor inhibitors. It works by blocking the activity of interleukin-17A, a substance in the body that causes inflammation. How should this medicine be used? Secukinumab injection comes as a solution (liquid) in single-dose, prefilled syringes and dosing pens to inject subcutaneously (under the skin). Do not inject more or less of it or inject it more often than prescribed by your doctor. question: How does the Soil Health Card Scheme empower farmers in decision-making?
ground_truth: By providing accurate soil nutrient data and expert guidance, the scheme empowers farmers to make informed decisions about crop selection, fertilizer application, and land management practices.
triseva_answer:
- The Soil Health Card (SHC) provides a detailed report on the nutrient status of a farmer’s soil, including pH, organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and micronutrients.
- Based on the SHC, farmers receive specific fertilizer and soil‑amendment recommendations, indicating the exact dosage of each nutrient needed.
- The card helps farmers decide which crops are suitable for their land and which ones to avoid, enabling better crop selection.
- Farmers get an updated soil health record every three years, ensuring they have current data to plan future cropping and land‑management practices.
- The scheme assigns the same soil‑analysis officer to a farmer over time, providing continuity and reliable guidance.
- By following the SHC advice, farmers can apply balanced fertilizers instead of relying solely on urea, improving yields and long‑term soil health.
- The government also organizes demonstrations, trainings, and farmer melas to educate farmers on the correct use of fertilizers and soil‑management practices.

question: What type of research or studies have been conducted on the Soil Health Card scheme's impact?
ground_truth: A study on the Impact of Soil Health Card Scheme has been conducted and documented, available through the PIB website, to assess the scheme's effectiveness.
triseva_answer:
The Soil Health Card (SHC) scheme has been evaluated through a specific research study conducted by the National Productivity Council (NPC). The study, titled “Soil Testing Infrastructure for Faster Delivery of Soil Health Card in India,” was carried out in February 2017 and covered:

- **Geographic scope:** 76 districts across 19 states.
- **Laboratory coverage:** 170 soil testing laboratories.
- **Farmer sample:** 1,700 farmers.

Key findings reported in the study include:
- Over 90 % of surveyed farmers had never had their soil tested before the SHC scheme.
- 92 % reported not using balanced fertilizers or micronutrients without soil‑test information.
- After applying fertilizer and micronutrient recommendations from SHCs, chemical fertilizer use decreased by 8‑10 %.
- Crop yields increased by approximately 5‑6 % due to the recommended nutrient applications.

These results constitute the primary research evidence on the scheme’s impact to date.

They are near the middle of your back, just below the rib cage. Inside each kidney there are about a million tiny structures called nephrons. They filter your blood. They remove wastes and extra water, which become urine. The urine flows through tubes called ureters. It goes to your bladder, which stores the urine until you go to the bathroom. Most kidney diseases attack the nephrons. This damage may leave kidneys unable to remove wastes. Causes can include genetic problems, injuries, or medicines. You have a higher risk of kidney disease if you have diabetes , high blood pressure , or a close family member with kidney disease. Chronic kidney disease damages the nephrons slowly over several years. Other kidney problems include: Cancer Cysts Stones Infections Your doctor can do blood and urine tests to check if you have kidney disease. If your kidneys fail , you will need dialysis or a kidney transplant . question: राष्ट्रीय आपदा के दौरान ग्राम पंचायत को प्रभावित आबादी को नौकरी के कार्ड फिर से जारी करने की आवश्यकता क्यों हो सकती है?
ground_truth: नौकरी कार्ड बाढ़ या भूकंप जैसी आपदाओं के दौरान खो या नष्ट हो सकते हैं, इसलिए प्रभावित श्रमिकों को रोजगार लाभ प्राप्त करने के लिए पुनः जारी करने के लिए आवेदन करने की आवश्यकता होती है।
triseva_answer:
राष्ट्रीय आपदा के दौरान, ग्राम पंचायत को निम्नलिखित कारणों से प्रभावित आबादी को रोजगार कार्ड (जॉब कार्ड) पुनः जारी करने की आवश्यकता हो सकती है:
- आपदा के कारण रोजगार कार्ड खो सकते हैं, नष्ट हो सकते हैं या अपठनीय हो सकते हैं, जिससे श्रमिकों के लिए रोजगार गारंटी योजना के तहत कार्य का दावा करना असंभव हो जाता है।
- ग्रामीण परिवारों का बड़े पैमाने पर विस्थापन हो सकता है; विस्थापित परिवार अस्थायी रूप से स्थानांतरित क्षेत्र में रह सकते हैं और उन्हें उस नए स्थान पर पंजीकरण करने तथा रोजगार कार्ड प्राप्त करने की आवश्यकता होती है ताकि वे कार्य के लिए आवेदन कर सकें और अपने 100-दिवसीय रोजगार के अधिकार को बनाए रख सकें।
- अधिनियम स्पष्ट रूप से ग्राम पंचायत (या कार्यक्रम अधिकारी) को प्रभावित परिवारों के वयस्क सदस्यों को पंजीकरण करने, रोजगार कार्ड जारी करने और किसी भी हानि या विनाश की स्थिति में पुनः पंजीकरण/पुनः जारी करने की अनुमति देने के लिए अधिकृत करता है।
- आपदा के बाद, अस्थायी रूप से जारी किए गए रोजगार कार्डों को मूल निवास स्थान पर पुनः पुष्ट (re-endorsed) किया जाना चाहिए और मूल कार्ड के साथ जोड़ा जाना चाहिए, जिसके लिए पुनः जारी करने और पुनः पुष्ट करने की प्रक्रिया की आवश्यकता होती है।

- आपदा के कारण मूल नौकरी के कार्ड खो सकते हैं, नष्ट हो सकते हैं या अपठनीय हो सकते हैं, जिससे पुन: जारी करना आवश्यक हो जाता है।

प्रदत्त संदर्भ में इस प्रश्न का उत्तर नहीं दिया गया है।

**सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर:**

राष्ट्रीय आपदा के दौरान, ग्राम पंचायत को प्रभावित आबादी को जॉब कार्ड (रोजगार कार्ड) पुन: जारी करने की आवश्यकता हो सकती है, जिसका मुख्य कारण महात्मा गांधी राष्ट्रीय ग्रामीण रोजगार गारंटी अधिनियम (MGNREGA) के तहत रोजगार के अवसरों तक उनकी पहुँच सुनिश्चित करना है।

इसके मुख्य कारण निम्नलिखित हैं:

1. **अभिलेखों की हानि:** बाढ़, भूकंप या आग जैसी आपदाएँ आधिकारिक अभिलेखों को नष्ट कर सकती हैं, जिसमें जॉब कार्ड की मूल प्रतियाँ भी शामिल हैं।
2. **विस्थापन:** प्रभावित परिवार अस्थायी राहत शिविरों में स्थानांतरित हो सकते हैं, जिससे उनके मूल जॉब कार्ड खो सकते हैं या उनके पास उनकी पहुँच नहीं रह सकती है।
3. **रोजगार की तत्काल आवश्यकता:** आपदाएँ अक्सर आजीविका को बाधित कर देती हैं। MGNREGA कानूनी रूप से प्रत्येक ग्रामीण परिवार को 100 दिनों के मजदूरी रोजगार की गारंटी देता है। जॉब कार्ड पुन: जारी करना यह सुनिश्चित करने का पहला कदम है कि विस्थापित और प्रभावित व्यक्ति इस महत्वपूर्ण आय सहायता तक पहुँच सकें और स्थानीय बुनियादी ढाँचे के पुनर्निर्माण के लिए सार्वजनिक कार्य परियोजनाओं में भाग ले सकें।

ग्राम पंचायत MGNREGA के तहत जॉब कार्ड जारी करने और उनके रखरखाव के लिए उत्तरदायी स्थानीय निकाय है। इसलिए, आपदा के बाद, यह सुनिश्चित करने के लिए कि सभी प्रभावित निवासियों को उनके रोजगार के अधिकार तक पहुँच प्राप्त हो, यह कार्डों के सत्यापन और पुन: जारी करने की प्रक्रिया शुरू करेगी।

Eligible families are based on SECC 2011 database. Documents required: Aadhaar card, ration card, income certificate. Over 1700 treatment packages covered. No premium to be paid by beneficiary.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) aims to provide affordable housing for all. Urban component provides interest subsidy on home loans. EWS category (income up to Rs 3 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. LIG category (income Rs 3-6 lakh): subsidy of 6.5% for loan up to Rs 6 lakh. MIG-I (income Rs 6-12 lakh): 4% subsidy. MIG-II (income Rs 12-18 lakh): 3% subsidy.

question: How would a farmer use Soil Health Card information to improve crop productivity?
ground_truth: A farmer can use the card to identify nutrient deficiencies in their soil and apply corrective measures, while adopting balanced and integrated nutrient management practices tailored to their cropping systems.
triseva_answer:
The Soil Health Card (SHC) provides a detailed report of the farm’s soil nutrient status and specific fertilizer recommendations. A farmer can use this information in the following ways:

- **Apply balanced fertilizers**: Follow the SHC’s dosage recommendations for nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulphur, zinc, iron, copper, manganese, boron, and other nutrients instead of using only urea.
- **Use recommended soil amendments**: Implement the suggested soil amendments (e.g., lime to adjust pH, organic matter) to correct deficiencies and improve soil health.
- **Select suitable crops**: Use the SHC data to decide which crops are best suited to the current soil conditions and avoid crops that may not thrive.
- **Plan nutrient management**: Follow the advisory on the quantities and types of fertilizers to apply for optimal nutrient use efficiency and higher yields.
- **Maintain records**: Keep the SHC report as a reference for future cropping cycles, updating it every three years as new cards are issued.

By adhering to the SHC’s recommendations, a farmer can correct nutrient imbalances, improve soil fertility, and enhance overall crop productivity.

The PM‑KISAN scheme uses the following land‑record sources to identify eligible beneficiaries:

- **State land‑revenue records** (land ownership and mutation records) maintained under the existing land‑revenue administrative regime. These records are used to verify ownership, assess cultivable land, and determine eligibility, especially for corrections arising from inheritance or transfer of land after 01.12.2018 or 01.02.2019. [Source 1, 2]
- **Certificates issued by village authorities** (e.g., Chairman/Chief, village council, or village chieftain) that authorize a tribal family to cultivate a piece of land. In Manipur and Nagaland, such certificates, authenticated by sub‑divisional officers and countersigned by the Deputy Commissioner, are accepted as proof of land holding. [Source 2, 3, 4]
- **Community‑owned land documentation** for North‑Eastern states where land rights are community‑based. In Nagaland, certificates from the village council/authority/village chieftain, verified by the administrative head of the circle/sub‑division and countersigned by the Deputy Commissioner, are used for both permanent cultivated land and Jhum land. [Source 4]
- **Lineage (Vanshavali) linked land records** submitted by farmers in Jharkhand to establish succession and ownership. [Source 5]
- **Supplementary databases** that may be cross‑referenced for farmer identification, including the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) database, Soil Health Card data, and the Socio‑Economic and Caste Census (SECC). [Source 5]

These records collectively form the basis for verifying that an applicant is a bona‑fide farmer with cultivable land and meets the scheme’s eligibility criteria. [Source 1‑5]

question: What unique approach does the government take in the Soil Health Card Scheme compared to other schemes?
ground_truth: The government ensures that the same person carries out soil analysis for a farmer across different assessments, rather than changing the person conducting the study as is common in other government schemes.
triseva_answer: The Soil Health Card Scheme uniquely ensures continuity of the soil‑testing personnel: the same analyst who conducts the soil analysis for a farmer is retained for that farmer’s subsequent tests, unlike many other government schemes where the responsible officer may change. This consistency is intended to improve the reliability and effectiveness of the soil health records and recommendations provided to farmers.

ground_truth: PM Modi ne 'Vande Mataram' ka zikr kiya yeh batane ke liye ki ek aisi zameen banana jo 'Sujalam, Suphalam' (fertile aur prosperous) ho, uske liye mitti ko palna zaroori hai, jo yeh scheme karne ka aim rakhti hai.
triseva_answer: Prime Minister Narendra Modi ne Soil Health Card scheme ke launch ke dauran 'Vande Mataram' gaane ka zikr kiya. Unhone kaha ki ek aisi zameen jo sach mein 'Sujalam, Suphalam' ho, use paane ke liye mitti ki dekhbhaal karna zaroori hai. Unhone Soil Health Card scheme ko iss sapne ko poora karne ki disha mein ek kadam bataya.

प्रधानमंत्री किसान सम्मान ननधध (PM-KISAN) उद्देश्य 1 देश भें छोटे औय सीभ ॊत किस नों िो प्रत्‍मऺत आम सॊफॊधी सह मत ददए ज ने िे प्रमोजन र्थ एि सुव्‍मवस्‍थर्त ि मथ व्‍मवस्‍र् ि मभ ियने िे लरए ब यत सयि य द्व य िेंद्र से शतप्रततशत सह मत िे स र् (ऩीएम -किसान ) न भ िी एि मोजन इसी ववत्तीम वषथ से आयॊब ियने ि तनर्थम लरम गम है। 2 मह मोजन छोटे औय सीभ ॊत किस नों िो उनिे तनवेश औय अन्म जरूयतों िे लरए एि सुतनश्चित आम सह मत सुतनश्चित ियते हुए ऩूयि आम प्रद न ियेग । श्जससे उनिी उबयती जरूयतों िो तर् ववशेष रूऩ से पसर िक्र िे ऩचि त सॊब ववत आम प्र प्त होने से ऩूवथ होने व रे सॊब ववत व्ममों िी ऩूततथ सुतनश्चित होगी। 3 मह मोजन उन्हें ऐसे खिों िो ऩूय ियते हुए उन्हें स हूि यों िे िॊगुर भें ऩड़ने से बी फि एगी औय खेती िे ि मथिर ऩों भें उनिी तनयॊतयत सुतनश्चित ियेगी। मह मोजन उन्हें अऩनी िृवष ऩद्धततमों िे आधुतनिीियर् िे लरए सऺभ फन एगी औय उनिे लरए सम्भ नजनि जीवनम ऩन ियने ि भ गथ प्रशस्त ियेगी। योजना िे ऱागू होने िी निधियााँ 4 मह मोजन 01.12.2018 से र गू िी ज एगी तर् ऩ त्र किस न ऩरयव यों िो मह र ब इसी ततथर् िे ऩचि त िी अवथध ि देम होग । 5 ऩ त्र किस न ऩरयव यों िी ऩहि न िे लरए िट आप डेट 01.02.2019 तनश्चित िी गई है।

question: Why is the 'Janata Information System' considered important for the Scheme's implementation?
ground_truth: The Janata Information System ensures transparency and accountability by mandatorily disclosing basic information to all common people and stakeholders, allowing them to verify the details of work, materials, labour days, and costs involved.
triseva_answer:
The Janata Information System is a mandatory proactive‑disclosure mechanism under the MGNREGA Act that underpins transparency and accountability in the scheme’s implementation. Its importance stems from the following statutory requirements:

- **Display at each worksite** – the ‘Janata’ estimate of the work, showing details, labour days, material quantities (in local terminology) and item‑wise costs must be posted on site. (Source 1)
- **Village‑level public boards** – job‑card lists, days of work provided, wages paid to each holder, and entitlements under the Act must be displayed prominently. (Source 1)
- **Gram Panchayat office boards** – a shelf of approved projects, year‑wise works taken up or completed, employment provided, funds received and expenditure, material lists with quantities, and procurement rates must be shown. (Source 1)
- **Website updates** – the Ministry of Rural Development and State Rural Development Departments must keep their websites fully compliant with Section 4(1)(b) of the Right to Information Act, making all scheme information publicly downloadable. (Source 1)
- **Facilitates social audit** – by providing free, timely access to work and financial details, the system enables concurrent social audits and public scrutiny, reducing corruption and ensuring that workers receive their entitled wages. (Source 1, Source 2)

Collectively, these provisions ensure that all stakeholders have real‑time, accurate information about scheme activities, thereby promoting transparency, accountability, and effective monitoring of implementation.

The Janata Information System is a mandatory proactive‑disclosure mechanism under the MGNREGA Act (Section 4(1)(b) of the Right to Information Act) that is essential for ensuring transparency and accountability in the scheme’s implementation. It requires that:

- At each worksite, the ‘Janata’ estimate of the work be displayed, showing details of the work, estimated labour days, quantities of materials (in local terminology) and item‑wise cost.
- On prominent village walls or public boards, the job‑card list, number of days of work provided, wages paid to each job‑card holder and other entitlements be displayed.
- At the Gram Panchayat office, a board must show the shelf of approved projects, year‑wise works taken up or completed, employment provided, funds received and expenditure, list of materials with quantities used and procurement rates.
- The Ministry of Rural Development and State Rural Development Departments must keep their websites updated to fully comply with the seventeen provisions of Section 4(1)(b) of the RTI Act, making all scheme information publicly available in downloadable electronic form.

These disclosures enable citizens, stakeholders and social‑audit bodies to monitor work progress, verify wage payments, track fund flows and material procurement, thereby reducing corruption and ensuring that the scheme is implemented as intended. राष्ट्रीय उत्पादकता परिषद (एन पी सी) द्वारा किए गए अध्ययन के अनुसार, मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड (सॉइल हेल्थ कार्ड) की सिफारिशों के अनुसार उर्वरकों और सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्वों के उपयोग के परिणामस्वरूप:

*   रासायनिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग में **8-10 प्रतिशत** की कमी आई।

आपके द्वारा वर्णित परिदृश्य, जिसमें रासायनिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग में 9 प्रतिशत की कमी और पैदावार में 5.5 प्रतिशत की वृद्धि हुई है, अध्ययन में बताए गए दायरे के भीतर ही आता है।

Study on Impact of Soil Health Card Scheme by National Productivity Council [21] National Productivity Council (NPC) [22] carried out a study on ‘Soil Testing Infrastructure for Faster Delivery of Soil Health Card in India’ and submitted its report in February 2017. The study was conducted in 76 districts in 19 States covering 170 soil testing labs and 1700 farmers. Some of the findings of the study are as follows: More than 90 per cent of farmers surveyed informed that they have not got their soil tested before the implementation of this scheme. 92 per cent farmers reported not having used balanced fertilizer and micro nutrients in absence of information related to availability of nutrients in their soil. As a result of application of fertilizer and micro-nutrients as per the recommendations on the Soil Health Cards, it was reported that there has been a decrease of use of chemical fertilizer application in the range of 8-10 per cent. A fever is a body temperature above 38°C (100.4°F). Common causes include viral infections, bacterial infections, and inflammation. The most common cause of anemia is not having enough iron . Your body needs iron to make hemoglobin. Hemoglobin is an iron-rich protein that gives the red color to blood. It carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body. Anemia has three main causes: blood loss, lack of red blood cell production, and high rates of red blood cell destruction. Conditions that may lead to anemia include: Heavy periods Pregnancy Ulcers Colon polyps or colon cancer Inherited disorders A diet that does not have enough iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 Blood disorders such as sickle cell anemia and thalassemia , or cancer Aplastic anemia , a condition that can be inherited or acquired G6PD deficiency , a metabolic disorder Anemia can make you feel tired, cold, dizzy, and irritable. You may be short of breath or have a headache. Your doctor will diagnose anemia with a physical exam and blood tests. Treatment depends on the kind of anemia you have. Why is this medication prescribed? Anti-thymocyte globulin is used to prevent or treat kidney transplant rejection (attack of the transplanted organ by the immune system of the person receiving the organ). Your health care provider or your local health department can test you to find out if you have TB germs in your body. They will give you either a TB skin or blood test . If your test shows that you have TB germs, you'll need to have other tests to see if the germs are actively growing: Tests for TB disease in the lungs usually include testing samples of your sputum and having chest x-rays . Tests for TB disease in other parts of your body may include tests of urine and tissue samples . You may need a TB test if you have symptoms of TB disease or if you are at high risk because you are more likely to be near someone with TB disease. People who have HIV also need to get tested for TB. HIV weakens your immune system. So if you have both HIV and inactive TB, the TB can quickly become active TB disease. You will need treatment for the inactive TB as soon as possible to prevent active TB disease. What is the treatment for tuberculosis (TB)? The treatment for both inactive TB infection and TB disease is antibiotics. To make sure you get rid of all the TB germs in your body, it's very important to follow the directions for taking your medicine. question: Why would the District Programme Coordinator need to be informed about job cards issued during a national calamity?
ground_truth: The District Programme Coordinator needs to be informed to maintain centralized records and coordination of job cards issued in affected areas during the calamity.
triseva_answer:
The scheme explicitly requires that the details of job cards issued during a national calamity be intimated to the District Programme Coordinator (Section 34.2). This intimation enables the Coordinator, whose statutory functions include implementation, coordination, monitoring and supervision of the scheme, to oversee the subsequent re‑endorsement of those job cards at the original place of habitation and their clubbing with the original job card when normalcy is restored (Section 34.3). The Coordinator’s role in ensuring that the re‑endorsed cards are properly integrated and that employment entitlements are correctly accounted for is therefore directly tied to the mandatory reporting of the job‑card details.

Source: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2014/5/a2005-42.pdf

b2_answer:
Under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), when a national calamity (e.g., flood, cyclone, tsunami, earthquake) causes mass displacement of rural households, the Act permits the issuance of job cards by the Gram Panchayat or Programme Officer in the area of temporary relocation. **Section 34(2) of the MGNREGA Act expressly requires that the details of such job cards be intimated to the District Programme Coordinator.** The purpose of this requirement is to:

- Ensure the District Programme Coordinator is aware of all newly issued job cards so that district‑level monitoring and coordination can be carried out effectively.
- Allow the Coordinator to verify that the employment days provided under these emergency job cards are counted toward the household’s 100‑day guaranteed employment entitlement.
- Facilitate the later re‑endorsement and merging of the emergency job card with the original job card once normalcy is restored, maintaining accurate records.
- Support the preparation of the district labour budget and overall planning for employment provision in the district.

Source: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, Section 34(2).

What are reasonable means or what is a reasonable time in such a case, is a question of fact. It is not necessary that the finder should know who is the owner of the property, or that any particular person is the owner of it; it is sufficient if, at the time of appropriating it, he does not believe it to be his own property, or in good faith believe that the real owner cannot be found. Illustrations. (a) A finds a rupee on the high road, not knowing to whom the rupee belongs, A picks up the rupee. Here A has not committed the offence defined in this section. (b) A finds a letter on the road, containing a bank note. From the direction and contents of the letter he learns to whom the note belongs. He appropriates the note. He is guilty of an offence under this section. (c) A finds a cheque payable to bearer. He can form no conjecture as to the person who has lost the cheque. question: What is the difference between macro-nutrients and micro-nutrients listed in the Soil Health Card?
ground_truth: Macro-nutrients (N, P, K) are required in larger quantities, while micro-nutrients (Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, Bo) are required in smaller quantities for plant growth.
triseva_answer:
The Soil Health Card reports 12 nutrient parameters, grouped as follows:
- **Macro‑nutrients (primary nutrients)**: Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K). These are required by plants in relatively large amounts.
- **Secondary nutrient**: Sulphur (S), listed separately from macro‑nutrients.
- **Micro‑nutrients (trace nutrients)**: Zinc (Zn), Iron (Fe), Copper (Cu), Manganese (Mn), Boron (B). These are needed only in small quantities.

Thus, macro‑nutrients are the three primary nutrients (N‑P‑K), while micro‑nutrients are the five trace elements listed above.

दस्तावेजों में उल्लेख किया गया है कि मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड (सॉइल हेल्थ कार्ड) योजना के अंतर्गत, किसान कार्ड पर दी गई सिफारिशों के आधार पर "संतुलित उर्वरक और सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्वों" का उपयोग करते हैं। इसमें यह भी उल्लेख किया गया है कि इसके परिणामस्वरूप रासायनिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग में कमी आई है और फसल की पैदावार में वृद्धि हुई है। हालाँकि, ये दस्तावेज यह परिभाषित नहीं करते हैं कि स्थूल पोषक तत्व (मैक्रो-न्यूट्रिएंट्स) और सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्व (माइक्रो-न्यूट्रिएंट्स) क्या हैं, और न ही उनके बीच के अंतर की व्याख्या करते हैं।

However, based on general knowledge about soil analysis programs like the Soil Health Card scheme, maintaining consistency in soil analysis personnel is important for the following reasons:

*   **Standardization and Accuracy:** Consistent personnel ensure that soil testing methods, protocols, and equipment calibration are applied uniformly. This reduces variability and ensures that the results are accurate, reliable, and comparable over time and across different locations.
*   **Data Integrity and Trend Analysis:** A stable team develops a deep understanding of the local soil conditions. This historical knowledge is crucial for interpreting data trends, identifying long-term changes in soil health (like degradation or improvement), and providing meaningful, context-specific recommendations to farmers.
*   **Trust and Credibility:** Farmers are more likely to trust and act upon recommendations if they come from a familiar and consistent source. This builds a relationship and confidence in the program and its advice.
*   **Efficiency:** A stable team is more efficient as they don't need to be constantly retrained on procedures and can focus on the core task of analysis, leading to faster and more consistent service delivery.

question: How would a farmer use the soil health card to decide which crops to cultivate?
ground_truth: A farmer would identify the nutrients lacking in their soil from the card, then select crops that either require less of those nutrients or plan to add the necessary fertilizers before planting those crops.
triseva_answer:
The farmer should:
- Examine the 12 soil parameters listed on the Soil Health Card (N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC, OC).
- Identify which nutrients are deficient or excessive according to the card.
- Use the advisory section on the card that provides fertilizer recommendations and required soil amendments.
- Match the soil’s nutrient status and pH with crops that are suited to those conditions, selecting crops that can thrive with the existing fertility.
- Avoid crops that require nutrients that are severely lacking unless the recommended corrective measures are applied.
- Follow the recommended fertilizer and amendment schedule before sowing the chosen crops.

The Soil Health Card (SHC) provides a detailed report of the farm’s soil nutrient status and physical parameters. A farmer can use this information to select suitable crops as follows:

- **Review nutrient levels**: Examine the macro‑nutrients (N, P, K), secondary nutrients (S), micro‑nutrients (Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B) and physical parameters (pH, EC, organic carbon) listed on the SHC.
- **Match crop requirements**: Compare the soil’s nutrient profile with the nutrient needs of potential crops. Choose crops that thrive in the existing nutrient balance and avoid those that require nutrients the soil lacks.
- **Follow advisory recommendations**: The SHC includes an advisory that suggests specific fertilizer dosages and soil amendments needed to correct deficiencies. Apply these recommendations to bring the soil to a condition suitable for the chosen crop.
- **Decide on crop inclusion/exclusion**: Based on the nutrient status and the advisory, the farmer can decide which crops to cultivate and which to skip, ensuring optimal yield and soil health.

By aligning crop selection with the SHC’s nutrient and amendment guidance, the farmer maximizes productivity while maintaining soil fertility.

question: What are three general symptoms of TB disease?
ground_truth: Three general symptoms include chills and fever, night sweats (heavy sweating during sleep), and losing weight without trying.
triseva_answer:
- Fever (chills and fever)
- Night sweats (heavy sweating during sleep)
- Unexplained weight loss
triseva_contexts: transplant , steroids , and specialized treatments for certain autoimmune diseases What are the symptoms of tuberculosis (TB)? Most people who have TB germs in their bodies don't get sick with TB disease. Instead, they have inactive TB infection. With an inactive TB infection, you: Don't have symptoms Can't spread TB to others Could get sick with active TB disease in the future if your immune system becomes weak for another reason Need to take medicine to prevent getting sick with active TB disease in the future If you have TB disease , the TB germs are active, meaning that they are growing (multiplying) inside your body and making you sick. If the TB is growing in your lungs or throat, you can spread the TB germs to other people. You can get sick with TB disease weeks to years after you're infected with TB germs. With TB disease, your symptoms will depend on where the TB is growing in your body: General symptoms may include: Chills and fever Night sweats (heavy sweating during sleep) Losing weight without trying Loss of appetite Weakness or fatigue Symptoms from TB disease in your lungs may include: A cough that lasts longer than 3 weeks Coughing up blood or sputum (a thick mucus from the lungs) Chest pain How is tuberculosis (TB) diagnosed? question: Why might a person with Type 1 diabetes require more than just insulin injections for treatment?
ground_truth: Some people with Type 1 diabetes also need to take another type of diabetes medicine that works with insulin to help manage their blood glucose levels effectively.
triseva_answer:
People with Type 1 diabetes often need more than insulin injections to manage their condition effectively. According to the medical information, comprehensive care includes:

- **Lifestyle modifications** such as adopting a balanced diet, engaging in regular physical activity, and quitting smoking.
- **Regular blood‑glucose monitoring** to keep track of sugar levels and adjust treatment as needed.
- **Additional medications** when necessary to address related health issues or to help control blood sugar.
- **Preventive measures** aimed at reducing the risk of serious complications like heart disease, stroke, kidney problems, nerve damage, and eye problems.

These elements work together with insulin therapy to improve overall health and lower the chances of diabetes‑related complications.

question: What is the difference between autoimmune arthritis and infectious arthritis?
ground_truth: Autoimmune arthritis occurs when the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy cells, with rheumatoid arthritis being the most common form. Infectious arthritis is an infection that spreads from another body part to the joint.
triseva_answer:
• **Autoimmune arthritis** – Occurs when the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy cells, leading to joint inflammation. Rheumatoid arthritis is the most common form of this type.
• **Infectious arthritis** – Results from an infection that spreads from another part of the body to the joint, causing joint inflammation.
• Both types can produce joint pain, redness, warmth, and swelling, but the underlying cause differs: an immune‑system error versus an external infection.

question: What role do State Governments play in the Soil Health Card Scheme?
ground_truth: State Governments are responsible for issuing soil health cards to all farmers in their respective states as part of the scheme's implementation.
triseva_answer:
State Governments support the Soil Health Card Scheme by:
- Setting up and strengthening soil testing laboratories (static, mobile, mini‑labs, and village‑level labs) and sanctioning these facilities to the states.
- Identifying villages for implementation, collecting soil samples, analysing them, and distributing the Soil Health Cards to farmers.
- Organizing demonstrations, farmer trainings, and farmer melas to promote the scheme.
- Working with state and district agriculture machinery, panchayats, and village‑level workers such as Krishi Sakhis and Pasu Sakhis to educate farmers on the correct use of fertilizers.
- Coordinating the overall implementation of the scheme at the state level, including monitoring sample collection, analysis, and card distribution.

question: How does the Soil Health Card scheme help farmers avoid crop failures?
ground_truth: By providing detailed soil information and recommendations on suitable crops based on soil nutrient status, farmers can skip unsuitable crops and select those that will thrive in their soil conditions.
triseva_answer:
The Soil Health Card (SHC) scheme helps farmers avoid crop failures by providing a detailed, farm‑specific soil report that includes:

- **Nutrient status** – pH, organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and micronutrient levels.
- **Crop suitability guidance** – recommendations on which crops to cultivate and which to avoid based on the soil’s nutrient profile.
- **Balanced fertilizer advice** – precise dosage and type of fertilizers and soil amendments needed, reducing reliance on excess urea or single‑nutrient applications.
- **Regular updates** – a new SHC is issued every three years, ensuring farmers have current data on any changes in soil health.

By applying the SHC’s fertilizer and amendment recommendations, farmers can maintain optimal soil fertility, improve yields (studies show a 5‑6 % increase), and lower the risk of nutrient‑deficiency‑related crop failures.

**सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर:**

"अस्थमा कार्य योजना" (asthma work plan) एक व्यक्तिगत कार्य योजना है जिसे किसी कर्मचारी को कार्यस्थल पर अपनी अस्थमा की स्थिति को प्रबंधित करने में सहायता करने के लिए तैयार किया जाता है। यह कई कारणों से महत्वपूर्ण है:

*   **सुरक्षा:** यह उन संभावित कार्यस्थल कारकों (जैसे धूल, रसायन या धुआं) की पहचान करने में मदद करती है जो अस्थमा के दौरे को सक्रिय कर सकते हैं और उनसे बचने या उन्हें कम करने के उपाय प्रदान करती है।
*   **स्वास्थ्य प्रबंधन:** यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि कर्मचारी और उनके सहकर्मी जानते हों कि अस्थमा के लक्षणों को कैसे पहचानना है, आपात स्थिति में क्या करना है और दवा का सही उपयोग कैसे करना है।
*   **कानूनी अनुपालन:** कई स्थानों पर, नियोक्ताओं के लिए यह कानूनी रूप से आवश्यक है कि वे अस्थमा जैसी ज्ञात चिकित्सा स्थितियों वाले कर्मचारियों के लिए उचित सुविधाएँ प्रदान करें ताकि एक सुरक्षित कार्य वातावरण सुनिश्चित किया जा सके।
*   **उत्पादकता:** अस्थमा को प्रभावी ढंग से प्रबंधित करके, यह योजना कर्मचारियों को स्वस्थ रहने, बीमारी की छुट्टी कम करने और अधिक निरंतरता के साथ कार्य करने में मदद करती है।
*   **आपातकालीन तैयारी:** यह एक स्पष्ट और त्वरित प्रतिक्रिया योजना प्रदान करती है ताकि यदि किसी कर्मचारी को कार्यस्थल पर अस्थमा का दौरा पड़ता है, तो सहकर्मी और पर्यवेक्षक उचित सहायता प्रदान कर सकें।

हालाँकि, सामान्य चिकित्सा ज्ञान के आधार पर, अस्थमा कार्य योजना (अस्थमा एक्शन प्लान) का होना महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह:

*   दैनिक अस्थमा के प्रबंधन के लिए स्पष्ट निर्देश प्रदान करती है, जिसमें यह भी शामिल है कि किन दवाओं का उपयोग करना है और उन्हें कब लेना है।
*   यह बताती है कि अस्थमा के लक्षणों के बिगड़ने पर क्या करना है, जिससे व्यक्ति को अस्थमा के गंभीर दौरे को रोकने के लिए शीघ्रता से उपचार करने में सहायता मिलती है।
*   यह अस्थमा के शुरुआती लक्षणों को पहचानने में मदद करती है, जिससे समय पर हस्तक्षेप संभव हो पाता है।
*   यह आपातकालीन कक्ष (इमरजेंसी रूम) जाने या अस्पताल में भर्ती होने की आवश्यकता को कम करती है।
*   यह रोगी और उनके देखभाल करने वालों को अपनी स्थिति पर नियंत्रण रखने के लिए सशक्त बनाती है।

A fever is a body temperature above 38°C (100.4°F). Common causes include viral infections, bacterial infections, and inflammation. Treatment includes rest, hydration, and paracetamol or ibuprofen for fever above 38.5°C. Seek immediate medical care if fever exceeds 40°C, or is accompanied by severe headache, stiff neck, or difficulty breathing.

question: Is malaria still a problem in the United States?
ground_truth: No, malaria is almost wiped out in the United States, though it remains a major cause of death worldwide.
triseva_answer: Malaria is almost wiped out in the United States; it is not a major public health problem domestically. Cases that occur are typically imported by travelers returning from regions where malaria is endemic.

The disease is mostly a problem in developing countries with warm climates. If you travel to these countries, you are at risk. There are four different types of malaria caused by four related parasites. The most deadly type occurs in Africa south of the Sahara Desert. Malaria symptoms include chills, flu-like symptoms, fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and jaundice. A blood test can diagnose it. It can be life-threatening. However, you can treat malaria with drugs. The type of drug depends on which kind of malaria you have and where you were infected. Malaria can be prevented. question: How does the parliamentary oversight mechanism work for the Authority's audit reports?
ground_truth: The Comptroller and Auditor-General certifies the accounts and audit report, which the Authority forwards to the Central Government, and the Central Government must lay the audit report before each House of Parliament as soon as possible.
triseva_answer:
The parliamentary oversight of the Authority’s audit reports operates as follows:

- **Annual Report Preparation** – The Authority must prepare an annual report each year, containing a description of its activities, the audited accounts for the previous year, and the work programme for the coming year. (Source: Source 1, Source 2)
- **Audit by the Comptroller and Auditor‑General (CAG)** – The Authority’s accounts are audited annually by the CAG (or a person appointed by the CAG). The CAG has the same rights and privileges as in the audit of government accounts, including the right to demand production of books, accounts, vouchers and other documents and to inspect any office of the Authority. (Source: Source 2, Source 4)
- **Forwarding to the Central Government** – After certification, the audited accounts together with the audit report are forwarded by the Authority to the Central Government. (Source: Source 2, Source 4)
- **Laying Before Parliament** – The Central Government, as soon as practicable after receipt, causes the audit report (along with the certified accounts) to be laid before each House of Parliament. (Source: Source 1, Source 2, Source 4)
- **Annual Report Laying** – A copy of the Authority’s annual report (including the audited accounts) is also laid before each House of Parliament by the Central Government. (Source: Source 1, Source 3)

Thus, the audit reports are subject to parliamentary scrutiny through the mandatory laying of both the audit report and the annual report before the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha each year.

*   **Doc 1** describes the myScheme platform for government schemes.
*   **Doc 2** details the oversight mechanisms (like social audits) for the MGNREGA Act.
*   **Doc 3** discusses the internal structure and functions of the "Authority," including that the chief executive officer submits reports and accounts to the Authority itself, but it does not mention any external or parliamentary oversight.

However, based on general knowledge of how parliamentary oversight typically works in systems like India's:

In a parliamentary democracy, the audit reports of government bodies and authorities are usually overseen by the Parliament. The process generally involves the following steps:

1.  **Submission to Parliament:** The audit report, often prepared by an independent body like the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), is submitted to the Parliament.
2.  **Laying on the Table:** The report is formally "laid on the table" of both houses of Parliament (e.g., the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), making it a public document.
3.  **Examination by a Committee:** The report is then referred to a specific parliamentary committee, most commonly the **Public Accounts Committee (PAC)**.
4.  **Committee Review:** The PAC, which consists of members of Parliament from various parties, examines the audit findings. They can summon officials from the Authority and the government to question them about the audit observations, financial irregularities, or performance issues.
5.  **Reporting to Parliament:** After its review, the PAC prepares its own report, which includes its findings and recommendations. This report is then presented to the Parliament.
6.  **Parliamentary Action:** The Parliament then debates the PAC's report and can take action, such as demanding explanations from the government, approving corrective measures, or initiating further proceedings.

This mechanism ensures that the executive branch (the Authority and the government) is accountable to the legislature (Parliament) for its use of public funds and adherence to laws.

question: Agar ek Gram Panchayat ₹100,000 ka construction project plan karta hai, toh maximum amount jo materials aur skilled worker wages par kharch kiya ja sakta hai, wo kya hai?
ground_truth: Maximum amount jo materials aur skilled worker wages par kharch kiya ja sakta hai, wo ₹40,000 hai (forty per cent of the total cost).
triseva_answer:
For works undertaken by a Gram Panchayat, the material component—including wages for skilled and semi‑skilled workers—must not exceed 40 % of the total project cost. Therefore, on a ₹100,000 construction project, the maximum amount that can be allocated to materials and skilled worker wages is:

- 40 % of ₹100,000 = **₹40,000**

Source: MGNREGA Act, Section 20 (material component limit for Gram Panchayat works).

- Weight gain
- Constipation
- Hair loss
- Dry skin
- Muscle cramps
- Decreased concentration
- Aches and pains
- Swelling of the legs
- Increased sensitivity to cold

These symptoms match the patient’s presentation of sudden weight gain, fatigue, and mood changes.

question: Why should aspirin and ibuprofen be avoided when treating dengue?

triseva_answer:

• **Ibuprofen** – Also generally avoided because, as a non‑steroidal anti‑inflammatory drug (NSAID), it can increase the likelihood of bleeding. Recent evidence indicates that at standard over‑the‑counter doses ibuprofen may not significantly raise bleeding risk, but it is still recommended to avoid it in dengue patients.
• The primary concern with both drugs is the potential to exacerbate dengue‑related bleeding tendencies, so safer alternatives (e.g., paracetamol) are preferred for fever and pain relief.

ground_truth: Prediabetes means blood glucose is higher than normal but not high enough to be called diabetes, indicating the body's glucose regulation is already compromised and may progress to Type 2 diabetes if lifestyle changes are not made.
triseva_answer: Prediabetes means your blood glucose is higher than normal but not yet high enough to be called diabetes. In people with prediabetes, the body shows insulin resistance and reduced beta‑cell function, which together cause persistent hyperglycemia. These same abnormalities—insulin resistance and impaired insulin secretion—are the mechanisms that lead to type 2 diabetes, so their presence in prediabetes indicates that the disease process has already begun, increasing the chance of progressing to diabetes.

Having a parent or sibling with type 1 diabetes may increase your chance of developing it. You are at higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes if you: Are overweight or have obesity. Are over age 35. Children, teenagers, and younger adults can get diabetes, but

If you have gestational diabetes, you may be able to lower your glucose levels by eating a healthy diet and getting regular exercise. But be sure to talk to your provider about your treatment options. Gestational diabetes usually goes away after you give birth. But you will have a higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes later. Checking your blood glucose levels is also an important part of managing your diabetes. Ask your provider about the best way to check your blood glucose level and how often you should check it. Can diabetes be prevented? Type 1 diabetes can't be prevented. You may be able to delay or prevent type 2 diabetes through the same lifestyle changes that are used to manage diabetes (eating a healthy diet, staying at a healthy weight, and getting regular physical activity). These lifestyle changes may also help prevent gestational diabetes . दस्तावेजों में "मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड" (Soil Health Card) और "17 जनवरी" की तिथि का उल्लेख है, परंतु इसमें वर्ष निर्दिष्ट नहीं है और न ही यह पुष्टि की गई है कि यही इस योजना के शुभारंभ की तिथि थी।

सामान्य ज्ञान के आधार पर, भारत सरकार द्वारा मृदा स्वास्थ्य कार्ड योजना का शुभारंभ फरवरी 2015 में किया गया था।
